winnow-1.0.2/src/error.rs\n23\t```\n24\t\n25\t`cargo build --release` and `cargo test --release` both passed\n26\ton the same tree.\n27\t\n28\t## Root cause\n29\t\n30\t`cargo install` ignores `Cargo.lock` by default and re-resolves\n31\tfrom scratch, picking the newest semver-compatible version of\n32\tevery dep independently.\n33\t\n34\t- The lockfile happens to pin one `winnow` that satisfies all\n35\t  the gix-* crates simultaneously.\n36\t- A fresh resolve picks two: `0.7.x` for one part of the gix\n37\t  graph, `1.0.x` for another. `gix-object` and `gix-actor` get\n38\t  compiled against different `winnow`s, so their `ErrMode<E>`\n39\t  types don't match even though they look identical.\n40\t\n41\tThe smoking gun in `cargo install` output is the\n42\t`Locking N packages to latest …` line — that's cargo\n43\tannouncing it just did a fresh resolve.\n44\t\n45\t## The asymmetry\n46\t\n47\t| command | reads `Cargo.lock`? | re-resolves? |\n48\t| --- | --- | --- |\n49\t| `cargo build` / `cargo test` / `cargo run` | yes | only if `Cargo.toml` changed |\n50\t| `cargo build --locked` (etc.) | yes | never; errors if it would need to |\n51\t| `cargo install` (default) | **no** | always, from scratch |\n52\t| `cargo install --locked` | yes | never; errors if it would need to |\n53\t\n54\tSo build/test pass against the lockfile's dep graph, then\n55\t`cargo install` silently produces a binary built from a\n56\tdifferent (and possibly broken) graph.\n57\t\n58\t## Workaround\n59\t\n60\t`cargo install --path . --locked`. Cargo has **no stable config\n61\tkey or env var** to make `--locked` the default for\n62\t`cargo install`. Verified against the [cargo config\n63\treference](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html):\n64\t`[install]` only controls the install root directory; nothing\n65\ttoggles lockfile behavior.\n66\t\n67\tThe discipline therefore lives in the project's pre-commit\n68\tchecklist (CLAUDE.md step 4) and in shell aliases\n69\t(e.g. `alias ci='cargo install --locked'`).\n70\t\n71\t## Upstream tracking — cargo issues\n72\t\n73\tCanonical:\n74\t\n75\t- [#7169 — \"`cargo install` apparently ignores `Cargo.lock` as opposed to `cargo build`\"](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/7169) —\n76\t  the original report (2019). Exact phrasing of the surprise.\n77\t- [#9436 — \"`cargo install` on local repo ignores `Cargo.lock`\"](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/9436) —\n78\t  narrower variant for the `--path .` case.\n79\t\n80\tAdjacent edges:\n81\t\n82\t- [#14308 — \"`cargo install --locked --path .` isn't locking unlike `cargo build --locked`\"](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/14308) —\n83\t  recent; even with `--locked` there are edge cases.\n84\t- [#9289 — \"`cargo install --locked` is not really locked\"](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/9289) —\n85\t  staleness gotcha; `--locked` doesn't enforce that the lockfile\n86\t  is up-to-date with `Cargo.toml` for install.\n87\t- [#16649 — contradictory documentation for `cargo install --locked`](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/16649) —\n88\t  the docs themselves disagree on the behavior.\n89\t- [#9106 — warn when `--locked` is used but no `Cargo.lock` exists](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/9106).\n90\t- [PR #14556 — \"lockfile path implies `--locked` on cargo install\"](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/pull/14556) —\n91\t  incremental fix in this area.\n92\t\n93\t## Community discussion\n94\t\n95\t- [internals.rust-lang.org — \"`cargo install --locked` or not locked middle ground?\"](https://internals.rust-lang.org/t/cargo-install-locked-or-not-locked-middle-ground/23893)\n96\t  (Jan 2026). The active design debate. `cargo install` and `Cargo.lock` — the `--locked` gotcha\n\nBackground reference for the rule in `CLAUDE.md` pre-commit\nchecklist step 4: `cargo install --path . --locked` is required;\nplain `cargo install --path .` is unsafe.\n\n## What we hit\n\nOn a clean worktree (after `rustup update` + `cargo clean`),\n`cargo install --path .` failed inside `gix-object 0.58.0`:\n\n```\nerror[E0308]: mismatched types\n  --> gix-object-0.58.0/src/parse.rs:72:5\n   |\n71 | ) -> ModalResult<gix_actor::SignatureRef<'a>, E> {\n72 |     gix_actor::signature::decode(i)\n   |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ expected `Result<…, ErrMode<E>>`,\n   |                                       found    `Result<…, ErrMode<_>>`\nnote: there are multiple different versions of crate `winnow` in the dependency graph\n   --> winnow-0.7.15/src/error.rs\n   --> winnow-1.0.2/src/error.rs\n```\n\n`cargo build --release` and `cargo test --release` both passed\non the same tree.\n\n## Root cause\n\n`cargo install` ignores `Cargo.lock` by default and re-resolves\nfrom scratch, picking the newest semver-compatible version of\nevery dep independently.\n\n- The lockfile happens to pin one `winnow` that satisfies all\n  the gix-* crates simultaneously.\n- A fresh resolve picks two: `0.7.x` for one part of the gix\n  graph, `1.0.x` for another. `gix-object` and `gix-actor` get\n  compiled against different `winnow`s, so their `ErrMode<E>`\n  types don't match even though they look identical.\n\nThe smoking gun in `cargo install` output is the\n`Locking N packages to latest …` line — that's cargo\nannouncing it just did a fresh resolve.\n\n## The asymmetry\n\n| command | reads `Cargo.lock`? | re-resolves? |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `cargo build` / `cargo test` / `cargo run` | yes | only if `Cargo.toml` changed |\n| `cargo build --locked` (etc.) | yes | never; errors if it would need to |\n| `cargo install` (default) | **no** | always, from scratch |\n| `cargo install --locked` | yes | never; errors if it would need to |\n\nSo build/test pass against the lockfile's dep graph, then\n`cargo install` silently produces a binary built from a\ndifferent (and possibly broken) graph.\n\n## Workaround\n\n`cargo install --path . --locked`. Cargo has **no stable config\nkey or env var** to make `--locked` the default for\n`cargo install`. Verified against the [cargo config\nreference](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html):\n`[install]` only controls the install root directory; nothing\ntoggles lockfile behavior.\n\nThe discipline therefore lives in the project's pre-commit\nchecklist (CLAUDE.md step 4) and in shell aliases\n(e.g. `alias ci='cargo install --locked'`).\n\n## Upstream tracking — cargo issues\n\nCanonical:\n\n- [#7169 — \"`cargo install` apparently ignores `Cargo.lock` as opposed to `cargo build`\"](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/7169) —\n  the original report (2019). Exact phrasing of the surprise.\n- [#9436 — \"`cargo install` on local repo ignores `Cargo.lock`\"](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/9436) —\n  narrower variant for the `--path .` case.\n\nAdjacent edges:\n\n- [#14308 — \"`cargo install --locked --path .` isn't locking unlike `cargo build --locked`\"](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/14308) —\n  recent; even with `--locked` there are edge cases.\n- [#9289 — \"`cargo install --locked` is not really locked\"](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/9289) —\n  staleness gotcha; `--locked` doesn't enforce that the lockfile\n  is up-to-date with `Cargo.toml` for install.\n- [#16649 — contradictory documentation for `cargo install --locked`](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/16649) —\n  the docs themselves disagree on the behavior.\n- [#9106 — warn when `--locked` is used but no `Cargo.lock` exists](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/9106).\n- [PR #14556 — \"lockfile path implies `--locked` on cargo install\"](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/pull/14556) —\n  incremental fix in this area.\n\n## Community discussion\n\n- [internals.rust-lang.org — \"`cargo install --locked` or not locked middle ground?\"](https://internals.rust-lang.org/t/cargo-install-locked-or-not-locked-middle-ground/23893)\n  (Jan 2026). The active design debate. Two camps:\n  predictable-as-tested vs. up-to-date-with-security-fixes.\n- [users.rust-lang.org — \"Cargo install and lock file\"](https://users.rust-lang.org/t/cargo-install-and-lock-file/4203) —\n  older but the long-running version of the same complaint.\n- [users.rust-lang.org — \"`Cargo.{toml,lock}` equivalent for cargo install\"](https://users.rust-lang.org/t/cargo-toml-lock-equivalent-for-cargo-install/108703) —\n  others asking for exactly the config knob we wanted.\n\nThe bot thinks the cargo team is aware and conflicted (not\nunaware), based on the internals thread being open and active\nin 2026 while #7169 has been open since 2019 — flipping the\ndefault has been weighed and rejected (or at least deferred)\nmultiple times.\n","numLines":108,"startLine":1,"totalLines":108}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"48cfaf33-1f19-4f6c-91d7-aac28afb7885","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/vc-template-x1","sessionId":"e5ec0e9d-b1c8-4143-a844-c6e520a1770b","version":"2.1.159","gitBranch":"HEAD"}

`gitk --all` sees all of these obsolete commits; `jj log` only\n166\tshows the current version of each change.\n167\t\n168\t## Useful commands\n169\t\n170\t| Command | Description |\n171\t|---------|-------------|\n172\t| `jj log` | Show recent visible commits (default revset) |\n173\t| `jj log -r ::@` | Show **all** ancestors of the working copy |\n174\t| `jj log -r 'all()'` | Show all non-hidden commits (needed if you have multiple heads/branches) |\n175\t| `jj st | Show the status of the Working and Parent commits |\n176\t| `jj st -r <chid> | Status of the commit, <chid> such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n177\t| `jj show | Show the Working commit, -r @ |\n178\t| `jj show -r <chid> | Show the commit, <chid> such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n179\t| `jj evolog -r <chid>` | Show the evolution history of a single change |\n180\t| `jj op log` | Show operation history (each rewrite operation) |\n181\t\n182\t\n183\tIn a single-branch workflow, `jj log -r ::@` and `jj log -r 'all()'` give\n184\tthe same result. ((main))\n$\n```\n\n## Why `jj log` shows fewer commits than `gitk`\n\nIf you're coming from git, jj's log output can be surprising compared to\ntools like `gitk --all`.\n\njj tracks *changes* (identified by change IDs), not individual git commits.\nWhen you rewrite a change (`jj describe`, `jj rebase`, `jj squash`, etc.),\njj creates a new git commit and keeps the old one under `refs/jj/keep/*` as\nundo history. `gitk --all` sees all of these obsolete commits; `jj log` only\nshows the current version of each change.\n\n## Useful commands\n\n| Command | Description |\n|---------|-------------|\n| `jj log` | Show recent visible commits (default revset) |\n| `jj log -r ::@` | Show **all** ancestors of the working copy |\n| `jj log -r 'all()'` | Show all non-hidden commits (needed if you have multiple heads/branches) |\n| `jj st | Show the status of the Working and Parent commits |\n| `jj st -r <chid> | Status of the commit, <chid> such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n| `jj show | Show the Working commit, -r @ |\n| `jj show -r <chid> | Show the commit, <chid> such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n| `jj evolog -r <chid>` | Show the evolution history of a single change |\n| `jj op log` | Show operation history (each rewrite operation) |\n\n\nIn a single-branch workflow, `jj log -r ::@` and `jj log -r 'all()'` give\nthe same result. --all`.\n228\t\n229\tjj tracks *changes* (identified by change IDs), not individual git commits.\n230\tWhen you rewrite a change (`jj describe`, `jj rebase`, `jj squash`, etc.),\n231\tjj creates a new git commit and keeps the old one under `refs/jj/keep/*` as\n232\tundo history. `gitk --all` sees all of these obsolete commits; `jj log` only\n233\tshows the current version of each change.\n234\t\n235\t### Useful commands\n236\t\n237\t| Command | Description |\n238\t|---------|-------------|\n239\t| `jj log` | Show recent visible commits (default revset) |\n240\t| `jj log -r ::@` | Show **all** ancestors of the working copy |\n241\t| `jj log -r 'all()'` | Show all non-hidden commits (needed if you have multiple heads/branches) |\n242\t| `jj st | Show the status of the Working and Parent commits |\n243\t| `jj st -r <chid> | Status of the commit, <chid> such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n244\t| `jj show | Show the Working commit, -r @ |\n245\t| `jj show -r <chid> | Show the commit, <chid> such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n246\t| `jj evolog -r <chid>` | Show the evolution history of a single change |\n247\t| `jj op log` | Show operation history (each rewrite operation) |\n248\t\n249\t\n250\tIn a single-branch workflow, `jj log -r ::@` and `jj log -r 'all()'` give\n251\tthe same result. Use `all()` when you have multiple branches or heads.\n252\t\n253\t## Cross-repo Linking with Git Trailers\n254\t\n255\tCommits in each repo use [git trailers](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-interpret-trailers)\n256\tto cross-reference their counterpart in the other repo. The `ochid`\n257\t(Other Change ID) trailer contains a workspace-root-relative path\n258\tand jj changeID:\n259\t\n260\t```\n261\tochid: /.claude/xvzvruqo   # points to a .claude repo change\n262\tochid: /wtpmottv            # points to an app repo change\n263\t```\n264\t\n265\tPaths always start with `/` (the workspace root, i.e. vc-x1).\n266\tEach repo has a `.vc-config.toml` that identifies its location\n267\twithin the workspace, so tools can resolve these paths locally.\n268\t\n269\tFor full details see:\n270\t- [Git trailer vc-template-x1\n\nThis is the main repo of a dual-repo convention for using\na bot to help in the development of a coding project. The goal\nis that this main repo contains the \"what\", while the partner\nbot repo contains \"why\" and \"how\". The key to the convention\nis each change is cross-referenced to the other. Thus there\nis a coherent story of the development of the project across time.\n\nThe beginnings of that tool is [vc-x1](https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1)\nwhich currently does achieve this goal, but is being used as a\nfirst test bed.\n\n## This is a template — customize freely\n\n`CLAUDE.md` and this `README.md` are just starting points.\nRead both and edit either to match the conventions you want for your\nproject. In particular, decisions like the `cargo install` behavior\n(default re-resolve vs `--locked`) under [Releasing](#releasing) are\nyours to make — pick what fits and update the docs (and the CLAUDE.md\npre-commit checklist) so the choice is recorded for future readers.\n\n## Cloning\n\nThe Bot session repo is setup as a git submodule which\nmakes it easier to clone both repos. The easiest is to\nclone both when doing the initial clone:\n```\ngit clone --recurisve git@github.com:winksaville/vc-template-x1\n```\n\nIf you forget to use --recurisze you need to do two additional\nsteps \"init\" and \"update\":\n```\ngit clone git@github.com:winksaville/vc-template-x1\ngit submodule init\ngit submodule update\n```\n\nAnd these can be combined using 'update --init' if you like\n```\ngit clone git@github.com:winksaville/vc-template-x1\ngit submodule update --init\n```\n\n## Releasing\n\n**`cargo install` lockfile gotcha.**\n\nIf you install your project's binary with `cargo install --path .`,\nthis template recommends also passing `--locked`. Plain\n`cargo install` ignores `Cargo.lock` and re-resolves dependencies\nfrom scratch, so it can silently produce a binary built from a\ndifferent (and possibly broken) dependency graph than `cargo build`\n/ `cargo test` ran against. There is no stable cargo config knob\nto make `--locked` the default for `cargo install`, so the\ndiscipline lives in the project's pre-commit checklist and shell\naliases.\n\nThe trade-off is predictable-as-tested (`--locked`) vs picking up\nupstream security/bug fixes via fresh resolves (default). Either\nis defensible — pick what fits your project, then edit this\nsection and CLAUDE.md's pre-commit step 6 to match.\n\nFull background, repro details, and upstream cargo-issue ((main))\n$\n```\n\n### Why `jj log` shows fewer commits than `gitk`\n\nIf you're coming from git, jj's log output can be surprising compared to\ntools like `gitk --all`.\n\njj tracks *changes* (identified by change IDs), not individual git commits.\nWhen you rewrite a change (`jj describe`, `jj rebase`, `jj squash`, etc.),\njj creates a new git commit and keeps the old one under `refs/jj/keep/*` as\nundo history. `gitk --all` sees all of these obsolete commits; `jj log` only\nshows the current version of each change.\n\n### Useful commands\n\n| Command | Description |\n|---------|-------------|\n| `jj log` | Show recent visible commits (default revset) |\n| `jj log -r ::@` | Show **all** ancestors of the working copy |\n| `jj log -r 'all()'` | Show all non-hidden commits (needed if you have multiple heads/branches) |\n| `jj st | Show the status of the Working and Parent commits |\n| `jj st -r <chid> | Status of the commit, <chid> such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n| `jj show | Show the Working commit, -r @ |\n| `jj show -r <chid> | Show the commit, <chid> such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n| `jj evolog -r <chid>` | Show the evolution history of a single change |\n| `jj op log` | Show operation history (each rewrite operation) |\n\n\nIn a single-branch workflow, `jj log -r ::@` and `jj log -r 'all()'` give\nthe same result. Use `all()` when you have multiple branches or heads.\n\n## Cross-repo Linking with Git Trailers\n\nCommits in each repo use [git trailers](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-interpret-trailers)\nto cross-reference their counterpart in the other repo. The `ochid`\n(Other Change ID) trailer contains a workspace-root-relative path\nand jj changeID:\n\n```\nochid: /.claude/xvzvruqo   # points to a .claude repo change\nochid: /wtpmottv            # points to an app repo change\n```\n\nPaths always start with `/` (the workspace root, i.e. vc-x1).\nEach repo has a `.vc-config.toml` that identifies its location\nwithin the workspace, so tools can resolve these paths locally.\n\nFor full details see:\n- [Git trailer convention](./notes/chores-01.md#git-trailer-convention)\n  — [ochid (Other Change ID)](./notes/chores-01.md#ochid-other-change-id)\n  — [ChangeID path syntax](./notes/chores-01.md#changeid-path-syntax)\n  — [.vc-config.toml](./notes/chores-01.md#vc-configtoml)\n\n## ((main))\n$\n```\n\n## Why `jj log` shows fewer commits than `gitk`\n\nIf you're coming from git, jj's log output can be surprising compared to\ntools like `gitk --all`.\n\njj tracks *changes* (identified by change IDs), not individual git commits.\nWhen you rewrite a change (`jj describe`, `jj rebase`, `jj squash`, etc.),\njj creates a new git commit and keeps the old one under `refs/jj/keep/*` as\nundo history. `gitk --all` sees all of these obsolete commits; `jj log` only\nshows the current version of each change.\n\n## Useful commands\n\n| Command | Description |\n|---------|-------------|\n| `jj log` | Show recent visible commits (default revset) |\n| `jj log -r ::@` | Show **all** ancestors of the working copy |\n| `jj log -r 'all()'` | Show all non-hidden commits (needed if you have multiple heads/branches) |\n| `jj st | Show the status of the Working and Parent commits |\n| `jj st -r <chid> | Status of the commit, <chid> such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n| `jj show | Show the Working commit, -r @ |\n| `jj show -r <chid> | Show the commit, <chid> such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n| `jj evolog -r <chid>` | Show the evolution history of a single change |\n| `jj op log` | Show operation history (each rewrite operation) |\n\n\nIn a single-branch workflow, `jj log -r ::@` and `jj log -r 'all()'` give\nthe same result. Use `all()` when you have multiple branches or heads.\n\n## Cross-repo Linking with Git Trailers\n\nCommits in each repo use [git trailers](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-interpret-trailers)\nto cross-reference their counterpart in the other repo. The `ochid`\n(Other Change ID) trailer contains a workspace-root-relative path\nand jj changeID:\n\n```\nochid: /.claude/xvzvruqo   # points to a .claude repo change\nochid: /wtpmottv            # points to an app repo change\n```\n\nPaths always start with `/` (the workspace root, i.e. vc-x1).\nEach repo has a `.vc-config.toml` that identifies its location\nwithin the workspace, so tools can resolve these paths locally.\n\nFor full details see:\n- [Git trailer convention](./notes/chores-01.md#git-trailer-convention)\n  — [ochid (Other Change ID)](./notes/chores-01.md#ochid-other-change-id)\n  — [ChangeID path syntax](./notes/chores-01.md#changeid-path-syntax)\n  — [.vc-config.toml](./notes/chores-01.md#vc-configtoml)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":6,"oldLines":9,"newStart":6,"newLines":9,"lines":[" "," ## Initial Commit for a repo"," ","-Create create directory add files.","+Create a directory and add your files."," ","-Minimal commands to push ","+Minimal commands to push"," "," ```"," jj git init ."]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"132af8d1-246f-47bc-ad98-e212310d48ac","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/vc-template-x1","sessionId":"e5ec0e9d-b1c8-4143-a844-c6e520a1770b","version":"2.1.159","gitBranch":"HEAD"}

((main))\n$\n```\n\n## Why `jj log` shows fewer commits than `gitk`\n\nIf you're coming from git, jj's log output can be surprising compared to\ntools like `gitk --all`.\n\njj tracks *changes* (identified by change IDs), not individual git commits.\nWhen you rewrite a change (`jj describe`, `jj rebase`, `jj squash`, etc.),\njj creates a new git commit and keeps the old one under `refs/jj/keep/*` as\nundo history. `gitk --all` sees all of these obsolete commits; `jj log` only\nshows the current version of each change.\n\n## Useful commands\n\n| Command | Description |\n|---------|-------------|\n| `jj log` | Show recent visible commits (default revset) |\n| `jj log -r ::@` | Show **all** ancestors of the working copy |\n| `jj log -r 'all()'` | Show all non-hidden commits (needed if you have multiple heads/branches) |\n| `jj st | Show the status of the Working and Parent commits |\n| `jj st -r <chid> | Status of the commit, <chid> such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n| `jj show | Show the Working commit, -r @ |\n| `jj show -r <chid> | Show the commit, <chid> such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n| `jj evolog -r <chid>` | Show the evolution history of a single change |\n| `jj op log` | Show operation history (each rewrite operation) |\n\n\nIn a single-branch workflow, `jj log -r ::@` and `jj log -r 'all()'` give\nthe same result. Use `all()` when you have multiple branches or heads.\n\n## Cross-repo Linking with Git Trailers\n\nCommits in each repo use [git trailers](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-interpret-trailers)\nto cross-reference their counterpart in the other repo. The `ochid`\n(Other Change ID) trailer contains a workspace-root-relative path\nand jj changeID:\n\n```\nochid: /.claude/xvzvruqo   # points to a .claude repo change\nochid: /wtpmottv            # points to an app repo change\n```\n\nPaths always start with `/` (the workspace root, i.e. vc-x1).\nEach repo has a `.vc-config.toml` that identifies its location\nwithin the workspace, so tools can resolve these paths locally.\n\nFor full details see:\n- [Git trailer convention](./notes/chores-01.md#git-trailer-convention)\n  — [ochid (Other Change ID)](./notes/chores-01.md#ochid-other-change-id)\n  — [ChangeID path syntax](./notes/chores-01.md#changeid-path-syntax)\n  — ((main))\n$\n```\n\n## Why `jj log` shows fewer commits than `gitk`\n\nIf you're coming from git, jj's log output can be surprising compared to\ntools like `gitk --all`.\n\njj tracks *changes* (identified by change IDs), not individual git commits.\nWhen you rewrite a change (`jj describe`, `jj rebase`, `jj squash`, etc.),\njj creates a new git commit and keeps the old one under `refs/jj/keep/*` as\nundo history. `gitk --all` sees all of these obsolete commits; `jj log` only\nshows the current version of each change.\n\n## Useful commands\n\n| Command | Description |\n|---------|-------------|\n| `jj log` | Show recent visible commits (default revset) |\n| `jj log -r ::@` | Show **all** ancestors of the working copy |\n| `jj log -r 'all()'` | Show all non-hidden commits (needed if you have multiple heads/branches) |\n| `jj st` | Show the status of the Working and Parent commits |\n| `jj st -r <chid>` | Status of the commit, `<chid>` such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n| `jj show` | Show the Working commit (`-r @`) |\n| `jj show -r <chid>` | Show the commit, `<chid>` such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n| `jj evolog -r <chid>` | Show the evolution history of a single change |\n| `jj op log` | Show operation history (each rewrite operation) |\n\n\nIn a single-branch workflow, `jj log -r ::@` and `jj log -r 'all()'` give\nthe same result. Use `all()` when you have multiple branches or heads.\n\n## Cross-repo Linking with Git Trailers\n\nCommits in each repo use [git trailers](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-interpret-trailers)\nto cross-reference their counterpart in the other repo. The `ochid`\n(Other Change ID) trailer contains a workspace-root-relative path\nand jj changeID:\n\n```\nochid: /.claude/xvzvruqo   # points to a .claude repo change\nochid: /wtpmottv            # points to an app repo change\n```\n\nPaths always start with `/` (the workspace root, i.e. vc-x1).\nEach repo has a `.vc-config.toml` that identifies its location\nwithin the workspace, so tools can resolve these paths locally.\n\nFor full details see:\n- [Git trailer convention](./notes/chores-01.md#git-trailer-convention)\n  — [ochid (Other Change ID)](./notes/chores-01.md#ochid-other-change-id)\n  — [ChangeID path syntax](./notes/chores-01.md#changeid-path-syntax)\n  — [.vc-config.toml](./notes/chores-01.md#vc-configtoml)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":195,"oldLines":12,"newStart":195,"newLines":13,"lines":[" ochid: /wtpmottv            # points to an app repo change"," ```"," ","-Paths always start with `/` (the workspace root, i.e. vc-x1).","-Each repo has a `.vc-config.toml` that identifies its location","-within the workspace, so tools can resolve these paths locally.","+Paths always start with `/` (the workspace root, i.e.","+vc-template-x1). By\n50\tdefault `cargo install` ignores `Cargo.lock` and re-resolves\n51\tdependencies from scratch, so it can silently build the binary from\n52\ta different — possibly broken — dependency graph than `cargo build`\n53\t/ `cargo test` ran against.\n54\t\n55\t| command | reads `Cargo.lock`? | re-resolves? |\n56\t| --- | --- | --- |\n57\t| `cargo build` / `test` / `run`  | yes     | only if `Cargo.toml` changed |\n58\t| `cargo build --locked` (etc.)   | yes     | never; errors if it would need to |\n59\t| `cargo install` (default)       | **no**  | always, from scratch |\n60\t| `cargo install --locked`        | yes     | never; errors if it would need to |\n61\t\n62\tThere's no stable cargo config knob to make `--locked` the default\n63\tfor `cargo install`, so the discipline lives in the per-commit cargo\n64\tcycle and shell aliases (e.g. `alias ci='cargo install --locked'`).\n65\t\n66\tThe trade-off is predictable-as-tested (`--locked`) vs picking up\n67\tupstream fixes via fresh resolves (default). Either is defensible —\n68\tpick what fits your project, then edit this section and the\n69\tper-commit cargo cycle to match. ((main))\n$\n```\n\n## Why `jj log` shows fewer commits than `gitk`\n\nIf you're coming from git, jj's log output can be surprising compared to\ntools like `gitk --all`.\n\njj tracks *changes* (identified by change IDs), not individual git commits.\nWhen you rewrite a change (`jj describe`, `jj rebase`, `jj squash`, etc.),\njj creates a new git commit and keeps the old one under `refs/jj/keep/*` as\nundo history. `gitk --all` sees all of these obsolete commits; `jj log` only\nshows the current version of each change.\n\n## Useful commands\n\n| Command | Description |\n|---------|-------------|\n| `jj log` | Show recent visible commits (default revset) |\n| `jj log -r ::@` | Show **all** ancestors of the working copy |\n| `jj log -r 'all()'` | Show all non-hidden commits (needed if you have multiple heads/branches) |\n| `jj st` | Show the status of the Working and Parent commits |\n| `jj st -r <chid>` | Status of the commit, `<chid>` such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n| `jj show` | Show the Working commit (`-r @`) |\n| `jj show -r <chid>` | Show the commit, `<chid>` such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n| `jj evolog -r <chid>` | Show the evolution history of a single change |\n| `jj op log` | Show operation history (each rewrite operation) |\n\n\nIn a single-branch workflow, `jj log -r ::@` and `jj log -r 'all()'` give\nthe same result. Use `all()` when you have multiple branches or heads.\n\n## Cross-repo Linking with Git Trailers\n\nCommits in each repo use [git trailers](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-interpret-trailers)\nto cross-reference their counterpart in the other repo. The `ochid`\n(Other Change ID) trailer contains a workspace-root-relative path\nand jj changeID:\n\n```\nochid: /.claude/xvzvruqo   # points to a .claude repo change\nochid: /wtpmottv            # points to an app repo change\n```\n\nPaths always start with `/` (the workspace root, i.e.\nvc-template-x1). Each repo has a `.vc-config.toml` that\nidentifies its location within the workspace, so tools can\nresolve these paths locally.\n\nFor full details see:\n- [Git trailer convention](vc-notes.md#git-trailer-convention)\n  — [ochid (Other Change ID)](vc-notes.md#ochid-other-change-id)\n  — [ChangeID path syntax](vc-notes.md#changeid-path-syntax)\n  — [.vc-config.toml](vc-notes.md#vc-configtoml)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":200,"oldLines":8,"newStart":200,"newLines":6,"lines":[" identifies its location within the workspace, so tools can"," resolve these paths locally."," ","-For full details see:","-- [Git trailer convention](vc-notes.md#git-trailer-convention)","-  — [ochid (Other Change ID)](vc-notes.md#ochid-other-change-id)","-  — [ChangeID path syntax](vc-notes.md#changeid-path-syntax)","-  — [.vc-config.toml](vc-notes.md#vc-configtoml)","+For the full convention — path syntax, per-commit mechanics, and","+`.vc-config.toml` — see","+[Cross-repo linking (ochid trailers)](../AGENTS.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)."]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"fc886d17-8eb2-4223-b123-58702da81540","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/vc-template-x1","sessionId":"e5ec0e9d-b1c8-4143-a844-c6e520a1770b","version":"2.1.159","gitBranch":"HEAD"}

A\nrevision is identified by `@`, a chid, or a cid, and revsets are\nbuilt from those identifiers plus the operators `-`, `+`, `..`,\nand `::`. There is a complete language available — see\n`jj help -k revsets`. The [`substep-test.sh`](substep-test.sh)\nscript scaffolds the example repo used below.\n\nSummary:\n\n- A revision (rev) is used for addressing/referring to commits.\n- jj supports a change_id (chid) and commit_id (cid).\n  - The chid is permanent and doesn't change.\n  - The cid is the SHA of the current commit and changes with any\n    change to it or its ancestors.\n- A revset is a set of revisions.\n- In many jj commands revsets can address multiple commits.\n- There is one root commit; chid=zzz sha=0 owner=root.\n- The root commit never has content nor description.\n- There can be multiple independent lineages of commits off root():\n  - to create:\n    - `jj new 'root()'`\n    - `git switch --orphan <name>`\n  - to see these:\n    - `jj log -r 'roots(~root())'`\n    - `git log --all --max-parents=0 --oneline`\n\nThe examples below show these primitives in action.\n\n### A jj repo with some commits\n\nSome examples of revisions/rev:\n   - @, chid=tkpvsrop, cid=ad2ba9b4 is the current commit\n   - @-, chid=wxtmosqz, cid=35ac2422 is the ancestor of the current commit\n   - @--, chid=vktlnyvm, cid=a0b0285e is the ancestor of the ancestor and so on\n\n```\n$ jj log -r 'all()'\n@  tkpvsrop wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 ad2ba9b4\n│  count 3\n○  wxtmosqz wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 35ac2422\n│  count 2\n○  vktlnyvm wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 a0b0285e\n│  count 1\n○  nvwytkrw wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 base 54fd18f7\n│  count 0\n◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000\n```\n\nMove @ to vktlnyvm. (This could also have been done with `jj edit -r @--`.)\n\n```\n$ jj edit -r vkt\nWorking copy  (@) now at: vktlnyvm a0b0285e count 1\nParent commit (@-)      : nvwytkrw 54fd18f7 base | count 0\n```\n\n### Referencing commits with relative revsets\n\n```\n$ jj log -r @\n@  vktlnyvm count 1\n$ jj log -r @-\n○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n$ jj log -r @--\n◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000\n$ jj log -r @+\n○  wxtmosqz count 2\n$ jj log -r @++\n○  tkpvsrop count 3\n$ jj log -r @+++      # empty — nothing that far out\n$ jj log -r @---      # empty\n$ jj log -r @..\n○  tkpvsrop count 3\n○  wxtmosqz count 2\n$ jj log -r @::\n○  tkpvsrop count 3\n○  wxtmosqz count 2\n@  vktlnyvm count 1\n$ jj log -r ..@\n@  vktlnyvm count 1\n○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n$ jj log -r ::@\n@  vktlnyvm count 1\n○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000\n```\n\n#### Interpretation\n\n- `@-` and `@--` resolve to single revisions: parent and\n  grandparent of @. `@+` and `@++` are children. The blank output\n  for `@+++` and `@---` is the empty revset — there is no revision\n  that far away in this chain.\n- `@..` and `@::` are ranges going outward from @ toward\n  descendants:\n  - `@..` is the *open* form: descendants of @, **excluding** @\n    itself (here: count 2 and count 3).\n  - `@::` is the *closed* form: descendants of @, **including** @\n    itself (here: @=count 1, count 2, count 3).\n- `..@` and `::@` are ranges going inward from some implicit start\n  toward ancestors of @:\n  - `..@` includes @ and its ancestors but **excludes** the root\n    commit (here: @=count 1, base=count 0).\n  - `::@` includes the root commit as well.\n\nMnemonic: `..` and `::` both produce ranges; `::` includes the\nimplicit endpoint (root or visible heads), `..` excludes it. The\nnamed operand is always part of the result on the target side; on\nthe source side it depends on which dot-form is used (excluded by\n`..`, included by `::`).\n\n### Referencing commits with absolute revsets\n\n```\n$ jj log -r v          # unambiguous prefix of vktlnyvm\n@  vktlnyvm count 1\n$ jj log -r vktln\n@  vktlnyvm count 1\n$ jj log -r w+         # w matches wxtmosqz, + takes its child\n○  tkpvsrop count 3\n$ jj log -r w--\n○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n$ jj log -r w..\n○  tkpvsrop count 3\n$ jj log -r ..w\n○  wxtmosqz count 2\n@  vktlnyvm count 1\n○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n$ jj log -r w::\n○  tkpvsrop count 3\n○  wxtmosqz count 2\n$ jj log -r ::w\n○  wxtmosqz count 2\n@  vktlnyvm count 1\n○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000\n```\n\n#### Interpretation\n\n- `v` and `vktln` both resolve to chid `vktlnyvm` because they are\n  unambiguous prefixes within this repo — no other chid starts\n  with those letters.\n- `w+` resolves in two stages: `w` matches `wxtmosqz` (count 2) by\n  prefix, then `+` takes its child, giving count 3.\n- `w--` grandparent of w.\n- `w..` descendants of w, excluding w.\n- `..w` ancestors of w, not including root.\n- `::w` ancestors of w, including root.\n- `w::` descendants of w, including w.\n\nPrefix rule: jj rejects ambiguous prefixes. [Steve Klabnik](https://github.com/steveklabnik)\n[Jujutsu-tutorial](https://steveklabnik.github.io/jujutsu-tutorial)\nand [jj docs](https://docs.jj-vcs.dev/latest/).\n\n## Initial Commit for a ((main))\n$\n```\n\n## Why `jj log` shows fewer commits than `gitk`\n\nIf you're coming from git, jj's log output can be surprising compared to\ntools like `gitk --all`.\n\njj tracks *changes* (identified by change IDs), not individual git commits.\nWhen you rewrite a change (`jj describe`, `jj rebase`, `jj squash`, etc.),\njj creates a new git commit and keeps the old one under `refs/jj/keep/*` as\nundo history. `gitk --all` sees all of these obsolete commits; `jj log` only\nshows the current version of each change.\n\n## Useful commands\n\n| Command | Description |\n|---------|-------------|\n| `jj log` | Show recent visible commits (default revset) |\n| `jj log -r ::@` | Show **all** ancestors of the working copy |\n| `jj log -r 'all()'` | Show all non-hidden commits (needed if you have multiple heads/branches) |\n| `jj st` | Show the status of the Working and Parent commits |\n| `jj st -r <chid>` | Status of the commit, `<chid>` such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n| `jj show` | Show the Working commit (`-r @`) |\n| `jj show -r <chid>` | Show the commit, `<chid>` such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n| `jj evolog -r <chid>` | Show the evolution history of a single change |\n| `jj op log` | Show operation history (each rewrite operation) |\n\n\nIn a single-branch workflow, `jj log -r ::@` and `jj log -r 'all()'` give\nthe same result. Use `all()` when you have multiple branches or heads.\n\n## Cross-repo Linking with Git Trailers\n\nCommits in each repo use [git trailers](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-interpret-trailers)\nto cross-reference their counterpart in the other repo. The `ochid`\n(Other Change ID) trailer contains a workspace-root-relative path\nand jj changeID:\n\n```\nochid: /.claude/xvzvruqo   # points to a .claude repo change\nochid: /wtpmottv            # points to an app repo change\n```\n\nPaths always start with `/` (the workspace root, i.e.\nvc-template-x1). A","+revision is identified by `@`, a chid, or a cid, and revsets are","+built from those identifiers plus the operators `-`, `+`, `..`,","+and `::`. There is a complete language available — see","+`jj help -k revsets`. The [`substep-test.sh`](substep-test.sh)","+script scaffolds the example repo used below.","+","+Summary:","+","+- A revision (rev) is used for addressing/referring to commits.","+- jj supports a change_id (chid) and commit_id (cid).","+  - The chid is permanent and doesn't change.","+  - The cid is the SHA of the current commit and changes with any","+    change to it or its ancestors.","+- A revset is a set of revisions.","+- In many jj commands revsets can address multiple commits.","+- There is one root commit; chid=zzz sha=0 owner=root.","+- The root commit never has content nor description.","+- There can be multiple independent lineages of commits off root():","+  - to create:","+    - `jj new 'root()'`","+    - `git switch --orphan <name>`","+  - to see these:","+    - `jj log -r 'roots(~root())'`","+    - `git log --all --max-parents=0 --oneline`","+","+The examples below show these primitives in action.","+","+### A jj repo with some commits","+","+Some examples of revisions/rev:","+   - @, chid=tkpvsrop, cid=ad2ba9b4 is the current commit","+   - @-, chid=wxtmosqz, cid=35ac2422 is the ancestor of the current commit","+   - @--, chid=vktlnyvm, cid=a0b0285e is the ancestor of the ancestor and so on","+","+```","+$ jj log -r 'all()'","+@  tkpvsrop wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 ad2ba9b4","+│  count 3","+○  wxtmosqz wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 35ac2422","+│  count 2","+○  vktlnyvm wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 a0b0285e","+│  count 1","+○  nvwytkrw wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 base 54fd18f7","+│  count 0","+◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000","+```","+","+Move @ to vktlnyvm. The blank output","+  for `@+++` and `@---` is the empty revset — there is no revision","+  that far away in this chain.","+- `@..` and `@::` are ranges going outward from @ toward","+  descendants:","+  - `@..` is the *open* form: descendants of @, **excluding** @","+    itself (here: count 2 and count 3).","+  - `@::` is the *closed* form: descendants of @, **including** @","+    itself (here: @=count 1, count 2, count 3).","+- `..@` and `::@` are ranges going inward from some implicit start","+  toward ancestors of @:","+  - `..@` includes @ and its ancestors but **excludes** the root","+    commit (here: @=count 1, base=count 0).","+  - `::@` includes the root commit as well.","+","+Mnemonic: `..` and `::` both produce ranges; `::` includes the","+implicit endpoint (root or visible heads), `..` excludes it. The goal\nis that this main repo contains the \"what\", while the partner\nbot repo contains \"why\" and \"how\". The key to the convention\nis each change is cross-referenced to the other. Thus there\nis a coherent story of the development of the project across time.\n\nThe beginnings of that tool is [vc-x1](https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1)\nwhich currently does achieve this goal, but is being used as a\nfirst test bed.\n\n## This is a template — customize freely\n\n`CLAUDE.md` and this `README.md` are just starting points.\nRead both and edit either to match the conventions you want for your\nproject. In particular, decisions like the `cargo install` behavior\n(default re-resolve vs `--locked`) under [Releasing](#releasing) are\nyours to make — pick what fits and update the docs (and the\nper-commit cargo cycle) so the choice is recorded for future readers.\n\n## Cloning\n\nThe Bot session repo is setup as a git submodule which\nmakes it easier to clone both repos. The easiest is to\nclone both when doing the initial clone:\n```\ngit clone --recurisve git@github.com:winksaville/vc-template-x1\n```\n\nIf you forget to use --recursive you need to do two additional\nsteps \"init\" and \"update\":\n```\ngit clone git@github.com:winksaville/vc-template-x1\ngit submodule init\ngit submodule update\n```\n\nAnd these can be combined using 'update --init' if you like\n```\ngit clone git@github.com:winksaville/vc-template-x1\ngit submodule update --init\n```\n\n## Releasing\n\n**`cargo install` lockfile gotcha.** If you install your project's\nbinary with `cargo install --path .`, also pass `--locked`. By\ndefault `cargo install` ignores `Cargo.lock` and re-resolves\ndependencies from scratch, so it can silently build the binary from\na different — possibly broken — dependency graph than `cargo build`\n/ `cargo test` ran against.\n\n| command | reads `Cargo.lock`? | re-resolves? |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `cargo build` / `test` / `run`  | yes     | only if `Cargo.toml` changed |\n| `cargo build --locked` (etc.)   | yes     | never; errors if it would need to |\n| `cargo install` (default)       | **no**  | always, from scratch |\n| `cargo install --locked`        | yes     | never; errors if it would need to |\n\nThere's no stable cargo config knob to make `--locked` the default\nfor `cargo install`, so the discipline lives in the per-commit cargo\ncycle and shell aliases (e.g. `alias ci='cargo install --locked'`).\n\nThe trade-off is predictable-as-tested (`--locked`) vs picking up\nupstream fixes via fresh resolves (default). Either is defensible —\npick what fits your project, then edit this section and the\nper-commit cargo cycle to match. ((main))\n190\t$\n191\t```\n192\t\n193\t### Why `jj log` shows fewer commits than `gitk`\n194\t\n195\tIf you're coming from git, jj's log output can be surprising compared to\n196\ttools like `gitk --all`.\n197\t\n198\tjj tracks *changes* (identified by change IDs), not individual git commits.\n199\tWhen you rewrite a change (`jj describe`, `jj rebase`, `jj squash`, etc.),\n200\tjj creates a new git commit and keeps the old one under `refs/jj/keep/*` as\n201\tundo history. `gitk --all` sees all of these obsolete commits; `jj log` only\n202\tshows the current version of each change.\n203\t\n204\t### Useful commands\n205\t\n206\t| Command | Description |\n207\t|---------|-------------|\n208\t| `jj log` | Show recent visible commits (default revset) |\n209\t| `jj log -r ::@` | Show **all** ancestors of the working copy |\n210\t| `jj log -r 'all()'` | Show all non-hidden commits (needed if you have multiple heads/branches) |\n211\t| `jj st | Show the status of the Working and Parent commits |\n212\t| `jj st -r <chid> | Status of the commit, <chid> such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n213\t| `jj show | Show the Working commit, -r @ |\n214\t| `jj show -r <chid> | Show the commit, <chid> such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n215\t| `jj evolog -r <chid>` | Show the evolution history of a single change |\n216\t| `jj op log` | Show operation history (each rewrite operation) |\n217\t\n218\t\n219\tIn a single-branch workflow, `jj log -r ::@` and `jj log -r 'all()'` give\n220\tthe same result. Use `all()` when you have multiple branches or heads.\n221\t\n222\t## Cross-repo Linking with Git Trailers\n223\t\n224\tCommits in each repo use [git trailers](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-interpret-trailers)\n225\tto cross-reference their counterpart in the other repo. The `ochid`\n226\t(Other Change ID) trailer contains a workspace-root-relative path\n227\tand jj changeID:\n228\t\n229\t```\n230\tochid: /.claude/xvzvruqo   # points to a .claude repo change\n231\tochid: /wtpmottv            # points to an app repo change\n232\t```\n233\t\n234\tPaths always start with `/` (the workspace root, i.e. vc-x1).\n235\tEach repo has a `.vc-config.toml` that identifies its location\n236\twithin the workspace, so tools can resolve these paths locally.\n237\t\n238\tFor full details see:\n239\t- [Git trailer vc-template-x1\n\nThis is the main repo of a dual-repo convention for using\na bot to help in the development of a coding project. The goal\nis that this main repo contains the \"what\", while the partner\nbot repo contains \"why\" and \"how\". The key to the convention\nis each change is cross-referenced to the other. The easiest is to\nclone both when doing the initial clone:\n```\ngit clone --recurisve git@github.com:winksaville/vc-template-x1\n```\n\nIf you forget to use --recurisze you need to do two additional\nsteps \"init\" and \"update\":\n```\ngit clone git@github.com:winksaville/vc-template-x1\ngit submodule init\ngit submodule update\n```\n\nAnd these can be combined using 'update --init' ((main))\n$\n```\n\n### Why `jj log` shows fewer commits than `gitk`\n\nIf you're coming from git, jj's log output can be surprising compared to\ntools like `gitk --all`.\n\njj tracks *changes* (identified by change IDs), not individual git commits.\nWhen you rewrite a change (`jj describe`, `jj rebase`, `jj squash`, etc.),\njj creates a new git commit and keeps the old one under `refs/jj/keep/*` as\nundo history. `gitk --all` sees all of these obsolete commits; `jj log` only\nshows the current version of each change.\n\n### Useful commands\n\n| Command | Description |\n|---------|-------------|\n| `jj log` | Show recent visible commits (default revset) |\n| `jj log -r ::@` | Show **all** ancestors of the working copy |\n| `jj log -r 'all()'` | Show all non-hidden commits (needed if you have multiple heads/branches) |\n| `jj st | Show the status of the Working and Parent commits |\n| `jj st -r <chid> | Status of the commit, <chid> such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n| `jj show | Show the Working commit, -r @ |\n| `jj show -r <chid> | Show the commit, <chid> such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n| `jj evolog -r <chid>` | Show the evolution history of a single change |\n| `jj op log` | Show operation history (each rewrite operation) |\n\n\nIn a single-branch workflow, `jj log -r ::@` and `jj log -r 'all()'` give\nthe same result. Use `all()` when you have multiple branches or heads.\n\n## Cross-repo Linking with Git Trailers\n\nCommits in each repo use [git trailers](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-interpret-trailers)\nto cross-reference their counterpart in the other repo. The `ochid`\n(Other Change ID) trailer contains a workspace-root-relative path\nand jj changeID:\n\n```\nochid: /.claude/xvzvruqo   # points to a .claude repo change\nochid: /wtpmottv            # points to an app repo change\n```\n\nPaths always start with `/` (the workspace root, i.e. vc-x1).\nEach repo has a `.vc-config.toml` that identifies its location\nwithin the workspace, so tools can resolve these paths locally.\n\nFor full details see:\n- [Git trailer convention](./notes/chores-01.md#git-trailer-convention)\n  — [ochid (Other Change ID)](./notes/chores-01.md#ochid-other-change-id)\n  — [ChangeID path syntax](./notes/chores-01.md#changeid-path-syntax)\n  — [.vc-config.toml](./notes/chores-01.md#vc-configtoml)\n\n## Long absolute paths\n28\tclutter the transcript without adding information. Out-of-workspace\n29\tpaths (`/tmp/...`, `~/.config/...`) stay absolute. In a dual-repo setup with\n37\tCLAUDE.md it provides no capability CLAUDE.md doesn't already cover,\n38\tand it loses on discoverability:\n39\t\n40\t- **CLAUDE.md** — at the repo root, a well-known location for bot\n41\t  instructions, committed, reviewable, visible to every collaborator\n42\t  (human or bot).\n43\t- **Memory directory** — hidden under the user's home, tied to one\n44\t  machine, invisible to anyone but the bot, never diffed or reviewed.\n45\t\n46\tEasy for everyone to find beats convenient for the bot alone. Put\n47\tdurable context in CLAUDE.md (or committed `notes/`) instead.\n48\t\n49\t## Speculation marker\n50\t\n51\tDurable text the bot writes — CLAUDE.md, `notes/`, commit bodies,\n52\tchores sections — should stick to observations and direct descriptions\n53\tof the code or data. If a mechanism, hypothesis, or causal claim\n54\tenters the text, prefix it with \"The bot thinks ...\" so a reader can\n55\ttell the measured from the inferred.\n56\t\n57\t**Why:** unmarked speculation reads like evidence, and a future reader\n58\t(or the bot on a later session) can pick it up as a known fact when\n59\tit's not. Measured / inferred is a distinction worth keeping visible\n60\tin the written record.\n61\t\n62\t**How to apply:** observations and factual descriptions need no\n63\tmarker. Prefix with \"The bot thinks ...\" (or a close variant like\n64\t\"The bot's guess is ...\") when the claim is a mechanism (\"X wins\n65\tbecause Y caches better\"), a cause (\"the drift was due to thermal\n66\tstate\"), a prediction (\"this should scale linearly\"), or any\n67\treasoning not directly supported by the data on hand.\n68\t\n69\t## Committing\n70\t\n71\tUse `-R` (`--repository`) at the end to target the correct repo. Use\n72\trelative paths to reduce noise. Putting `-R` last keeps the verb/action\n73\tvisible at the start of the command.\n74\t\n75\t### App repo\n76\t```\n77\tjj commit -m \\\n78\t\"title\" \\\n79\t-m \"body\n80\t\n81\tochid: /.claude/<changeID>\" \\\n82\t-R .\n83\t```\n84\t\n85\t### Bot session repo\n86\t```\n87\tjj commit -m \\\n88\t\"title\" \\\n89\t-m \"body\n90\t\n91\tochid: /<changeID>\" \\\n92\t-R .claude\n93\t```\n94\t\n95\t## jj Basics\n96\t\n97\t- `jj st -R .` / `jj st -R .claude` — show working copy status\n98\t- `jj log -R .` / `jj log -R .claude` — show commit log\n99\t- `jj commit -m \"title\" -m \"body\" -R <repo>` — finalize working copy into a commit\n100\t- `jj describe -m \"title\" -m \"body\" -R <repo>` — set description without committing\n101\t- `jj git push --bookmark <name> -R <repo>` — push a bookmark (no\n102\t  `--allow-new` flag; jj pushes new bookmarks without special flags)\n103\t- In jj, the working copy (@) is always a mutable commit being edited.\n104\t  `jj commit` finalizes it and creates a new empty working copy on top.\n105\t- The `.claude` repo always has uncommitted changes during an active\n106\t  session because session data updates continuously.\n107\t\n108\t## Commit Message Style\n109\t\n110\tUse [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) with\n111\ta version suffix:\n112\t\n113\t```\n114\t<type>: <short description> (<version>)\n115\t```\n116\t\n117\t- **Title**: target ~50 chars, short summary of *what* changed.\n118\t  Include the version. Common types: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`,\n119\t  `test`, `docs`, `chore`.\n120\t- **App-repo body**: short intro paragraph (1–3 sentences), then a\n121\t  terse bullet list. Each bullet corresponds one-to-one with the\n122\t  edits structure already documented in `notes/chores-*.md` for\n123\t  this step — just the file and a one-line gist (e.g.\n124\t  `README.md: new Overview intro`). Do *not* restate the detail\n125\t  that lives in chores; the commit body is a scan-able index, not\n126\t  a duplicate. The chores section is the source of truth.\n127\t- **Session-repo body**: terse intro + a few session-activity\n128\t  bullets. Doesn't need to mirror chores since it describes\n129\t  in-session work, not code changes.\n130\t- Examples:\n131\t  - `feat: add fix-ochid subcommand (0.22.0)`\n132\t  - `fix: fix-ochid prefix bug (0.22.1)`\n133\t  - `refactor: deduplicate common CLI flags (0.21.1)`\n134\t\n135\t## Pre-commit Requirements\n136\t\n137\t### User approval\n138\t\n139\tNever execute commit, squash, push, or finalize commands without the\n140\tuser's explicit approval. Present changes for review first; only run\n141\tthem after the user confirms. This applies to late changes too —\n142\tpause for review before squashing into an existing commit.\n143\t\n144\t### Review before proposing the commit block\n145\t\n146\tAfter finishing a unit of work, **summarize what changed and stop\n147\tthere**. Do not pre-emptively lay out the Checkpoint-1 commit\n148\tcommands. Wait for the user to signal review is complete before\n149\tproposing the commit block. Changes during review are the norm,\n150\tnot the exception; proposing commit text too early creates noise\n151\tand signals that I consider the work done when it usually isn't.\n152\t\n153\tThis applies per-step in a multi-step flow too — each step gets a\n154\treview pause before its commit block appears.\n155\t\n156\tSignals that review is complete include explicit approval (\"let's\n157\tcommit\", \"looks good, commit it\") **and any directive to start the\n158\tnext step** (\"do step 4\", \"next\", \"go N+1\"). In that case the\n159\tprevious step must be committed first — always commit the current\n160\tstep before starting the next; don't ask.\n161\t\n162\t### Notes references\n163\t\n164\tMultiple references must be separated: `[2],[3]` not `[2,3]` or `[2][3]`.\n165\tSee [Todo format](notes/README.md#todo-format) for details.\n166\t\n167\t### Markdown anchor links\n168\t\n169\tGitHub anchor algorithm: lowercase, strip non-alphanumeric\n170\tcharacters in place, map remaining spaces to hyphens 1-for-1. Do\n171\t**not** collapse adjacent whitespace — so `a + b` → `a--b` (spaces\n172\ton both sides of `+`), but `a: b` → `a-b` (only trailing space on\n173\t`:`). General markdown reference:\n174\t[markdownguide.org](https://www.markdownguide.org). GitHub\n175\tpublishes no official spec for auto-generated anchors; the\n176\tde-facto reference implementation is\n177\t[github-slugger](https://github.com/Flet/github-slugger).\n178\t\n179\t### Versioning\n180\t\n181\tEvery plan must start with a version bump. Choose the approach based\n182\ton scope:\n183\t\n184\t- **Single-step** (recommended for mechanical/focused changes): bump\n185\t  directly to `X.Y.Z`, implement in one commit. Simpler history.\n186\t- **Multi-step** (for exploratory/large changes): bump to `X.Y.Z-0`,\n187\t  implement across multiple commits incrementing the numeric\n188\t  suffix. The final commit drops the suffix.\n189\t\n190\tThe plan should recommend one approach and get user approval before\n191\tstarting.\n192\t\n193\tFor multi-step:\n194\t\n195\t1. Bump version to `X.Y.Z-0` with the plan and commit as a chore\n196\t   marker.\n197\t2. Implement in one or more `X.Y.Z-N` commits (increment N as\n198\t   needed).\n199\t3. Final commit bumps to `X.Y.Z` (no suffix), updates\n200\t   `notes/todo.md` and `notes/chores-*.md` — this is the \"done\"\n201\t   marker.\n202\t\n203\tMulti-step cycles surface the ladder at the top of\n204\t`notes/todo.md > ## In Progress` as a bullet list with `(done)` /\n205\t`(current)` markers — see the file's intro paragraph for the\n206\tformat. Update the markers as each step ships so the In Progress\n207\tview stays current at a glance.\n208\t\n209\t**Why numeric suffixes (`-0`, `-1`, …) rather than `-devN`:**\n210\tsemver pre-release identifiers may consist of a single numeric\n211\tcomponent, and they compare numerically per spec. So\n212\t`X.Y.Z-1 < X.Y.Z-2 < … < X.Y.Z` correctly orders the dev ladder\n213\tbelow the done marker. Cargo accepts this form. The `-dev` prefix\n214\tadds no information the git log doesn't already convey and\n215\tdoubles typing per commit.\n216\t\n217\tThe final release commit (no suffix) signals completion rather than\n218\tamending prior commits. This keeps history readable and makes it easy\n219\tto see which commits were exploratory vs final.\n220\t\n221\t### Chores section headers\n222\t\n223\tChores section headers use trailing version format:\n224\t\n225\t```\n226\t## Description (X.Y.Z)\n227\t```\n228\t\n229\tExample: `` ## Add `fn claude-symlink` (0.27.0) ``\n230\t\n231\t### Pre-commit checklist\n232\t\n233\tBefore proposing a commit, run all of the following and fix any issues:\n234\t\n235\t1. `cargo fmt`\n236\t2. `cargo clippy`\n237\t3. `cargo test`\n238\t4. `cargo install --path . --locked` (if applicable) — `--locked`\n239\t   is required: without it, `cargo install` ignores `Cargo.lock`\n240\t   and re-resolves from scratch, which can pick incompatible\n241\t   versions even when `cargo build` / `cargo test` succeed.\n242\t5. Retest after install\n243\t6. Update `notes/todo.md` — add to `## Done` if completing a task\n244\t7. Update `notes/chores-*.md` — add a subsection describing the change\n245\t8. Update `notes/README.md` — if functionality changed (new flags,\n246\t   new subcommands, changed behavior)\n247\t\n248\t## Code Conventions\n249\t\n250\t### Doc comments on every file, function, and method\n251\t\n252\tEvery `.rs` file must begin with a `//!` module docstring. Every\n253\tfunction and method must have a `///` doc comment. Keep them brief —\n254\tone sentence of purpose is often enough; the discipline is that the\n255\tcomment exists, not that it be long.\n256\t\n257\tThis is a deliberate override of the generic \"write no comments\"\n258\tdefault that applies to inline `//` comments. Summarize what's blocking — unclear\nrequirements, unfamiliar API surface, conflicting signals — and ask.\nContinued flailing produces worse outcomes than a direct \"I'm stuck\non X.\"\n\n## ochid Trailers\n\nEvery commit body must include an `ochid:` trailer pointing to the\ncounterpart commit in the other repo. Failures inside the\nlocal mutation window roll both repos back via `jj op restore`;\nafter `push-app` succeeds the remote boundary is crossed and\nrecovery is forward-only.\n\n**Run this flow after every step** — not only at session end.\nSingle-step and multi-step changes are of equal importance: a\nsingle-step change is one `push` invocation; a multi-step change\nis one `push` per `X.Y.Z-N` commit plus one for the final release\ncommit. Approve = \"the work is done right\".\n2. **Message** — push either uses `--title`/`--body` (non-editor\n   path) or opens `$EDITOR` on a template. Approve = \"the message\n   reads right\".\n\nBoth titles and bodies are the **same** across the two commits;\nonly the `ochid:` trailer differs per repo. Push collects the\npre-commit chids internally so you don't hand-manage them.\n\nFor the full flag list and stage machine, see `vc-x1 push --help`\nand `notes/chores-05.md > Add push subcommand (0.37.0)`.\n\n### Bot communication during the flow\n\nWhen applying the flow on the user's behalf, use plain prose at\neach gate — no insider jargon (\"Gate N signal\", \"Checkpoint N\",\netc.):\n\n1. **After completing the work** — summarize what changed\n   (file-by-file or feature-by-feature, terse) and end with\n   something like:\n\n   > Work complete. Check\nmode verifies divergence without applying — if anything is `behind`\nor `diverged`, preflight errors and you resolve explicitly with\n`vc-x1 sync --no-check` before re-running push. This keeps the\ntwo approval gates (review, message) authoritative; push never\nperforms an unsupervised rebase.\n\nRunning sync manually before you *start* editing is still cheap\n(one line when clean) and surfaces remote changes earlier:\n\n```\nvc-x1 sync --check                    # dual-repo workspace, verify\nvc-x1 sync --no-check                 # apply (rebase / fast-forward)\nvc-x1 sync --check -R .               # single-repo project\nvc-x1 sync --check --quiet            # silent; exit code signals result\n```\n\nBots and scripts must pass `--check` or `--no-check` explicitly —\ndefaults can shift, explicit flags lock in the contract. Interactive\nuse can take the default (which is `--check`).\n\nOutput shape:\n\n- **Clean**: one line — `sync: N repos, all bookmarks up-to-date`.\n  Note: scope is bookmark-vs-remote tracking, not working-copy\n  cleanliness — `@` may have uncommitted changes; sync doesn't\n  speak to that. Treat finalize as\na hard stop for the whole turn. Do not proceed on a guess and hope the\nresult lands right — a clarifying question costs a few seconds;\nredoing misaligned work costs much more.\n\n### Recognize when stuck\n\nIf a simple task has eaten 5+ minutes of thinking or back-and-forth\nwithout progress, stop. Summarize what's blocking — unclear\nrequirements, unfamiliar API surface, conflicting signals — and ask.\nContinued flailing produces worse outcomes than a direct \"I'm stuck\non X.\"\n\n## ochid Trailers\n\nEvery commit body must include an `ochid:` trailer pointing to the\ncounterpart commit in the other repo. Failures inside the\nlocal mutation window roll both repos back via `jj op restore`;\nafter `push-app` succeeds the remote boundary is crossed and\nrecovery is forward-only.\n\n**Run this flow after every step** — not only at session end.\nSingle-step and multi-step changes are of equal importance: a\nsingle-step change is one `push` invocation; a multi-step change\nis one `push` per `X.Y.Z-N` commit plus one for the final release\ncommit. Each step gets its own commit, its own push, and its own\nfinalize — so dev markers land on the remote and in `.claude` as\nthey happen rather than being batched until the end.\n\n### Run `vc-x1 push`\n\n```\nvc-x1 push main                                      # interactive (review + $EDITOR)\nvc-x1 push main --title \"...\" --body \"...\"           # flags skip $EDITOR\nvc-x1 push main --yes --title \"...\" --body \"...\"     # full non-interactive\nvc-x1 push main --dry-run                            # preview (no side effects)\nvc-x1 push main --from commit-app                    # resume from specific stage\nvc-x1 push --status                                  # show saved state\nvc-x1 push main --restart                            # clear saved state; start fresh\n```\n\nThe two approval gates are surfaced by push itself:\n\n1. **Review** — push prints `jj diff --stat` for both repos and\n   prompts `[y/N]`. Used by `vc-x1 push` internally; also available as a\n  manual fallback. See\n  [Manual finalize fallback](#manual-finalize-fallback) below.\n- `vc-x1 chid -R <r,...> -L` — print change IDs for the current\n  working commit in each repo, one per line. Used to compose\n  `ochid:` trailers when committing manually.\n- `vc-x1 fix-ochid` — repair a missing or stale `ochid:` trailer\n  in an existing commit.\n\nThe bot thinks the in-flight `--scope`, `--squash`, and\n`--message-file` flags on `vc-x1 push` are intended to replace\nthe current `--title` / `--body` flags with a richer message\nsource and a per-step scope selector; once shipped, they should\nbecome the default invocation. Until then, follow the flag set\ndocumented in [Run `vc-x1 push`](#run-vc-x1-push) below.\n\nFor the full command surface, run `vc-x1 --help` and\n`vc-x1 <subcommand> --help`.\n\n## Commits\n\n### Per-repo commit commands\n\nWhen committing manually (i.e. not via `vc-x1 push`), use `-R`\n(`--repository`) at the end to target the correct repo. Use\nrelative paths to reduce noise. Putting `-R` last keeps the\nverb/action visible at the start of the command.\n\n#### App repo\n```\njj commit -m \\\n\"title\" \\\n-m \"body\n\nochid: /.claude/<changeID>\" \\\n-R .\n```\n\n#### Bot session repo\n```\njj commit -m \\\n\"title\" \\\n-m \"body\n\nochid: /<changeID>\" \\\n-R .claude\n```\n\n### Commit message style\n\nUse [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) with\na version suffix:\n\n```\n<type>: <short description> (<version>)\n```\n\n- **Title**: target ~50 chars, short summary of *what* changed.\n  Include the version. Common types: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`,\n  `test`, `docs`, `chore`.\n- **Body** (same across both repos): short intro paragraph (1–3\n  sentences), then a terse bullet list. Each bullet corresponds\n  one-to-one with the edits structure already documented in\n  `notes/chores-*.md` for this step — just the file and a\n  one-line gist (e.g. `README.md: new Overview intro`). Do *not*\n  restate the detail that lives in chores; the commit body is a\n  scan-able index, not a duplicate. The chores section is the\n  source of truth.\n- **Session notes** (optional tail, appended to the body): if the\n  session produced items worth preserving that don't fit the\n  code-change index — in-session tooling work, dead ends,\n  rationale — append a trailing subsection titled\n  `## <other-repo> session notes:` (e.g.\n  `## .claude session notes:`) with those items as bullets. The\n  same body (main content plus any session-notes subsection)\n  lands in both commits.\n- **`ochid` trailer**: do *not* include `ochid:` in the body you\n  pass via `--body`. `vc-x1 push` appends the correct per-repo\n  trailer at the commit stages\n  (`ochid: /.claude/<chid>` for the app-repo commit;\n  `ochid: /<chid>` for the `.claude` commit). When committing\n  manually, append the trailer yourself per the templates above.\n- Examples:\n  - `feat: add fix-ochid subcommand (0.22.0)`\n  - `fix: fix-ochid prefix bug (0.22.1)`\n  - `refactor: deduplicate common CLI flags (0.21.1)`\n\n### Chores section headers\n\nChores section headers use trailing version format:\n\n```\n## Description (X.Y.Z)\n```\n\nExample: `` ## Add `fn claude-symlink` (0.27.0) ``\n\n### Notes references\n\nMultiple references must be separated: `[2],[3]` not `[2,3]` or `[2][3]`.\nSee [Todo format](notes/README.md#todo-format) for details.\n\n### Markdown anchor links\n\nGitHub anchor algorithm: lowercase, strip non-alphanumeric\ncharacters in place, map remaining spaces to hyphens 1-for-1. Do\n**not** collapse adjacent whitespace — so `a + b` → `a--b` (spaces\non both sides of `+`), but `a: b` → `a-b` (only trailing space on\n`:`). General markdown reference:\n[markdownguide.org](https://www.markdownguide.org). GitHub\npublishes no official spec for auto-generated anchors; the\nde-facto reference implementation is\n[github-slugger](https://github.com/Flet/github-slugger).\n\n### ochid trailers\n\nEvery commit body must include an `ochid:` trailer pointing to the\ncounterpart commit in the other repo. The value is a workspace-root-relative\npath followed by the changeID:\n\n- App repo commits point to `.claude`: `ochid: /.claude/<changeID>`\n- Bot session commits point to app repo: `ochid: /<changeID>`\n\n`vc-x1 push` appends the correct trailer per repo automatically.\nFor manual commits, use `vc-x1 chid -R .,.claude -L` to get both\nchangeIDs (first line is app repo, second is `.claude`).\n\n## Code Conventions\n\n### Doc comments on every file, function, and method\n\nEvery `.rs` file must begin with a `//!` module docstring. Every\nfunction and method must have a `///` doc comment. Keep them brief —\none sentence of purpose is often enough; the discipline is that the\ncomment exists, not that it be long.\n\nThis is a deliberate override of the generic \"write no comments\"\ndefault that applies to inline `//` comments. Doc comments on the\nmodule / item surface are expected; inline explanatory comments\ninside function bodies remain discouraged unless they capture a\nnon-obvious WHY.\n\nFor longer doc comments, follow\n[Writing style: prefer sub-bullets](#writing-style-prefer-sub-bullets)\n— short intro then a bullet list, with the `verbatim_doc_comment`\ncaveat for clap-derive args.\n\n### `// OK: …` comments on `unwrap*` calls (Rust)\n\nNon-test code that calls `.unwrap()`, `.unwrap_or(…)`,\n`.unwrap_or_default()`, or `.unwrap_or_else(…)` must have a trailing\n`// OK: …` comment that justifies why the call is acceptable.\n\n- `// OK: <specific reason>` — document the real precondition,\n  invariant, or domain reason. Preferred whenever the reason isn't\n  self-evident.\n- `// OK: obvious` — the default is self-evident from context (e.g.\n  `desc.lines().next().unwrap_or(\"\")` — empty desc → empty title).\n\nBare `// OK` is not used (reads like a truncated comment).\nAbbreviations (e.g. `SE`) are not used because they require a decoder\nring for readers seeing the code out of context.\n\nFor provably-unreachable `.unwrap()` calls, also prefix with\n`#[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]` so the site stays silent if we enable\nthe project-wide `clippy::unwrap_used` lint later.\n\n```rust\nlet max = stderr_level.unwrap_or(LevelFilter::Info); // OK: default verbosity when -v/-vv absent\nlet first_line = desc.lines().next().unwrap_or(\"\");  // OK: obvious\n\nmatch matches.len() {\n    1 => {\n        #[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]\n        // OK: `1 =>` arm guarantees matches.len() == 1\n        Ok(TitleMatch::One(matches.into_iter().next().unwrap()))\n    }\n    // ...\n}\n```\n\nTests (`#[cfg(test)]`) are exempt — panicking on setup failure is the\ncorrect test behavior.\n\n### Ask for clarification on ambiguous input\n\nWhen user input is ambiguous or missing necessary detail, stop and\nask a specific question. Do not proceed on a guess and hope the\nresult lands right — a clarifying question costs a few seconds;\nredoing misaligned work costs much more.\n\n### Recognize when stuck\n\nIf a simple task has eaten 5+ minutes of thinking or back-and-forth\nwithout progress, stop. Summarize what's blocking — unclear\nrequirements, unfamiliar API surface, conflicting signals — and ask.\nContinued flailing produces worse outcomes than a direct \"I'm stuck\non X.\"\n\n## Workflow\n\nThe end-to-end flow for a step is: **edit → review → commit → push\n→ finalize**, executed via `vc-x1 push` with two interactive\napproval gates (review, message). Finalize is launched detached as\nthe absolute last action in the turn so trailing bot writes land in\nthe session repo.\n\n**Run this flow after every step** — not only at session end.\nSingle-step and multi-step changes are of equal importance: a\nsingle-step change is one `push` invocation; a multi-step change\nis one `push` per `X.Y.Z-N` commit plus one for the final release\ncommit. Each step gets its own commit, its own push, and its own\nfinalize — so dev markers land on the remote and in `.claude` as\nthey happen rather than being batched until the end.\n\n### User approval points\n\nNever execute commit, squash, push, or finalize commands without\nthe user's explicit approval. Present changes for review first;\nonly run them after the user confirms. This applies to late\nchanges too — pause for review before squashing into an existing\ncommit. The two approval gates surfaced by `vc-x1 push` (review,\nmessage) are part of this discipline, not a substitute for it.\n\n### Review before proposing the commit block\n\nAfter finishing a unit of work, **summarize what changed and stop\nthere**. Do not pre-emptively lay out the commit / push commands.\nWait for the user to signal review is complete before proposing\nthe commit block. Changes during review are the norm, not the\nexception; proposing commit text too early creates noise and\nsignals that I consider the work done when it usually isn't.\n\nThis applies per-step in a multi-step flow too — each step gets\na review pause before its commit block appears.\n\nSignals that review is complete include explicit approval (\"let's\ncommit\", \"looks good, commit it\") **and any directive to start the\nnext step** (\"do step 4\", \"next\", \"go N+1\"). In that case the\nprevious step must be committed first — always commit the current\nstep before starting the next; don't ask.\n\n### Versioning\n\nEvery plan must start with a version bump. Choose the approach based\non scope:\n\n- **Single-step** (recommended for mechanical/focused changes): bump\n  directly to `X.Y.Z`, implement in one commit. Simpler history.\n- **Multi-step** (for scope that splits naturally into\n  independently-reviewable steps): bump to `X.Y.Z-0`, implement\n  across multiple `X.Y.Z-N` commits incrementing the numeric\n  suffix. The final commit drops the suffix to close the ladder.\n\nThe plan should recommend one approach and get user approval before\nstarting.\n\nFor multi-step:\n\n1. Bump version to `X.Y.Z-0` with the plan and commit as a chore\n   marker.\n2. Implement in one or more `X.Y.Z-N` commits (increment N as\n   needed). Every `X.Y.Z-N` commit is a complete checkpoint in\n   its own right — the `-N` suffix only signals that more steps\n   in the same ladder are coming, not that the commit is partial\n   or exploratory. Run the full pre-commit checklist (including\n   `notes/todo.md` and `notes/chores-*.md` updates) on every\n   `-N` commit exactly as you would on a single-step release.\n3. Final commit bumps to `X.Y.Z` (no suffix) to close the ladder.\n\nMulti-step cycles surface the ladder at the top of\n`notes/todo.md > ## In Progress` as a bullet list with `(done)` /\n`(current)` markers — see the file's intro paragraph for the\nformat. Update the markers as each step ships so the In Progress\nview stays current at a glance.\n\n**Why numeric suffixes (`-0`, `-1`, …) rather than `-devN`:**\nsemver pre-release identifiers may consist of a single numeric\ncomponent, and they compare numerically per spec. So\n`X.Y.Z-1 < X.Y.Z-2 < … < X.Y.Z` correctly orders the ladder:\neach `-N` sorts before its final unsuffixed sibling. Cargo\naccepts this form. The `-dev` prefix adds no information the\ngit log doesn't already convey and doubles typing per commit.\n\nThe final release commit (no suffix) closes the ladder rather\nthan amending prior commits. This keeps history readable: a\nchain of complete checkpoints ending in an `X.Y.Z` marker.\n\n### Pre-commit checklist\n\nBefore proposing a commit, run all of the following and fix any issues:\n\n1. `cargo fmt`\n2. `cargo clippy`\n3. `cargo test`\n4. `cargo install --path . --locked` (if applicable) — `--locked`\n   is required: without it, `cargo install` ignores `Cargo.lock`\n   and re-resolves from scratch, which can pick incompatible\n   versions even when `cargo build` / `cargo test` succeed.\n5. Retest after install\n6. Update `notes/todo.md` — add to `## Done` if completing a task\n7. Update `notes/chores-*.md` — add a subsection describing the change\n8. Update `notes/README.md` — if functionality changed (new flags,\n   new subcommands, changed behavior)\n\nPush's preflight re-runs `vc-x1 sync` + `cargo fmt` +\n`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` + `cargo test` as a\nsafety net. Run the checklist above locally anyway — fmt / clippy /\ntest iteration is cheaper in-conversation than bouncing off\npreflight after review approval. Steps 4–5 (`cargo install --path .`\nand retest) are **not** in push's preflight (project-specific); the\nbot runs them.\n\n### Pre-step: `vc-x1 sync`\n\nPush's preflight runs `vc-x1 sync --check` as its first step. Check\nmode verifies divergence without applying — if anything is `behind`\nor `diverged`, preflight errors and you resolve explicitly with\n`vc-x1 sync --no-check` before re-running push. This keeps the\ntwo approval gates (review, message) authoritative; push never\nperforms an unsupervised rebase.\n\nRunning sync manually before you *start* editing is still cheap\n(one line when clean) and surfaces remote changes earlier:\n\n```\nvc-x1 sync --check                    # dual-repo workspace, verify\nvc-x1 sync --no-check                 # apply (rebase / fast-forward)\nvc-x1 sync --check -R .               # single-repo project\nvc-x1 sync --check --quiet            # silent; exit code signals result\n```\n\nBots and scripts must pass `--check` or `--no-check` explicitly —\ndefaults can shift, explicit flags lock in the contract. Interactive\nuse can take the default (which is `--check`).\n\nOutput shape:\n\n- **Clean**: one line — `sync: N repos, all bookmarks up-to-date`.\n  Note: scope is bookmark-vs-remote tracking, not working-copy\n  cleanliness — `@` may have uncommitted changes; sync doesn't\n  speak to that. Proceed.\n- **Action needed** (`behind` / `diverged`) under `--check`:\n  per-repo fetch + state lines, then a fatal\n  `sync: N repos need action — resolve with vc-x1 sync --no-check\n  and re-run`. Inspect, run `vc-x1 sync --no-check`, then proceed.\n- **`--quiet`**: no output; exit code is the only signal.\n\n### Run `vc-x1 push`\n\n**Prerequisites — one-time per repo:**\n\n- `.gitignore` must include `/.vc-x1` so push's in-progress\n  state files (`.vc-x1/push-state.toml`) don't get committed.\n  Push warns at preflight if the entry is missing.\n- The target bookmark must have a tracking remote\n  (`jj bookmark track <bookmark>@origin -R .`). `jj git fetch`\n  creates remote bookmarks as non-tracking by default; push\n  currently surfaces this as a raw jj error at `push-app` after\n  commits are locally made, so confirm tracking is set up\n  before the first push in a new clone.\n\n**`vc-x1 push <bookmark>` wraps the full flow in one command with\ntwo interactive approval gates.** Push runs preflight (sync + fmt\n+ clippy + test), prompts for review, composes the commit message\n(via `--title`/`--body` or `$EDITOR`), prompts for message\napproval, then commits both repos → advances bookmarks → pushes\napp → finalizes `.claude`. Failures inside the local mutation\nwindow roll both repos back via `jj op restore`; after `push-app`\nsucceeds the remote boundary is crossed and recovery is\nforward-only.\n\n```\nvc-x1 push main                                      # interactive (review + $EDITOR)\nvc-x1 push main --title \"...\" --body \"...\"           # flags skip $EDITOR\nvc-x1 push main --yes --title \"...\" --body \"...\"     # full non-interactive\nvc-x1 push main --dry-run                            # preview (no side effects)\nvc-x1 push main --from commit-app                    # resume from specific stage\nvc-x1 push --status                                  # show saved state\nvc-x1 push main --restart                            # clear saved state; start fresh\n```\n\nThe two approval gates are surfaced by push itself:\n\n1. **Review** — push prints `jj diff --stat` for both repos and\n   prompts `[y/N]`. Approve = \"the work is done right\".\n2. **Message** — push either uses `--title`/`--body` (non-editor\n   path) or opens `$EDITOR` on a template. Approve = \"the message\n   reads right\".\n\nBoth titles and bodies are the **same** across the two commits;\nper-repo `ochid:` trailers are appended by push itself. See\n[Commit message style](#commit-message-style) for body structure.\n\nFor the full flag list and stage machine, see `vc-x1 push --help`.\n\n### Bot communication during the flow\n\nWhen applying the flow on the user's behalf, use plain prose at\neach gate — no insider jargon (\"Gate N signal\", \"Checkpoint N\",\netc.):\n\n1. **After completing the work** — summarize what changed\n   (file-by-file or feature-by-feature, terse) and end with\n   something like:\n\n   > Work complete. Please review.
