Use\n`--ignore-immutable` to squash the changes into `@-` — the\nbookmark moves with the rewritten commit — then re-push:\n\n```\njj squash --ignore-immutable -R .\njj git push --bookmark <bookmark> -R .\n```\n\nIf you squash somewhere other than `@-`, add\n`jj bookmark set <bookmark> -r <target> -R .` between those\ntwo commands so the bookmark lands on the rewritten commit.\n\n`.claude` is also mutable via this pattern when needed, though\npush's `finalize-claude` stage normally handles trailing session\nwrites so you rarely hit this case there.\n\n### Finalize is the absolute last action\n\n`vc-x1 finalize` runs detached with `--squash` and a short\n`--delay` so any writes the bot makes immediately after launching\nfinalize still land in the squash window and end up in the\nsession-repo commit. **That guarantee depends on finalize being\nthe last thing in the turn.**\n\nAfter `vc-x1 finalize` is launched — **whether mid-session\nper-step or at session end** — you **MUST NEVER** proceed to a\nnext step, edit files, run tools, or emit any text (prose,\nrecaps, acknowledgements), until the user explicitly directs you\nto continue. Treat finalize as a hard stop for the whole turn.\nAny final words (e.g. \"next is ...\") must be said in the\napproval prompt *before* executing finalize; the finalize `Bash`\ncall is the last thing in the turn and nothing follows it.\n\nThis holds even when the next step seems obvious (e.g. \"next is\nN+1\" or \"now I should bump the version and commit the release\").\nWait. The user controls cadence — every push+finalize is a\ncheckpoint they may want to inspect, think about, hand off, or\ntake a break at. Auto-proceeding bypasses that checkpoint and\nproduces unwanted writes between finalize and the next explicit\ninstruction.\n\nDo **not** echo or restate the finalize output — the Bash tool\nalready displays it. Any trailing text creates writes that miss\nthe finalize squash window.\n\nExceptions to this rule may emerge later but are not authorized\nat this stage. Applies to:\n\n- `notes/chores-*.md`, `notes/todo.md`, committed READMEs, design notes.\n- Module `//!` docstrings, item `///` doc comments on traits / structs / functions / methods, and any other doc comment that runs more than a few sentences.\n\nShort intro sentences (1–3) at the top of a section / item are\nfine; detail goes into hierarchical bullet lists.\n\n**Why:** easier to scan and cross-reference during review;\nmatches how the user reads and edits committed reference\nmaterial. A wall of prose hides structure that a nested list\nmakes visible — and the same is true inside doc comments,\nwhere rustdoc renders the list cleanly.\n\n**How to apply:**\n\n- Default to bullet structure for any non-trivial section or\n  doc comment. Reserve paragraphs for brief intros and\n  occasional contextual framing.\n- If a paragraph runs past ~3 sentences, look for the implicit\n  list inside it and break it out.\n- Design-decision entries benefit most — the *reason* /\n  *what-was-rejected* / *how-it-applies* decomposition reads\n  naturally as sub-bullets.\n- Single-line doc comments on trivial methods stay one line —\n  bullets are not mandatory, just *available* when content is\n  long enough to warrant them.\n\n**Clap-derive args caveat.** Doc comments on `#[arg(...)]`\nfields drive `--help` output. Clap reflows by default and\ncollapses bullets into running prose. Add\n`#[arg(verbatim_doc_comment, ...)]` on any field whose doc\ncomment uses bullets so each `- …` lands on its own line in\nthe rendered help.\n\n## jj Basics\n\n- `jj st -R .` / `jj st -R .claude` — show working copy status\n- `jj log -R .` / `jj log -R .claude` — show commit log\n- `jj commit -m \"title\" -m \"body\" -R <repo>` — finalize working copy into a commit\n- `jj describe -m \"title\" -m \"body\" -R <repo>` — set description without committing\n- `jj git push --bookmark <name> -R <repo>` — push a bookmark (no\n  `--allow-new` flag; jj pushes new bookmarks without special flags)\n- In jj, the working copy (@) is always a mutable commit being edited.\n  `jj commit` finalizes it and creates a new empty working copy on top.\n- The `.claude` repo always has uncommitted changes during an active\n  session because session data updates continuously.\n\n## vc-x1 Basics\n\n`vc-x1` is the workspace tool that wraps jj operations across the\napp and bot session repos. Once installed, it should drive 99% of\nthe commit / push / finalize flow — direct `jj` is the fallback\nwhen something goes off-rails.\n\nSubcommands in current use:\n\n- `vc-x1 sync` — verify (or apply) bookmark divergence between\n  local and remote across all workspace repos. See\n  [Pre-step: `vc-x1 sync`](#pre-step-vc-x1-sync) below.\n- `vc-x1 push <bookmark>` — full commit + push + finalize flow\n  with two interactive approval gates. The primary command for\n  shipping a step. See [Run `vc-x1 push`](#run-vc-x1-push) below.\n- `vc-x1 finalize --repo <r> --squash --push <bookmark> --delay <s> --detach --log <path>`\n  — squash trailing session writes into the working commit and\n  push. Used by `vc-x1 push` internally; also available as a\n  manual fallback. See\n  [Manual finalize fallback](#manual-finalize-fallback) below.\n- `vc-x1 chid -R <r,...> -L` — print change IDs for the current\n  working commit in each repo, one per line. Used to compose\n  `ochid:` trailers when committing manually.\n- `vc-x1 fix-ochid` — repair a missing or stale `ochid:` trailer\n  in an existing commit.\n\nThe bot thinks the in-flight `--scope`, `--squash`, and\n`--message-file` flags on `vc-x1 push` are intended to replace\nthe current `--title` / `--body` flags with a richer message\nsource and a per-step scope selector; once shipped, they should\nbecome the default invocation. Until then, follow the flag set\ndocumented in [Run `vc-x1 push`](#run-vc-x1-push) below.\n\nFor the full command surface, run `vc-x1 --help` and\n`vc-x1 <subcommand> --help`.\n\n## Commits\n\n### Per-repo commit commands\n\nWhen committing manually (i.e. not via `vc-x1 push`), use `-R`\n(`--repository`) at the end to target the correct repo. Use\nrelative paths to reduce noise. Putting `-R` last keeps the\nverb/action visible at the start of the command.\n\n#### App repo\n```\njj commit -m \\\n\"title\" \\\n-m \"body\n\nochid: /.claude/<changeID>\" \\\n-R .\n```\n\n#### Bot session repo\n```\njj commit -m \\\n\"title\" \\\n-m \"body\n\nochid: /<changeID>\" \\\n-R .claude\n```\n\n### Commit message style\n\nUse [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) with\na version suffix:\n\n```\n<type>: <short description> (<version>)\n```\n\n- **Title**: target ~50 chars, short summary of *what* changed.\n  Include the version. Common types: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`,\n  `test`, `docs`, `chore`.\n- **Body** (same across both repos): short intro paragraph (1–3\n  sentences), then a terse bullet list. Each bullet corresponds\n  one-to-one with the edits structure already documented in\n  `notes/chores-*.md` for this step — just the file and a\n  one-line gist (e.g. `README.md: new Overview intro`). Do *not*\n  restate the detail that lives in chores; the commit body is a\n  scan-able index, not a duplicate. The chores section is the\n  source of truth.\n- **Session notes** (optional tail, appended to the body): if the\n  session produced items worth preserving that don't fit the\n  code-change index — in-session tooling work, dead ends,\n  rationale — append a trailing subsection titled\n  `## <other-repo> session notes:` (e.g.\n  `## .claude session notes:`) with those items as bullets. The\n  same body (main content plus any session-notes subsection)\n  lands in both commits.\n- **`ochid` trailer**: do *not* include `ochid:` in the body you\n  pass via `--body`. `vc-x1 push` appends the correct per-repo\n  trailer at the commit stages\n  (`ochid: /.claude/<chid>` for the app-repo commit;\n  `ochid: /<chid>` for the `.claude` commit). When committing\n  manually, append the trailer yourself per the templates above.\n- Examples:\n  - `feat: add fix-ochid subcommand (0.22.0)`\n  - `fix: fix-ochid prefix bug (0.22.1)`\n  - `refactor: deduplicate common CLI flags (0.21.1)`\n\n### Chores section headers\n\nChores section headers use trailing version format:\n\n```\n## Description (X.Y.Z)\n```\n\nExample: `` ## Add `fn claude-symlink` (0.27.0) ``\n\n### Notes references\n\nMultiple references must be separated: `[2],[3]` not `[2,3]` or `[2][3]`.\nSee [Todo format](notes/README.md#todo-format) for details.\n\n### Markdown anchor links\n\nGitHub anchor algorithm: lowercase, strip non-alphanumeric\ncharacters in place, map remaining spaces to hyphens 1-for-1. Do\n**not** collapse adjacent whitespace — so `a + b` → `a--b` (spaces\non both sides of `+`), but `a: b` → `a-b` (only trailing space on\n`:`). General markdown reference:\n[markdownguide.org](https://www.markdownguide.org). GitHub\npublishes no official spec for auto-generated anchors; the\nde-facto reference implementation is\n[github-slugger](https://github.com/Flet/github-slugger).\n\n### ochid trailers\n\nEvery commit body must include an `ochid:` trailer pointing to the\ncounterpart commit in the other repo. The value is a workspace-root-relative\npath followed by the changeID:\n\n- App repo commits point to `.claude`: `ochid: /.claude/<changeID>`\n- Bot session commits point to app repo: `ochid: /<changeID>`\n\n`vc-x1 push` appends the correct trailer per repo automatically.\nFor manual commits, use `vc-x1 chid -R .,.claude -L` to get both\nchangeIDs (first line is app repo, second is `.claude`).\n\n## Code Conventions\n\n### Doc comments on every file, function, and method\n\nEvery `.rs` file must begin with a `//!` module docstring. Every\nfunction and method must have a `///` doc comment. Keep them brief —\none sentence of purpose is often enough; the discipline is that the\ncomment exists, not that it be long.\n\nThis is a deliberate override of the generic \"write no comments\"\ndefault that applies to inline `//` comments. Doc comments on the\nmodule / item surface are expected; inline explanatory comments\ninside function bodies remain discouraged unless they capture a\nnon-obvious WHY.\n\nFor longer doc comments, follow\n[Writing style: prefer sub-bullets](#writing-style-prefer-sub-bullets)\n— short intro then a bullet list, with the `verbatim_doc_comment`\ncaveat for clap-derive args.\n\n### `// OK: …` comments on `unwrap*` calls (Rust)\n\nNon-test code that calls `.unwrap()`, `.unwrap_or(…)`,\n`.unwrap_or_default()`, or `.unwrap_or_else(…)` must have a trailing\n`// OK: …` comment that justifies why the call is acceptable.\n\n- `// OK: <specific reason>` — document the real precondition,\n  invariant, or domain reason. Preferred whenever the reason isn't\n  self-evident.\n- `// OK: obvious` — the default is self-evident from context (e.g.\n  `desc.lines().next().unwrap_or(\"\")` — empty desc → empty title).\n\nBare `// OK` is not used (reads like a truncated comment).\nAbbreviations (e.g. `SE`) are not used because they require a decoder\nring for readers seeing the code out of context.\n\nFor provably-unreachable `.unwrap()` calls, also prefix with\n`#[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]` so the site stays silent if we enable\nthe project-wide `clippy::unwrap_used` lint later.\n\n```rust\nlet max = stderr_level.unwrap_or(LevelFilter::Info); // OK: default verbosity when -v/-vv absent\nlet first_line = desc.lines().next().unwrap_or(\"\");  // OK: obvious\n\nmatch matches.len() {\n    1 => {\n        #[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]\n        // OK: `1 =>` arm guarantees matches.len() == 1\n        Ok(TitleMatch::One(matches.into_iter().next().unwrap()))\n    }\n    // ...\n}\n```\n\nTests (`#[cfg(test)]`) are exempt — panicking on setup failure is the\ncorrect test behavior.\n\n### Ask for clarification on ambiguous input\n\nWhen user input is ambiguous or missing necessary detail, stop and\nask a specific question. Do not proceed on a guess and hope the\nresult lands right — a clarifying question costs a few seconds;\nredoing misaligned work costs much more.\n\n### Recognize when stuck\n\nIf a simple task has eaten 5+ minutes of thinking or back-and-forth\nwithout progress, stop. Summarize what's blocking — unclear\nrequirements, unfamiliar API surface, conflicting signals — and ask.\nContinued flailing produces worse outcomes than a direct \"I'm stuck\non X.\"\n\n## Workflow\n\nThe end-to-end flow for a step is: **edit → review → commit → push\n→ finalize**, executed via `vc-x1 push` with two interactive\napproval gates (review, message). Finalize is launched detached as\nthe absolute last action in the turn so trailing bot writes land in\nthe session repo.\n\n**Run this flow after every step** — not only at session end.\nSingle-step and multi-step changes are of equal importance: a\nsingle-step change is one `push` invocation; a multi-step change\nis one `push` per `X.Y.Z-N` commit plus one for the final release\ncommit. Each step gets its own commit, its own push, and its own\nfinalize — so dev markers land on the remote and in `.claude` as\nthey happen rather than being batched until the end.\n\n### User approval points\n\nNever execute commit, squash, push, or finalize commands without\nthe user's explicit approval. Present changes for review first;\nonly run them after the user confirms. This applies to late\nchanges too — pause for review before squashing into an existing\ncommit. The two approval gates surfaced by `vc-x1 push` (review,\nmessage) are part of this discipline, not a substitute for it.\n\n### Review before proposing the commit block\n\nAfter finishing a unit of work, **summarize what changed and stop\nthere**. Do not pre-emptively lay out the commit / push commands.\nWait for the user to signal review is complete before proposing\nthe commit block. Changes during review are the norm, not the\nexception; proposing commit text too early creates noise and\nsignals that I consider the work done when it usually isn't.\n\nThis applies per-step in a multi-step flow too — each step gets\na review pause before its commit block appears.\n\nSignals that review is complete include explicit approval (\"let's\ncommit\", \"looks good, commit it\") **and any directive to start the\nnext step** (\"do step 4\", \"next\", \"go N+1\"). In that case the\nprevious step must be committed first — always commit the current\nstep before starting the next; don't ask.\n\n### Versioning\n\nEvery plan must start with a version bump. Choose the approach based\non scope:\n\n- **Single-step** (recommended for mechanical/focused changes): bump\n  directly to `X.Y.Z`, implement in one commit. Simpler history.\n- **Multi-step** (for scope that splits naturally into\n  independently-reviewable steps): bump to `X.Y.Z-0`, implement\n  across multiple `X.Y.Z-N` commits incrementing the numeric\n  suffix. The final commit drops the suffix to close the ladder.\n\nThe plan should recommend one approach and get user approval before\nstarting.\n\nFor multi-step:\n\n1. Bump version to `X.Y.Z-0` with the plan and commit as a chore\n   marker.\n2. Implement in one or more `X.Y.Z-N` commits (increment N as\n   needed). Every `X.Y.Z-N` commit is a complete checkpoint in\n   its own right — the `-N` suffix only signals that more steps\n   in the same ladder are coming, not that the commit is partial\n   or exploratory. Run the full pre-commit checklist (including\n   `notes/todo.md` and `notes/chores-*.md` updates) on every\n   `-N` commit exactly as you would on a single-step release.\n3. Final commit bumps to `X.Y.Z` (no suffix) to close the ladder.\n\nMulti-step cycles surface the ladder at the top of\n`notes/todo.md > ## In Progress` as a bullet list with `(done)` /\n`(current)` markers — see the file's intro paragraph for the\nformat. Update the markers as each step ships so the In Progress\nview stays current at a glance.\n\n**Why numeric suffixes (`-0`, `-1`, …) rather than `-devN`:**\nsemver pre-release identifiers may consist of a single numeric\ncomponent, and they compare numerically per spec. So\n`X.Y.Z-1 < X.Y.Z-2 < … < X.Y.Z` correctly orders the ladder:\neach `-N` sorts before its final unsuffixed sibling. Cargo\naccepts this form. The `-dev` prefix adds no information the\ngit log doesn't already convey and doubles typing per commit.\n\nThe final release commit (no suffix) closes the ladder rather\nthan amending prior commits. This keeps history readable: a\nchain of complete checkpoints ending in an `X.Y.Z` marker.\n\n### Pre-commit checklist\n\nBefore proposing a commit, run all of the following and fix any issues:\n\n1. `cargo fmt`\n2. `cargo clippy`\n3. `cargo test`\n4. `cargo install --path . --locked` (if applicable) — `--locked`\n   is required: without it, `cargo install` ignores `Cargo.lock`\n   and re-resolves from scratch, which can pick incompatible\n   versions even when `cargo build` / `cargo test` succeed.\n5. Retest after install\n6. Update `notes/todo.md` — add to `## Done` if completing a task\n7. Update `notes/chores-*.md` — add a subsection describing the change\n8. Update `notes/README.md` — if functionality changed (new flags,\n   new subcommands, changed behavior)\n\nPush's preflight re-runs `vc-x1 sync` + `cargo fmt` +\n`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` + `cargo test` as a\nsafety net. Run the checklist above locally anyway — fmt / clippy /\ntest iteration is cheaper in-conversation than bouncing off\npreflight after review approval. Steps 4–5 (`cargo install --path .`\nand retest) are **not** in push's preflight (project-specific); the\nbot runs them.\n\n### Pre-step: `vc-x1 sync`\n\nPush's preflight runs `vc-x1 sync --check` as its first step. Check\nmode verifies divergence without applying — if anything is `behind`\nor `diverged`, preflight errors and you resolve explicitly with\n`vc-x1 sync --no-check` before re-running push. This keeps the\ntwo approval gates (review, message) authoritative; push never\nperforms an unsupervised rebase.\n\nRunning sync manually before you *start* editing is still cheap\n(one line when clean) and surfaces remote changes earlier:\n\n```\nvc-x1 sync --check                    # dual-repo workspace, verify\nvc-x1 sync --no-check                 # apply (rebase / fast-forward)\nvc-x1 sync --check -R .               # single-repo project\nvc-x1 sync --check --quiet            # silent; exit code signals result\n```\n\nBots and scripts must pass `--check` or `--no-check` explicitly —\ndefaults can shift, explicit flags lock in the contract. Interactive\nuse can take the default (which is `--check`).\n\nOutput shape:\n\n- **Clean**: one line — `sync: N repos, all bookmarks up-to-date`.\n  Note: scope is bookmark-vs-remote tracking, not working-copy\n  cleanliness — `@` may have uncommitted changes; sync doesn't\n  speak to that. Proceed.\n- **Action needed** (`behind` / `diverged`) under `--check`:\n  per-repo fetch + state lines, then a fatal\n  `sync: N repos need action — resolve with vc-x1 sync --no-check\n  and re-run`. Inspect, run `vc-x1 sync --no-check`, then proceed.\n- **`--quiet`**: no output; exit code is the only signal.\n\n### Run `vc-x1 push`\n\n**Prerequisites — one-time per repo:**\n\n- `.gitignore` must include `/.vc-x1` so push's in-progress\n  state files (`.vc-x1/push-state.toml`) don't get committed.\n  Push warns at preflight if the entry is missing.\n- The target bookmark must have a tracking remote\n  (`jj bookmark track <bookmark>@origin -R .`). `jj git fetch`\n  creates remote bookmarks as non-tracking by default; push\n  currently surfaces this as a raw jj error at `push-app` after\n  commits are locally made, so confirm tracking is set up\n  before the first push in a new clone.\n\n**`vc-x1 push <bookmark>` wraps the full flow in one command with\ntwo interactive approval gates.** Push runs preflight (sync + fmt\n+ clippy + test), prompts for review, composes the commit message\n(via `--title`/`--body` or `$EDITOR`), prompts for message\napproval, then commits both repos → advances bookmarks → pushes\napp → finalizes `.claude`. Failures inside the local mutation\nwindow roll both repos back via `jj op restore`; after `push-app`\nsucceeds the remote boundary is crossed and recovery is\nforward-only.\n\n```\nvc-x1 push main                                      # interactive (review + $EDITOR)\nvc-x1 push main --title \"...\" --body \"...\"           # flags skip $EDITOR\nvc-x1 push main --yes --title \"...\" --body \"...\"     # full non-interactive\nvc-x1 push main --dry-run                            # preview (no side effects)\nvc-x1 push main --from commit-app                    # resume from specific stage\nvc-x1 push --status                                  # show saved state\nvc-x1 push main --restart                            # clear saved state; start fresh\n```\n\nThe two approval gates are surfaced by push itself:\n\n1. **Review** — push prints `jj diff --stat` for both repos and\n   prompts `[y/N]`. Approve = \"the work is done right\".\n2. **Message** — push either uses `--title`/`--body` (non-editor\n   path) or opens `$EDITOR` on a template. Approve = \"the message\n   reads right\".\n\nBoth titles and bodies are the **same** across the two commits;\nper-repo `ochid:` trailers are appended by push itself. See\n[Commit message style](#commit-message-style) for body structure.\n\nFor the full flag list and stage machine, see `vc-x1 push --help`.\n\n### Bot communication during the flow\n\nWhen applying the flow on the user's behalf, use plain prose at\neach gate — no insider jargon (\"Gate N signal\", \"Checkpoint N\",\netc.):\n\n1. **After completing the work** — summarize what changed\n   (file-by-file or feature-by-feature, terse) and end with\n   something like:\n\n   > Work complete. Please review. On approval I'll prep the\n   > commit title and body for a second approval before pushing.\n\n2. **After review approval** — present the proposed `$TITLE` and\n   `$BODY` explicitly, then ask permission to run `vc-x1 push`.\n   Do **not** spell out the full\n   `vc-x1 push <bookmark> --yes --title \"$TITLE\" --body \"$BODY\"`\n   invocation by default — it's mechanical and obvious from the\n   title/body. Show it only on explicit request (verbose mode /\n   debugging).\n\n3. **After execution approval** — run the push command. `push`\n   handles commit + bookmark + push + finalize internally;\n   nothing should be output after the push command (finalize is\n   detached and absolute-last; see\n   [Finalize is the absolute last action](#finalize-is-the-absolute-last-action)\n   below).\n\n### Late changes after push\n\nIf the app repo needs a tweak after `push-app` succeeded (e.g.\nupdating CLAUDE.md or memory), the commit is immutable. Use\n`--ignore-immutable` to squash the changes into `@-` — the\nbookmark moves with the rewritten commit — then re-push:\n\n```\njj squash --ignore-immutable -R .\njj git push --bookmark <bookmark> -R .\n```\n\nIf you squash somewhere other than `@-`, add\n`jj bookmark set <bookmark> -r <target> -R .` between those\ntwo commands so the bookmark lands on the rewritten commit.\n\n`.claude` is also mutable via this pattern when needed, though\npush's `finalize-claude` stage normally handles trailing session\nwrites so you rarely hit this case there.\n\n### Finalize is the absolute last action\n\n`vc-x1 finalize` runs detached with `--squash` and a short\n`--delay` so any writes the bot makes immediately after launching\nfinalize still land in the squash window and end up in the\nsession-repo commit. **That guarantee depends on finalize being\nthe last thing in the turn.**\n\nAfter `vc-x1 finalize` is launched — **whether mid-session\nper-step or at session end** — you **MUST NEVER** proceed to a\nnext step, edit files, run tools, or emit any text (prose,\nrecaps, acknowledgements), until the user explicitly directs you\nto continue. Treat finalize as a hard stop for the whole turn.\nAny final words (e.g. \"next is ...\") must be said in the\napproval prompt *before* executing finalize; the finalize `Bash`\ncall is the last thing in the turn and nothing follows it.\n\nThis holds even when the next step seems obvious (e.g. \"next is\nN+1\" or \"now I should bump the version and commit the release\").\nWait. The user controls cadence — every push+finalize is a\ncheckpoint they may want to inspect, think about, hand off, or\ntake a break at. Auto-proceeding bypasses that checkpoint and\nproduces unwanted writes between finalize and the next explicit\ninstruction.\n\nDo **not** echo or restate the finalize output — the Bash tool\nalready displays it. Any trailing text creates writes that miss\nthe finalize squash window.\n\nExceptions to this rule may emerge later but are not authorized\nat this stage. Until told otherwise, treat as absolute.\n\n### Manual finalize fallback\n\nIf push exited before `finalize-claude` (e.g. `--no-finalize`\nwas set, or a failure between `push-app` and `finalize-claude`),\nrun finalize by hand:\n\n```\nvc-x1 finalize --repo .claude --squash --push <bookmark> --delay 10 --detach --log /tmp/vc-x1-finalize.log\n```\n\nThe same \"finalize is the absolute last action\" rule applies —\nnothing should happen after finalize. If any work is done after\nfinalize, run finalize again so the trailing writes are captured.\n\n**Clear push's saved state after any out-of-band recovery** —\nmanual `vc-x1 finalize`, manual `jj squash --ignore-immutable`\n+ force-push, etc., all leave `.vc-x1/push-state.toml` pointing\nat a now-stale halt point. Either `rm .vc-x1/push-state.toml`\nor run `vc-x1 push <bookmark> --restart` (which clears and\nrestarts in one go) before the next `vc-x1 push`. Otherwise\npush resumes from a bogus stage and can falsely declare\nsuccess.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":15,"oldLines":6,"newStart":15,"newLines":12,"lines":[" - Bot session repo: `.claude`","   (symlink from `~/.claude/projects/<path-to-project-root>/.claude`)"," ","+The bot session repo is this project's **`other-repo`** — the","+path is set by `[workspace].other-repo` in `.vc-config.toml`","+(default `.claude`, as used here). Concrete examples below use\n21\t`.claude` for readability; treat the path as configurable where\n22\tit appears in prose.\n23\t\n24\t## Working Directory\n25\t\n26\tPrefer staying in the project root. Use `-R` flags or absolute paths\n27\tto target other directories rather than `cd`. If `cd` seems necessary,\n28\tdiscuss with the user first — losing track of cwd causes subtle\n29\tcommand failures downstream.\n30\t\n31\tWhen invoking shell commands, prefer the shortest unambiguous path —\n32\tusually relative to cwd (`ls notes/`, not\n33\t`ls /home/wink/data/prgs/rust/vc-template-x1/notes/`). Long absolute\n34\tpaths clutter the transcript without adding information. Out-of-workspace\n35\tpaths (`/tmp/...`, `~/.config/...`) stay absolute. Read/Edit/Write\n36\ttool args also stay absolute — that's a tool-boundary constraint,\n37\tnot a stylistic choice.\n38\t\n39\t## Memory\n40\t\n41\tDo not use the bot's per-project memory directory\n42\t(`~/.claude/projects/<path>/memory/`). In a dual-repo setup with\n43\tCLAUDE.md it provides no capability CLAUDE.md doesn't already cover,\n44\tand it loses on discoverability:\n45\t\n46\t- **CLAUDE.md** — at the repo root, a well-known location for bot\n47\t  instructions, committed, reviewable, visible to every collaborator\n48\t  (human or bot).\n49\t- **Memory directory** — hidden under the user's home, tied to one\n50\t  machine, invisible to anyone but the bot, never diffed or reviewed.\n51\t\n52\tEasy for everyone to find beats convenient for the bot alone. Put\n53\tdurable context in CLAUDE.md (or committed `notes/`) instead.\n54\t\n55\t## Speculation marker\n56\t\n57\tDurable text the bot writes — CLAUDE.md, `notes/`, commit bodies,\n58\tchores sections — should stick to observations and direct descriptions\n59\tof the code or data. If a mechanism, hypothesis, or causal claim\n60\tenters the text, prefix it with \"The bot thinks ...\" so a reader can\n61\ttell the measured from the inferred.\n62\t\n63\t**Why:** unmarked speculation reads like evidence, and a future reader\n64\t(or the bot on a later session) can pick it up as a known fact when\n65\tit's not. Measured / inferred is a distinction worth keeping visible\n66\tin the written record.\n67\t\n68\t**How to apply:** observations and factual descriptions need no\n69\tmarker. Prefix with \"The bot thinks ...\" (or a close variant like\n70\t\"The bot's guess is ...\") when the claim is a mechanism (\"X wins\n71\tbecause Y caches better\"), a cause (\"the drift was due to thermal\n72\tstate\"), a prediction (\"this should scale linearly\"), or any\n73\treasoning not directly supported by the data on hand.\n74\t\n75\t## Writing style: prefer sub-bullets\n76\t\n77\tDurable text the bot writes should itemize with sub-bullets\n78\trather than run as large prose paragraphs. Applies to:\n79\t\n80\t- `notes/chores-*.md`, `notes/todo.md`, committed READMEs, design notes.\n81\t- Module `//!` docstrings, item `///` doc comments on traits / structs / functions / methods, and any other doc comment that runs more than a few sentences.\n82\t\n83\tShort intro sentences (1–3) at the top of a section / item are\n84\tfine; detail goes into hierarchical bullet lists.\n85\t\n86\t**Why:** easier to scan and cross-reference during review;\n87\tmatches how the user reads and edits committed reference\n88\tmaterial. A wall of prose hides structure that a nested list\n89\tmakes visible — and the same is true inside doc comments,\n90\twhere rustdoc renders the list cleanly.\n91\t\n92\t**How to apply:**\n93\t\n94\t- Default to bullet structure for any non-trivial section or\n95\t  doc comment. Reserve paragraphs for brief intros and\n96\t  occasional contextual framing.\n97\t- If a paragraph runs past ~3 sentences, look for the implicit\n98\t  list inside it and break it out.\n99\t- Design-decision entries benefit most — the *reason* /\n100\t  *what-was-rejected* / *how-it-applies* decomposition reads\n101\t  naturally as sub-bullets.\n102\t- Single-line doc comments on trivial methods stay one line —\n103\t  bullets are not mandatory, just *available* when content is\n104\t  long enough to warrant them.\n105\t\n106\t**Clap-derive args caveat.** Doc comments on `#[arg(...)]`\n107\tfields drive `--help` output. Clap reflows by default and\n108\tcollapses bullets into running prose. Add\n109\t`#[arg(verbatim_doc_comment, ...)]` on any field whose doc\n110\tcomment uses bullets so each `- …` lands on its own line in\n111\tthe rendered help.\n112\t\n113\t## jj Basics\n114\t\n115\t- `jj st -R .` / `jj st -R .claude` — show working copy status\n116\t- `jj log -R .` / `jj log -R .claude` — show commit log\n117\t- `jj commit -m \"title\" -m \"body\" -R <repo>` — finalize working copy into a commit\n118\t- `jj describe -m \"title\" -m \"body\" -R <repo>` — set description without committing\n119\t- `jj git push --bookmark <name> -R <repo>` — push a bookmark (no\n120\t  `--allow-new` flag; jj pushes new bookmarks without special flags)\n121\t- In jj, the working copy (@) is always a mutable commit being edited.\n122\t  `jj commit` finalizes it and creates a new empty working copy on top.\n123\t- The `.claude` repo always has uncommitted changes during an active\n124\t  session because session data updates continuously.\n125\t\n126\t## vc-x1 Basics\n127\t\n128\t`vc-x1` is the workspace tool that wraps jj operations across the\n129\tapp and bot session repos. Once installed, it should drive 99% of\n130\tthe commit / push / finalize flow — direct `jj` is the fallback\n131\twhen something goes off-rails.\n132\t\n133\tSubcommands in current use:\n134\t\n135\t- `vc-x1 sync` — verify (or apply) bookmark divergence between\n136\t  local and remote across all workspace repos. See\n137\t  [Pre-step: `vc-x1 sync`](#pre-step-vc-x1-sync) below.\n138\t- `vc-x1 push <bookmark>` — full commit + push + finalize flow\n139\t  with two interactive approval gates. The primary command for\n140\t  shipping a step. See [Run `vc-x1 push`](#run-vc-x1-push) below.\n141\t- `vc-x1 finalize --repo <r> --squash --push <bookmark> --delay <s> --detach --log <path>`\n142\t  — squash trailing session writes into the working commit and\n143\t  push. Used by `vc-x1 push` internally; also available as a\n144\t  manual fallback. See\n145\t  [Manual finalize fallback](#manual-finalize-fallback) below.\n146\t- `vc-x1 chid -R <r,...> -L` — print change IDs for the current\n147\t  working commit in each repo, one per line. Used to compose\n148\t  `ochid:` trailers when committing manually.\n149\t- `vc-x1 fix-ochid` — repair a missing or stale `ochid:` trailer\n150\t  in an existing commit.\n151\t\n152\tThe bot thinks the in-flight `--scope`, `--squash`, and\n153\t`--message-file` flags on `vc-x1 push` are intended to replace\n154\tthe current `--title` / `--body` flags with a richer message\n155\tsource and a per-step scope selector; once shipped, they should\n156\tbecome the default invocation. broken) graph.\n\n## Workaround\n\n`cargo install --path . --locked`. Cargo has **no stable config\nkey or env var** to make `--locked` the default for\n`cargo install`. Verified against the [cargo config\nreference](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html):\n`[install]` only controls the install root directory; nothing\ntoggles lockfile behavior.\n\nThe discipline therefore lives in the project's pre-commit\nchecklist (CLAUDE.md step 4) and in shell aliases\n(e.g. `alias ci='cargo install --locked'`).\n\n## Upstream tracking — cargo issues\n\nCanonical:\n\n- [#7169 — \"`cargo install` apparently ignores `Cargo.lock` as opposed to `cargo build`\"](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/7169) —\n  the original report (2019). Plain\n52\t`cargo install` ignores `Cargo.lock` and re-resolves dependencies\n53\tfrom scratch, so it can silently produce a binary built from a\n54\tdifferent (and possibly broken) dependency graph than `cargo build`\n55\t/ `cargo test` ran against. There is no stable cargo config knob\n56\tto make `--locked` the default for `cargo install`, so the\n57\tdiscipline lives in the project's pre-commit checklist and shell\n58\taliases.\n59\t\n60\tThe trade-off is predictable-as-tested (`--locked`) vs picking up\n61\tupstream security/bug fixes via fresh resolves (default). Either\n62\tis defensible — pick what fits your project, then edit this\n63\tsection and CLAUDE.md's pre-commit step 6 to match.\n64\t\n65\tFull background, repro details, and upstream cargo-issue It\n4\tcontains instructions on how a commit cycle is accomplished.\n5\t\n6\t## Cycles\n7\t\n8\tA cycle has three phases:\n9\t\n10\t- **[Preparation](#preparation)** (`X.Y.Z-0`) — the cycle's\n11\t  first commit. Sets up the cycle:\n12\t  - Backfill the previous cycle's chores `Commits:` ref.\n13\t  - Bump `Cargo.toml` to `X.Y.Z-0`.\n14\t  - Pick up a `## Todo` item (typically the top-ranked,\n15\t    #1) into `## In Progress` (bold title + succinct problem\n16\t    statement + plan ladder).\n17\t  - Open the [chores section](#chores-sections).\n18\t- **[Work-N](#work-n)** (`X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, …) — the\n19\t  commits that implement the change. As many as the change\n20\t  needs; each runs through the\n21\t  [per-commit flow](#per-commit-flow).\n22\t- **[Close-out](#close-out)** (bare `X.Y.Z`) — the cycle's\n23\t  last commit. Bookkeeping only:\n24\t  - Move the picked-up item to a one-line entry in\n25\t    `## Done`.\n26\t  - Move the `## In Progress` block into the\n27\t    [chores section](#chores-sections).\n28\t  - Optionally update `notes/README.md` if functionality\n29\t    changed.\n30\t\n31\tA cycle's commits are published to the project remote\n32\teither incrementally or as one batch at close-out; the\n33\tresult must always be published at close-out. See\n34\t[Pushing](#pushing).\n35\t\n36\t**Sub-cycles.** When a Work commit's scope grows enough to\n37\twarrant its own ladder, it subdivides — `X.Y.Z-3.0`\n38\tPreparation, `X.Y.Z-3.1` / `X.Y.Z-3.2` Work, `X.Y.Z-3`\n39\tClose-out. The same three-phase shape applies recursively\n40\tat every depth. See [Numbering](#numbering) for the\n41\tsuffix rule and [Sub-cycle ladders](#sub-cycle-ladders)\n42\tfor the local-ladder mechanics.\n43\t\n44\t## Chores sections\n45\t\n46\tA **chores section** is a `##` section in\n47\t`notes/chores/chores-NN.md` recording one cycle:\n48\t\n49\t- One section per cycle is the default.\n50\t- Per-commit sections (one section per commit) are a\n51\t  deliberate alternative.\n52\t\n53\tThe phrase **\"Open\" the chores section** means append a\n54\t`##` header to the current `notes/chores/chores-NN.md`\n55\twith the cycle's anticipated close-out title (e.g.\n56\t`## refactor: foo bar (X.Y.Z)`). The body is empty;\n57\tcontent arrives at close-out (see [Close-out](#close-out)).\n58\t\n59\tFuller chores conventions (content rules, header sync,\n60\tdesign subsection pattern, `Commits:` formatting) live in\n61\tAGENTS.md [Chores conventions](../AGENTS.md#chores-conventions).\n62\t\n63\t## Preparation\n64\t\n65\tThe cycle's first commit (`X.Y.Z-0`):\n66\t\n67\t- **Backfill the previous cycle's chores section\n68\t  `Commits:` ref** — see\n69\t  [Chores commit references](../AGENTS.md#chores-commit-references).\n70\t- **Bump the version** in `Cargo.toml` to `X.Y.Z-0`.\n71\t- **Update `Cargo.lock`** to match — run `cargo build`\n72\t  (or `cargo check`) so the lockfile's `vc-x1` version\n73\t  tracks `Cargo.toml` in the same commit.\n74\t- **Move a `## Todo` item** (if the cycle has one) into\n75\t  `## In Progress` and the todo item should have:\n76\t  - A **bold title line** — that will be the chores\n77\t    section header, minus the `## ` prefix.\n78\t  - A **succinct problem statement**; add if one is needed\n79\t  - A **plan ladder**.\n80\t- **Open the [chores section](#chores-sections)** —\n81\t  append a `##` header with the cycle's anticipated\n82\t  close-out title.\n83\t\n84\t## Work-N\n85\t\n86\tThe cycle's work commits (`X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, …)\n87\timplement the change. As many as needed:\n88\t\n89\t- Each commit runs through the\n90\t  **[per-commit flow](#per-commit-flow)**.\n91\t- **Interim pushes** are optional (backup, progress\n92\t  visibility).\n93\t- Close-out is the only mandatory push (see\n94\t  [Pushing](#pushing)).\n95\t- **Subdivide into a sub-cycle** if a Work commit's\n96\t  scope grows enough (see\n97\t  [Sub-cycle ladders](#sub-cycle-ladders)).\n98\t\n99\t## Close-out\n100\t\n101\tThe cycle's last commit (bare `X.Y.Z`) does bookkeeping\n102\tonly — the commit body describes that bookkeeping, not\n103\twhat happens post-squash:\n104\t\n105\t- **Move the picked-up item** from `## In Progress` to a\n106\t  one-line entry (with a chores `[N]` ref) in `## Done`.\n107\t- **Move the `## In Progress` block into the\n108\t  [chores section](#chores-sections)** (the title-only\n109\t  placeholder opened during Preparation):\n110\t  - Cut the problem statement + plan ladder out of\n111\t    `## In Progress` (drop the bold title line — the\n112\t    chores `##` header already carries that string).\n113\t  - Paste under the chores `##` header.\n114\t  - Sync the chores header to the **final** commit title\n115\t    if the cycle's scope shifted; update every anchor\n116\t    back-reference.\n117\t  - Add an `### As-built ladder` listing the cycle's\n118\t    commits; optional `### Outcome` notes.\n119\t  - Replace `## In Progress` with\n120\t    `_No cycle currently in progress._`.\n121\t- **Update `notes/README.md`** if functionality changed\n122\t  (new flags, new subcommands, changed behavior).\n123\t\n124\tWhether to **squash** the cycle into one commit before the\n125\tpublishing push, or push as-is, is decided at push time —\n126\tsee [Pushing](#pushing).\n127\t\n128\t## Numbering\n129\t\n130\tThe version suffix on each commit encodes its phase —\n131\tthe **final identifier `0` marks a Preparation**:\n132\t\n133\t- `X.Y.Z-0` — Preparation\n134\t- `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, … — Work commits\n135\t- `X.Y.Z` — Close-out (bare version, no suffix)\n136\t\n137\tDisambiguation:\n138\t\n139\t- `-10` — Work commit #10 (final identifier `10`), not a\n140\t  Preparation.\n141\t- `-1.0` — Preparation of the `-1` sub-cycle (final\n142\t  identifier `0`).\n143\t\n144\t**Nesting.** Sub-cycles append another level, recursively:\n145\t\n146\t- `X.Y.Z-3.0` — Preparation of the `-3` sub-cycle\n147\t- `X.Y.Z-3.1`, `X.Y.Z-3.2` — its Work\n148\t- `X.Y.Z-3` — its Close-out\n149\t- `X.Y.Z-3.1.0` — Preparation of the `-3.1` sub-sub-cycle\n150\t\n151\tSub-cycles needing no Preparation omit `.0` (`-3.1`,\n152\t`-3.2`, `-3`); one that grows a Preparation later adds\n153\t`-3.0` without renumbering siblings.\n154\t\n155\tBump `Cargo.toml` at the start of each phase so `vc-x1 -V`\n156\treports the active phase at build time.\n157\t\n158\t## Per-commit flow\n159\t\n160\tEvery commit (Preparation, each Work commit, Close-out) goes\n161\tthrough:\n162\t\n163\t1. **Mark this commit `(current)`** as the first edit in\n164\t   `notes/todo.md > ## In Progress`.\n165\t2. **Do the work** (see [Iterative work](#iterative-work)\n166\t   for the loop-and-squash technique).\n167\t3. **Flip this commit `(current)` → `(done)`** in `## In\n168\t   Progress` — before the cargo cycle and the commit.\n169\t4. **Cargo cycle** (skip-able for purely-docs commits; full\n170\t   cycle mandatory at close-out):\n171\t   1. `cargo fmt`\n172\t   2. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`\n173\t   3. `cargo test`\n174\t   4. `cargo install --path . --locked`\n175\t   5. (re-test if anything substantive changed)\n176\t5. **Work review.** Stop *before* writing any description;\n177\t   tell the user \"ready to commit.\" The user reviews the\n178\t   changes and we iterate until complete.\n179\t6. **Write the commit description** — see\n180\t   [Commit description](#commit-description).\n181\t7. **Commit Description review.** Show the title + body\n182\t   and stop. The user reviews the description. Iterate.\n183\t8. **Commit.** `jj commit -m \"title\" -m \"body\" -R .` for\n184\t   the app repo, `-R .claude` for the bot repo (`-R` last\n185\t   keeps the verb visible):\n186\t\n187\t   ```\n188\t   jj commit -m \\\n189\t   \"<type>: <short description> (<version>)\" \\\n190\t   -m \"<intro paragraph>\n191\t\n192\t   - file1: gist\n193\t   - file2: gist\n194\t\n195\t   ochid: /.claude/<chid>\" \\\n196\t   -R .\n197\t   ```\n198\t\n199\t**Two overrides apply:**\n200\t\n201\t- **Deviation or question** — any time the work deviates\n202\t  from the agreed plan, or a question arises, stop and\n203\t  surface it; don't push through.\n204\t- **ESC-ESC** — the user can interrupt at any point to pull\n205\t  a review or question forward.\n206\t\n207\t## Commit description\n208\t\n209\t[Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)\n210\twith a version suffix:\n211\t\n212\t```\n213\t<type>: <short description> (<version>)\n214\t```\n215\t\n216\t### Title\n217\t\n218\t- ≤50 chars total (version suffix counts).\n219\t- Common types: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `test`,\n220\t  `docs`, `chore`.\n221\t- Favor terse phrasings.\n222\t\n223\t### Body\n224\t\n225\t[Prose form](../AGENTS.md#prose-form) (intro + bullets),\n226\twrap ≤72. Bullet content differs per repo:\n227\t\n228\t- **App-repo body**: file-by-file. One bullet per file\n229\t  changed (file plus a one-line gist). Sub-bullets for\n230\t  files with multiple distinct changes:\n231\t\n232\t  ```\n233\t  - path/to/file1\n234\t    - first distinct change\n235\t    - second distinct change, wrapping to next line\n236\t       with continuation indented 5\n237\t  ```\n238\t\n239\t  The file-by-file list is the source of truth for the\n240\t  cycle's mechanical change record. Chores carries the\n241\t  narrative + design, not a copy of it. Promote any\n242\t  \"why\" beyond one sentence to a chores `###` subsection.\n243\t\n244\t- **Session-repo (`.claude`) body**: bullets describe\n245\t  in-session activity rather than code changes.\n246\t\n247\t### Trailer\n248\t\n249\t`ochid:` as the last line of the body — see\n250\t[Cross-repo linking (ochid trailers)](../AGENTS.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)\n251\tin AGENTS.md for the convention.\n252\t\n253\tFor breaking changes, use the hyphenated `BREAKING-CHANGE:`\n254\ttrailer key. `BREAKING CHANGE:` (with a space) is the only\n255\tspace-separated key the Conventional Commits spec allows; the\n256\thyphenated form is also valid and avoids the space ambiguity.\n257\t\n258\t## Reviewing changes\n259\t\n260\tWork review looks at the **uncommitted working-copy diff**,\n261\ton the way to commit. The user opens diffs in their\n262\teditor (Zed, VSCode); jj commands are for terminal:\n263\t\n264\t- `jj diff` — working-copy diff (uncommitted)\n265\t- `jj diff -r @-` — diff of the previous commit\n266\t- `jj diff --from <X> --to <Y>` — any two revisions\n267\t- `jj show -r <X>` — description + diff for one rev\n268\t\n269\tDon't `jj edit -r @-` to view a past commit — that marks\n270\tit mutable and shifts `@`; use `jj diff -r @-` or\n271\t`jj show -r @-`.\n272\t\n273\tSee [Sub-cycle ladders](#sub-cycle-ladders) for the\n274\tclose-out squash recipe and recovery; revset primitives\n275\tare in [`jj-tips.md`](jj-tips.md#revsets).\n276\t\n277\t## Pushing\n278\t\n279\t### Policy\n280\t\n281\tPush is **discretionary** during the cycle (backup,\n282\tprogress visibility) and **mandatory at close-out** —\n283\tthe cycle's result must be published.\n284\t\n285\t### Shape at close-out push\n286\t\n287\tAt close-out the cycle's *work* is done; its *published\n288\tshape* is the remaining choice, made at push time. Surface\n289\tthe options and get user approval before pushing — once on\n290\tthe target, changing shape is a remote rewrite (force-push,\n291\tneeds approval), so choose deliberately.\n292\t\n293\t- **Squash to one commit** — single entry on the target.\n294\t  Right for straightforward changes where the Work-N is\n295\t  focused on one or two files.\n296\t- **Merge non-ff** *(current default)* — `main` gains a\n297\t  merge commit (`X.Y.Z`); cycle commits stay reachable via\n298\t  two parents. `jj log -r ..@ -n <N>` shows the trapezoidal\n299\t  shape. See [Merge non-ff recipe](#merge-non-ff-recipe)\n300\t  for the full setup sequence.\n301\t- **Keep separate** — one commit per cycle entry on\n302\t  `main`. Use when the decomposition itself is\n303\t  informative. Each chores section keeps its own header /\n304\t  `Commits:` ref; no consolidation churn.\n305\t\n306\tSet up squash/merge before invoking `vc-x1 push`; use\n307\t`jj git push` directly for non-standard shapes.\n308\t\n309\t### Merge non-ff recipe\n310\t\n311\tSetting up a [Merge non-ff](#shape-at-close-out-push)\n312\tclose-out is a fixed sequence. `<closeout>` is the cycle's\n313\tclose-out commit, `<prev>` the previous cycle's close-out\n314\t(the current `main` tip), `<work-tip>` the cycle's last\n315\tWork commit:\n316\t\n317\t1. **Rebase the close-out into a merge** — `jj rebase -r\n318\t   <closeout> --onto <prev> --onto <work-tip>`.\n319\t   - `-r <closeout>` keeps the `<closeout>` commit in place.\n320\t   - `--onto <prev>` becomes its first parent (trunk).\n321\t   - `--onto <work-tip>` becomes the second parent.\n322\t\n323\t   Together these make `<closeout>` a merge of\n324\t   `<prev>` + `<work-tip>`, forming a trapezoidal commit.\n325\t2. **Use `jj new <merge>`** to add an empty `@` above the\n326\t   merge. The rebase left `@` *on* the now-content-bearing\n327\t   merge, which git/IDE diff views show as uncommitted;\n328\t   `jj new` restores the clean empty `@` on top.\n329\t3. **Push** — `jj git push --bookmark main -R .`.\n330\t\n331\t**Post-hoc caveat.** If the cycle was already pushed\n332\t[Keep separate](#shape-at-close-out-push) its commits are\n333\timmutable: the rebase needs `--ignore-immutable` and the\n334\tpush force-updates `main`.\n335\tThe standard sequence assumes the merge is set up *before*\n336\tthe close-out push.\n337\t\n338\t### vc-x1 push wrapper\n339\t\n340\t`vc-x1 push <bookmark>` wraps per-push mechanics. See\n341\t`vc-x1 push --help` for current flags.\n342\t\n343\t**Current limitation**: only fully supports the\n344\t[Keep separate](#shape-at-close-out-push) shape; other\n345\tshapes need manual jj steps. Improvements tracked /\n346\tplanned:\n347\t\n348\t- N:1 code↔bot for Merge non-ff (`## Todo` entry P1).\n349\t- Symmetric squash (planned, to be captured in `-2`).\n350\t- Per-repo bookmark names (planned).\n351\t\n352\t### .claude cadence\n353\t\n354\t**Cadence**: one push = one `.claude` commit, paired\n355\twith every code commit in that push.\n356\t\n357\tThe `.claude` working copy accumulates session data\n358\tacross the cycle; its change ID stays stable across\n359\tsnapshots, `jj describe`, and the finalize commit, so\n360\tcode-side `ochid:` trailers resolve.\n361\t\n362\t`.claude` is a linear journal — all session work lives\n363\ton `main`, regardless of the app-side bookmark. **Do not\n364\tcreate or maintain `.claude` bookmarks that mirror\n365\tapp-side branches** — risks the bot steering session\n366\tpushes to the wrong remote ref.\n367\t\n368\tEnding a session: if the user runs `/exit` there will be\n369\tsession information created, which we don't worry about.\n370\tThe user can close the terminal instead and `@` will\n371\tremain empty.\n372\t\n373\t### Bot communication at the reviews\n374\t\n375\tUse plain prose — no insider jargon (\"Gate N signal\",\n376\t\"Checkpoint N\", etc.):\n377\t\n378\t- **At Work review** — summarize what changed and stop.\n379\t  \"Work complete. Please review.\"\n380\t- **At Commit Description review** — present `$TITLE`\n381\t  and `$BODY` explicitly; ask permission to commit/push.\n382\t  Don't spell out the full `vc-x1 push ... --title ...\n383\t  --body ...` invocation by default.\n384\t- **At Post close-out review** — surface the shape\n385\t  options (squash / merge / keep) and the push target;\n386\t  wait for the user's choice before any `jj squash` /\n387\t  `jj rebase` / `jj git push` invocation.\n388\t\n389\t### After push or finalize: stop and wait\n390\t\n391\tAfter you **push** (cross the remote boundary) or launch\n392\t**finalize** on the `.claude` repo (`vc-x1 finalize --repo\n393\t.claude --squash --push <bookmark> --delay 10 --detach`) — by\n394\thand or via the `vc-x1 push` wrapper — you **MUST NEVER**\n395\tproceed (next step, edit, tool call, text output) until the\n396\tuser explicitly directs you to continue. **Even when the next\n397\tstep seems obvious — wait.** Treat push-or-finalize as a hard\n398\tstop for the whole turn.\n399\t\n400\t`vc-x1 push` performs both as its tail stages — `push-app`\n401\tthen the detached `vc-x1 finalize` on `.claude` — so there is\n402\tno gap left to speak in once the push is invoked. Put **all**\n403\tclosing words *before* invoking it; do not purposely emit anything\n404\tafter the tool returns.\n405\t\n406\tWhy (`.claude` is the live journal finalize snapshots →\n407\tsquashes → pushes):\n408\t\n409\t- **`--detach`**: lets the tool return immediately so the\n410\t  harness can keep flushing the *trailing* session-data — the\n411\t  tool call's own transcript and any words emitted *before*\n412\t  the invoke — into the snapshot.\n413\t- **`--delay 10`**: gives the harness time to complete that\n414\t  flush before the snapshot is taken. It is **not** time for\n415\t  the bot to do more work.\n416\t- **silence**: the bot must not summarize or perform any work\n417\t  after the tool returns.\n418\t\n419\t**Known slip**: the bot has emitted a summary after launching\n420\tfinalize. It\ncontains instructions on how a commit cycle is accomplished.\n\n## Cycles\n\nA cycle has three phases:\n\n- **[Preparation](#preparation)** (`X.Y.Z-0`) — the cycle's\n  first commit. Sets up the cycle:\n  - Backfill the previous cycle's chores `Commits:` ref.\n  - Bump `Cargo.toml` to `X.Y.Z-0`.\n  - Pick up a `## Todo` item (typically the top-ranked,\n    #1) into `## In Progress` (bold title + succinct problem\n    statement + plan ladder).\n  - Open the [chores section](#chores-sections).\n- **[Work-N](#work-n)** (`X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, …) — the\n  commits that implement the change. See\n[Pushing](#pushing).\n\n**Sub-cycles.** When a Work commit's scope grows enough to\nwarrant its own ladder, it subdivides — `X.Y.Z-3.0`\nPreparation, `X.Y.Z-3.1` / `X.Y.Z-3.2` Work, `X.Y.Z-3`\nClose-out. The same three-phase shape applies recursively\nat every depth. As many as needed:\n\n- Each commit runs through the\n  **[per-commit flow](#per-commit-flow)**.\n- **Interim pushes** are optional (backup, progress\n  visibility).\n- Close-out is the only mandatory push (see\n  [Pushing](#pushing)).\n- **Subdivide into a sub-cycle** if a Work commit's\n  scope grows enough (see\n  [Sub-cycle ladders](#sub-cycle-ladders)).\n\n## Close-out\n\nThe cycle's last commit (bare `X.Y.Z`) does bookkeeping\nonly — the commit body describes that bookkeeping, not\nwhat happens post-squash:\n\n- **Move the picked-up item** from `## In Progress` to a\n  one-line entry (with a chores `[N]` ref) in `## Done`.\n- **Move the `## In Progress` block into the\n  [chores section](#chores-sections)** (the title-only\n  placeholder opened during Preparation):\n  - Cut the problem statement + plan ladder out of\n    `## In Progress` (drop the bold title line — the\n    chores `##` header already carries that string).\n  - Paste under the chores `##` header.\n  - Sync the chores header to the **final** commit title\n    if the cycle's scope shifted; one that grows a Preparation later adds\n`-3.0` without renumbering siblings.\n\nBump `Cargo.toml` at the start of each phase so `vc-x1 -V`\nreports the active phase at build time.\n\n## Per-commit flow\n\nEvery commit (Preparation, each Work commit, Close-out) goes\nthrough:\n\n1. **Mark this commit `(current)`** as the first edit in\n   `notes/todo.md > ## In Progress`.\n2. **Do the work** (see [Iterative work](#iterative-work)\n   for the loop-and-squash technique).\n3. **Flip this commit `(current)` → `(done)`** in `## In\n   Progress` — before the cargo cycle and the commit.\n4. **Cargo cycle** (skip-able for purely-docs commits; The user reviews the description. Chores carries the\n  narrative + design, not a copy of it. Promote any\n  \"why\" beyond one sentence to a chores `###` subsection.\n\n- **Session-repo (`.claude`) body**: bullets describe\n  in-session activity rather than code changes.\n\n### Trailer\n\n`ochid:` as the last line of the body — see\n[Cross-repo linking (ochid trailers)](../AGENTS.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)\nin AGENTS.md for the convention.\n\nFor breaking changes, use the hyphenated `BREAKING-CHANGE:`\ntrailer key. `BREAKING CHANGE:` (with a space) is the only\nspace-separated key the Conventional Commits spec allows; the\nhyphenated form is also valid and avoids the space ambiguity.\n\n## Reviewing changes\n\nWork review looks at the **uncommitted working-copy diff**,\non the way to commit. The user opens diffs in their\neditor (Zed, VSCode); jj commands are for terminal:\n\n- `jj diff` — working-copy diff (uncommitted)\n- `jj diff -r @-` — diff of the previous commit\n- `jj diff --from <X> --to <Y>` — any two revisions\n- `jj show -r <X>` — description + diff for one rev\n\nDon't `jj edit -r @-` to view a past commit — that marks\nit mutable and shifts `@`; use `jj diff -r @-` or\n`jj show -r @-`.\n\nSee [Sub-cycle ladders](#sub-cycle-ladders) for the\nclose-out squash recipe and recovery; revset primitives\nare in [`jj-tips.md`](jj-tips.md#revsets).\n\n## Pushing\n\n### Policy\n\nPush is **discretionary** during the cycle (backup,\nprogress visibility) and **mandatory at close-out** —\nthe cycle's result must be published.\n\n### Shape at close-out push\n\nAt close-out the cycle's *work* is done; its *published\nshape* is the remaining choice, made at push time. Surface\nthe options and get user approval before pushing — once on\nthe target, changing shape is a remote rewrite (force-push,\nneeds approval), so choose deliberately.\n\n- **Squash to one commit** — single entry on the target.\n  Right for straightforward changes where the Work-N is\n  focused on one or two files.\n- **Merge non-ff** *(current default)* — `main` gains a\n  merge commit (`X.Y.Z`); cycle commits stay reachable via\n  two parents. `jj log -r ..@ -n <N>` shows the trapezoidal\n  shape. See [Merge non-ff recipe](#merge-non-ff-recipe)\n  for the full setup sequence.\n- **Keep separate** — one commit per cycle entry on\n  `main`. Use when the decomposition itself is\n  informative. Each chores section keeps its own header /\n  `Commits:` ref; no consolidation churn.\n\nSet up squash/merge before invoking `vc-x1 push`; use\n`jj git push` directly for non-standard shapes.\n\n### Merge non-ff recipe\n\nSetting up a [Merge non-ff](#shape-at-close-out-push)\nclose-out is a fixed sequence. `<closeout>` is the cycle's\nclose-out commit, `<prev>` the previous cycle's close-out\n(the current `main` tip), `<work-tip>` the cycle's last\nWork commit:\n\n1. **Rebase the close-out into a merge** — `jj rebase -r\n   <closeout> --onto <prev> --onto <work-tip>`.\n   - `-r <closeout>` keeps the `<closeout>` commit in place.\n   - `--onto <prev>` becomes its first parent (trunk).\n   - `--onto <work-tip>` becomes the second parent.\n\n   Together these make `<closeout>` a merge of\n   `<prev>` + `<work-tip>`, forming a trapezoidal commit.\n2. **Use `jj new <merge>`** to add an empty `@` above the\n   merge. The rebase left `@` *on* the now-content-bearing\n   merge, which git/IDE diff views show as uncommitted;\n   `jj new` restores the clean empty `@` on top.\n3. **Push** — `jj git push --bookmark main -R .`.\n\n**Post-hoc caveat.** If the cycle was already pushed\n[Keep separate](#shape-at-close-out-push) its commits are\nimmutable: the rebase needs `--ignore-immutable` and the\npush force-updates `main`.\nThe standard sequence assumes the merge is set up *before*\nthe close-out push.\n\n### vc-x1 push wrapper\n\n`vc-x1 push <bookmark>` wraps per-push mechanics. It is **not** time for\n  the bot to do more work.\n- **silence**: the bot must not summarize or perform any work\n  after the tool returns.\n\n**Known slip**: the bot has emitted a summary after launching\nfinalize. There is no \"harmless\" closing line — if it's worth\nsaying, say it *before* the invoke.\n\n### Recovery\n\n- **If push exits before `finalize-claude`** (e.g.\n  failure between `push-app` and `finalize-claude`), run\n  finalize by hand:\n\n  ```\n  vc-x1 finalize --repo .claude --squash --push <bookmark> --delay 10 --detach --log /tmp/vc-x1-finalize.log\n  ```\n\n- **Run finalize again if `@` is non-empty** after the\n  finalize's squash-and-commit (also desirable after\n  extra activity by the bot's agents).\n  - Why: finalize snapshots `.claude` at `--delay`, but the\n    bot keeps writing session data while it runs — the tool's\n    own invocation plus the bot's closing response land\n    *after* the snapshot.\n  - Safe to repeat: bot session data is append-only, so a\n    re-run never conflicts or overwrites. (This could\n    change; it is not under the user's control.)\n  - Fix: run `vc-x1 finalize --repo .claude --squash --push\n    <bookmark> --delay 10 --detach` another time to capture\n    that tail; one extra pass is generally enough.\n  - No guarantees: events outside the bot's control can leave\n    `@` non-empty — e.g. the bot's back end may decide to\n    squash/consolidate session data, which can take minutes\n    and land after the snapshot. This is why a single pass is never\n    guaranteed to leave `@` empty.\n- **Clear push's saved state** after any out-of-band\n  recovery — `rm .vc-x1/push-state.toml` or `vc-x1 push\n  <bookmark> --restart` — otherwise push resumes from a\n  stale stage.\n- **Late code-repo tweak after `push-app` succeeded**\n  (e.g. updating AGENTS.md or memory) requires `jj\n  squash --ignore-immutable` and a re-push; that is a\n  remote rewrite and needs explicit approval like any\n  push.\n\n## Iterative work\n\nWhen work for a single commit (the **target**) benefits\nfrom incremental review, loop:\n\n1. `jj new -R .` — fresh empty `@` on top of the target.\n2. Make the next round of changes.\n3. User reviews the round (see\n   [Reviewing changes](#reviewing-changes)).\n4. `jj squash -R .` folds into the target and creates a\n   new empty `@`.\n5. If not done, go to step 2.\n\nSame jj mechanics as a\n[sub-cycle ladder](#sub-cycle-ladders), but at\nsingle-commit scope — the cycle's version suffix\ndoesn't change.\n\n## Sub-cycle ladders\n\nWhen a Work commit subdivides into a sub-cycle (see\n[Numbering](#numbering) for suffix nesting), its Work\ncommits typically live as a local jj `@` chain and\n**collapse into the sub-cycle's Close-out** before the\nparent cycle continues. Ladder commits are scratch —\nfor review and bisection only.\n\n### Per-Work-commit contract within a ladder\n\nFor each Work commit in the ladder:\n\n1. `jj new -R .` — create a fresh empty `@`.\n2. Do the commit's work.\n3. Run `cargo test --bins`. **Non-negotiable** — build\n   and clippy alone miss regressions until a later\n   commit runs the full suite, raising bisection cost.\n4. `jj describe -m \"...\" -m \"...\" -R .` — working title\n   only (no version suffix); the sub-cycle Close-out\n   collects everything into one final commit with the\n   `(X.Y.Z-N)` marker.\n\n### Navigating the ladder\n\nCommon moves:\n\n- `jj log -r '<base>::' -R .` — see the whole ladder\n  from its base.\n- `jj edit -r <prefix> -R .` — jump `@` to any ladder\n  commit by chid prefix; useful for bisection.\n- `jj edit @-- -R .` — quick-jump back two commits.\n- `jj diff -r <chid> -R .` — review one commit in\n  isolation.\n\nModifications to any ladder commit rewrite it in place;\ndescendants auto-rebase.\n\n### Close-out: squash the ladder\n\nWhen all ladder Work commits are done and tests pass:\n\n```\njj squash --from \"<base>..@-\" --into @ -u -R .\n```\n\n`<base>` is the parent of the first ladder commit; `-u`\nkeeps `@`'s description and discards the sources'.\nAfter squash, history is linear: `<base> → @`;\nintermediate commits are auto-abandoned.\n\nThen `vc-x1 push <bookmark>` as for any other commit.\n\nFor N = 1 the squash is a no-op (`<base>..@-` is empty\nwhen `@-` is `<base>`); push the single commit directly.\n\n### Recovery\n\nIf a ladder commit goes wrong, back out without losing\nprior commits:\n\n- **Discard the current commit.** `jj abandon @ -R .`\n  drops it; you get a fresh empty `@` on the same\n  parent.\n- **Edit an earlier commit.** `jj edit -r <chid> -R .`,\n  make corrections, then `jj edit -r <last-ladder-chid>`\n  to return. Descendants auto-rebase.\n- **Discard the entire ladder.** `jj op log -R .` shows\n  the op history; `jj op restore <op-id> -R .` reverts\n  to that point. Full undo — removes *all* ladder work\n  after the chosen op. Use only to start over.\n\n# References\n\n- [`jj-tips.md`](jj-tips.md#revsets) — revset primitives\n  (chid/cid, `@`/`@-`/`@+`, `..`/`::` ranges, prefix matching).\n- [`substep-test.sh`](substep-test.sh) — script that\n  scaffolds a 4-revision ladder under `/tmp/substep-test`\n  for squash-recipe experiments.\n- The per-commit `cargo test --bins` gate exists because a\n  regression introduced in an early ladder commit can go\n  uncaught until a later commit runs the full suite, raising\n  bisection cost.\n","numLines":563,"startLine":1,"totalLines":563}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"51d1883c-5cbb-4776-bd25-39b18e2e65f8","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/vc-template-x1","sessionId":"c1080192-9374-42c5-a6b4-38ea90600a52","version":"2.1.162","gitBranch":"HEAD"}

`gitk`\n158\t\n159\tIf you're coming from git, jj's log output can be surprising compared to\n160\ttools like `gitk --all`.\n161\t\n162\tjj tracks *changes* (identified by change IDs), not individual git commits.\n163\tWhen you rewrite a change (`jj describe`, `jj rebase`, `jj squash`, etc.),\n164\tjj creates a new git commit and keeps the old one under `refs/jj/keep/*` as\n165\tundo history. `gitk --all` sees all of these obsolete commits; `jj log` only\n166\tshows the current version of each change.\n167\t\n168\t## Useful commands\n169\t\n170\t| Command | Description |\n171\t|---------|-------------|\n172\t| `jj log` | Show recent visible commits (default revset) |\n173\t| `jj log -r ::@` | Show **all** ancestors of the working copy |\n174\t| `jj log -r 'all()'` | Show all non-hidden commits (needed if you have multiple heads/branches) |\n175\t| `jj st` | Show the status of the Working and Parent commits |\n176\t| `jj st -r <chid>` | Status of the commit, `<chid>` such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n177\t| `jj show` | Show the Working commit (`-r @`) |\n178\t| `jj show -r <chid>` | Show the commit, `<chid>` such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n179\t| `jj evolog -r <chid>` | Show the evolution history of a single change |\n180\t| `jj op log` | Show operation history (each rewrite operation) |\n181\t\n182\t\n183\tIn a single-branch workflow, `jj log -r ::@` and `jj log -r 'all()'` give\n184\tthe same result. Use `all()` when you have multiple branches or heads.\n185\t\n186\t## Revsets\n187\t\n188\tRevsets (sets of revisions) are how jj addresses commits. A\n189\trevision is identified by `@`, a chid, or a cid, and revsets are\n190\tbuilt from those identifiers plus the operators `-`, `+`, `..`,\n191\tand `::`. There is a complete language available — see\n192\t`jj help -k revsets`. The [`substep-test.sh`](substep-test.sh)\n193\tscript scaffolds the example repo used below.\n194\t\n195\tSummary:\n196\t\n197\t- A revision (rev) is used for addressing/referring to commits.\n198\t- jj supports a change_id (chid) and commit_id (cid).\n199\t  - The chid is permanent and doesn't change.\n200\t  - The cid is the SHA of the current commit and changes with any\n201\t    change to it or its ancestors.\n202\t- A revset is a set of revisions.\n203\t- In many jj commands revsets can address multiple commits.\n204\t- There is one root commit; chid=zzz sha=0 owner=root.\n205\t- The root commit never has content nor description.\n206\t- There can be multiple independent lineages of commits off root():\n207\t  - to create:\n208\t    - `jj new 'root()'`\n209\t    - `git switch --orphan <name>`\n210\t  - to see these:\n211\t    - `jj log -r 'roots(~root())'`\n212\t    - `git log --all --max-parents=0 --oneline`\n213\t\n214\tThe examples below show these primitives in action.\n215\t\n216\t### A jj repo with some commits\n217\t\n218\tSome examples of revisions/rev:\n219\t   - @, chid=tkpvsrop, cid=ad2ba9b4 is the current commit\n220\t   - @-, chid=wxtmosqz, cid=35ac2422 is the ancestor of the current commit\n221\t   - @--, chid=vktlnyvm, cid=a0b0285e is the ancestor of the ancestor and so on\n222\t\n223\t```\n224\t$ jj log -r 'all()'\n225\t@  tkpvsrop wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 ad2ba9b4\n226\t│  count 3\n227\t○  wxtmosqz wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 35ac2422\n228\t│  count 2\n229\t○  vktlnyvm wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 a0b0285e\n230\t│  count 1\n231\t○  nvwytkrw wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 base 54fd18f7\n232\t│  count 0\n233\t◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000\n234\t```\n235\t\n236\tMove @ to vktlnyvm. The blank output\n279\t  for `@+++` and `@---` is the empty revset — there is no revision\n280\t  that far away in this chain.\n281\t- `@..` and `@::` are ranges going outward from @ toward\n282\t  descendants:\n283\t  - `@..` is the *open* form: descendants of @, **excluding** @\n284\t    itself (here: count 2 and count 3).\n285\t  - `@::` is the *closed* form: descendants of @, **including** @\n286\t    itself (here: @=count 1, count 2, count 3).\n287\t- `..@` and `::@` are ranges going inward from some implicit start\n288\t  toward ancestors of @:\n289\t  - `..@` includes @ and its ancestors but **excludes** the root\n290\t    commit (here: @=count 1, base=count 0).\n291\t  - `::@` includes the root commit as well.\n292\t\n293\tMnemonic: `..` and `::` both produce ranges; `::` includes the\n294\timplicit endpoint (root or visible heads), `..` excludes it. ((main))\n$\n```\n\n## Why `jj log` shows fewer commits than `gitk`\n\nIf you're coming from git, jj's log output can be surprising compared to\ntools like `gitk --all`.\n\njj tracks *changes* (identified by change IDs), not individual git commits.\nWhen you rewrite a change (`jj describe`, `jj rebase`, `jj squash`, etc.),\njj creates a new git commit and keeps the old one under `refs/jj/keep/*` as\nundo history. `gitk --all` sees all of these obsolete commits; `jj log` only\nshows the current version of each change.\n\n## Useful commands\n\n| Command | Description |\n|---------|-------------|\n| `jj log` | Show recent visible commits (default revset) |\n| `jj log -r ::@` | Show **all** ancestors of the working copy |\n| `jj log -r 'all()'` | Show all non-hidden commits (needed if you have multiple heads/branches) |\n| `jj st` | Show the status of the Working and Parent commits |\n| `jj st -r <chid>` | Status of the commit, `<chid>` such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n| `jj show` | Show the Working commit (`-r @`) |\n| `jj show -r <chid>` | Show the commit, `<chid>` such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n| `jj evolog -r <chid>` | Show the evolution history of a single change |\n| `jj op log` | Show operation history (each rewrite operation) |\n\n\nIn a single-branch workflow, `jj log -r ::@` and `jj log -r 'all()'` give\nthe same result. Use `all()` when you have multiple branches or heads.\n\n## Revsets\n\nRevsets (sets of revisions) are how jj addresses commits. A\nrevision is identified by `@`, a chid, or a cid, and revsets are\nbuilt from those identifiers plus the operators `-`, `+`, `..`,\nand `::`. There is a complete language available — see\n`jj help -k revsets`. The [`substep-test.sh`](substep-test.sh)\nscript scaffolds the example repo used below.\n\nSummary:\n\n- A revision (rev) is used for addressing/referring to commits.\n- jj supports a change_id (chid) and commit_id (cid).\n  - The chid is permanent and doesn't change.\n  - The cid is the SHA of the current commit and changes with any\n    change to it or its ancestors.\n- A revset is a set of revisions.\n- In many jj commands revsets can address multiple commits.\n- There is one root commit; chid=zzz sha=0 owner=root.\n- The root commit never has content nor description.\n- There can be multiple independent lineages of commits off root():\n  - to create:\n    - `jj new 'root()'`\n    - `git switch --orphan <name>`\n  - to see these:\n    - `jj log -r 'roots(~root())'`\n    - `git log --all --max-parents=0 --oneline`\n\nThe examples below show these primitives in action.\n\n### A jj repo with some commits\n\nSome examples of revisions/rev:\n   - @, chid=tkpvsrop, cid=ad2ba9b4 is the current commit\n   - @-, chid=wxtmosqz, cid=35ac2422 is the ancestor of the current commit\n   - @--, chid=vktlnyvm, cid=a0b0285e is the ancestor of the ancestor and so on\n\n```\n$ jj log -r 'all()'\n@  tkpvsrop wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 ad2ba9b4\n│  count 3\n○  wxtmosqz wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 35ac2422\n│  count 2\n○  vktlnyvm wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 a0b0285e\n│  count 1\n○  nvwytkrw wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 base 54fd18f7\n│  count 0\n◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000\n```\n\nMove @ to vktlnyvm. (This could also have been done with `jj edit -r @--`.)\n\n```\n$ jj edit -r vkt\nWorking copy  (@) now at: vktlnyvm a0b0285e count 1\nParent commit (@-)      : nvwytkrw 54fd18f7 base | count 0\n```\n\n### Referencing commits with relative revsets\n\n```\n$ jj log -r @\n@  vktlnyvm count 1\n$ jj log -r @-\n○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n$ jj log -r @--\n◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000\n$ jj log -r @+\n○  wxtmosqz count 2\n$ jj log -r @++\n○  tkpvsrop count 3\n$ jj log -r @+++      # empty — nothing that far out\n$ jj log -r @---      # empty\n$ jj log -r @..\n○  tkpvsrop count 3\n○  wxtmosqz count 2\n$ jj log -r @::\n○  tkpvsrop count 3\n○  wxtmosqz count 2\n@  vktlnyvm count 1\n$ jj log -r ..@\n@  vktlnyvm count 1\n○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n$ jj log -r ::@\n@  vktlnyvm count 1\n○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000\n```\n\n#### Interpretation\n\n- `@-` and `@--` resolve to single revisions: parent and\n  grandparent of @. `@+` and `@++` are children. The blank output\n  for `@+++` and `@---` is the empty revset — there is no revision\n  that far away in this chain.\n- `@..` and `@::` are ranges going outward from @ toward\n  descendants:\n  - `@..` is the *open* form: descendants of @, **excluding** @\n    itself (here: count 2 and count 3).\n  - `@::` is the *closed* form: descendants of @, **including** @\n    itself (here: @=count 1, count 2, count 3).\n- `..@` and `::@` are ranges going inward from some implicit start\n  toward ancestors of @:\n  - `..@` includes @ and its ancestors but **excludes** the root\n    commit (here: @=count 1, base=count 0).\n  - `::@` includes the root commit as well.\n\nMnemonic: `..` and `::` both produce ranges; `::` includes the\nimplicit endpoint (root or visible heads), `..` excludes it. The\nnamed operand is always part of the result on the target side; on\nthe source side it depends on which dot-form is used (excluded by\n`..`, included by `::`).\n\n### Referencing commits with absolute revsets\n\n```\n$ jj log -r v          # unambiguous prefix of vktlnyvm\n@  vktlnyvm count 1\n$ jj log -r vktln\n@  vktlnyvm count 1\n$ jj log -r w+         # w matches wxtmosqz, + takes its child\n○  tkpvsrop count 3\n$ jj log -r w--\n○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n$ jj log -r w..\n○  tkpvsrop count 3\n$ jj log -r ..w\n○  wxtmosqz count 2\n@  vktlnyvm count 1\n○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n$ jj log -r w::\n○  tkpvsrop count 3\n○  wxtmosqz count 2\n$ jj log -r ::w\n○  wxtmosqz count 2\n@  vktlnyvm count 1\n○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000\n```\n\n#### Interpretation\n\n- `v` and `vktln` both resolve to chid `vktlnyvm` because they are\n  unambiguous prefixes within this repo — no other chid starts\n  with those letters.\n- `w+` resolves in two stages: `w` matches `wxtmosqz` (count 2) by\n  prefix, then `+` takes its child, giving count 3.\n- `w--` grandparent of w.\n- `w..` descendants of w, excluding w.\n- `..w` ancestors of w, not including root.\n- `::w` ancestors of w, including root.\n- `w::` descendants of w, including w.\n\nPrefix rule: jj rejects ambiguous prefixes. If two chids both\nstart with the same letters, the prefix must be lengthened until\nexactly one chid matches.\n\n## Cross-repo Linking with Git Trailers\n\nCommits in each repo use [git trailers](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-interpret-trailers)\nto cross-reference their counterpart in the other repo. The goal\nis that this main repo contains the \"what\", while the partner\nbot repo contains \"why\" and \"how\". The key to the convention\nis each change is cross-referenced to the other. By\ndefault `cargo install` ignores `Cargo.lock` and re-resolves\ndependencies from scratch, so it can silently build the binary from\na different — possibly broken — dependency graph than `cargo build`\n/ `cargo test` ran against.\n\n| command | reads `Cargo.lock`? | re-resolves? |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `cargo build` / `test` / `run`  | yes     | only if `Cargo.toml` changed |\n| `cargo build --locked` (etc.)   | yes     | never; errors if it would need to |\n| `cargo install` (default)       | **no**  | always, from scratch |\n| `cargo install --locked`        | yes     | never; errors if it would need to |\n\nThere's no stable cargo config knob to make `--locked` the default\nfor `cargo install`, so the discipline lives in the per-commit cargo\ncycle and shell aliases (e.g. `alias ci='cargo install --locked'`).\n\nThe trade-off is predictable-as-tested (`--locked`) vs picking up\nupstream fixes via fresh resolves (default). Either is defensible —\npick what fits your project, then edit this section and the\nper-commit cargo cycle to match.
