In particular, decisions like the `cargo install` behavior\n(default re-resolve vs `--locked`) under [Releasing](#releasing) are\nyours to make — pick what fits and update the docs (and the\nper-commit cargo cycle) so the choice is recorded for future readers.\n\n## Assumptions\n\nThe workflow documented here presumes two things this template\ndoes not itself ship:\n\n- **A Rust crate.** The per-commit cargo cycle (`cargo fmt` /\n  `clippy` / `test` / `install`) and the `Cargo.toml` version\n  bumps assume you have added a crate; the template carries docs\n  and notes only (no `Cargo.toml` / `src/` yet).\n- **The `vc-x1` companion tool.** Steps that invoke `vc-x1`\n  (`fix-todo`, `validate-todo`, `chid`, `push`, `finalize`) need\n  [vc-x1](https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1) installed; the\n  underlying jj steps are documented so the flow also works\n  without it.\n\n## Cloning\n\nThe Bot session repo is setup as a git submodule which\nmakes it easier to clone both repos. The easiest is to\nclone both when doing the initial clone:\n```\ngit clone --recursive git@github.com:winksaville/vc-template-x1\n```\n\nIf you forget to use --recursive you need to do two additional\nsteps \"init\" and \"update\":\n```\ngit clone git@github.com:winksaville/vc-template-x1\ngit submodule init\ngit submodule update\n```\n\nAnd these can be combined using 'update --init' if you like\n```\ngit clone git@github.com:winksaville/vc-template-x1\ngit submodule update --init\n```\n\n## Releasing\n\n**`cargo install` lockfile gotcha.** If you install your project's\nbinary with `cargo install --path .`, also pass `--locked`. By\ndefault `cargo install` ignores `Cargo.lock` and re-resolves\ndependencies from scratch, so it can silently build the binary from\na different — possibly broken — dependency graph than `cargo build`\n/ `cargo test` ran against.\n\n| command | reads `Cargo.lock`? | re-resolves? |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `cargo build` / `test` / `run`  | yes     | only if `Cargo.toml` changed |\n| `cargo build --locked` (etc.)   | yes     | never; errors if it would need to |\n| `cargo install` (default)       | **no**  | always, from scratch |\n| `cargo install --locked`        | yes     | never; errors if it would need to |\n\nThere's no stable cargo config knob to make `--locked` the default\nfor `cargo install`, so the discipline lives in the per-commit cargo\ncycle and shell aliases (e.g. `alias ci='cargo install --locked'`).\n\nThe trade-off is predictable-as-tested (`--locked`) vs picking up\nupstream fixes via fresh resolves (default). Either is defensible —\npick what fits your project, then edit this section and the\nper-commit cargo cycle to match. Background:\n[cargo#7169](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/7169),\n[cargo#9436](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/9436).\n\n## jj Tips for Git Users\n\nThis project uses [Jujutsu (jj)](https://docs.jj-vcs.dev/latest/)\nalongside git. New to jj? See\n[Steve Klabnik](https://github.com/steveklabnik)'s\n[Jujutsu tutorial](https://steveklabnik.github.io/jujutsu-tutorial).\n\nRepo-specific how-tos — initial commit, pushing, modifying and\nforce-pushing a commit, revsets, and a useful-commands reference —\nlive in [notes/jj-tips.md](notes/jj-tips.md).\n\n## Cross-repo Linking with Git Trailers\n\nCommits in each repo use [git trailers](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-interpret-trailers)\nto cross-reference their counterpart in the other repo via an\n`ochid` (Other Change ID) trailer — the defining mechanism of the\ndual-repo convention. For the full definition — trailer syntax,\nthe example shape, per-commit mechanics, and `.vc-config.toml` —\nsee\n[Cross-repo linking (ochid trailers)](AGENTS.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers).\n\n## Contributing\n\nBot-following workflow, commit conventions, and code style are\ncanonical in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md):\n\n- [Versioning during development](CLAUDE.md#versioning) — `-N`\n  pre-release suffix convention (single-step vs multi-step).\n- [Commit message style](CLAUDE.md#commit-message-style).\n- [Commit-Push-Finalize Flow](CLAUDE.md#commit-push-finalize-flow) —\n  two-checkpoint per-step discipline.\n- [Code Conventions](CLAUDE.md#code-conventions) — doc comments on\n  every file / fn / method, `// OK: …` on `unwrap*` calls,\n  ask-on-ambiguity, stuck detection.\n- [Pre-commit checklist](CLAUDE.md#pre-commit-checklist).\n\nTask tracking and release details live under [notes/](notes/):\nnear-term tasks in [notes/todo.md](notes/todo.md), per-release\ndetails in `notes/chores-*.md`, and notes-specific formatting\nrules in [notes/README.md](notes/README.md).\n\n## License\n\nLicensed under either of\n\n- Apache License, Version 2.0 ([LICENSE-APACHE](LICENSE-APACHE) or http://apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0)\n- MIT license ([LICENSE-MIT](LICENSE-MIT) or http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)\n\n### Contribution\n\nUnless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted\nfor inclusion in the work by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall\nbe dual licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.\n\n[1]: https://github.com/karpathy/autoresearch\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":109,"oldLines":22,"newStart":109,"newLines":26,"lines":[" ## The goal\nis that this main repo contains the \"what\", while the partner\nbot repo contains \"why\" and \"how\". The key to the convention\nis each change is cross-referenced to the other. Thus there\nis a coherent story of the development of the project across time.\n\nThe beginnings of that tool is [vc-x1](https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1)\nwhich currently does achieve this goal, but is being used as a\nfirst test bed.\n\n## This is a template — customize freely\n\n`CLAUDE.md` and this `README.md` are just starting points.\nRead both and edit either to match the conventions you want for your\nproject. In particular, decisions like the `cargo install` behavior\n(default re-resolve vs `--locked`) under [Releasing](#releasing) are\nyours to make — pick what fits and update the docs (and the\nper-commit cargo cycle) so the choice is recorded for future readers.\n\n## Assumptions\n\nThe workflow documented here presumes two things this template\ndoes not itself ship:\n\n- **A Rust crate.** The per-commit cargo cycle (`cargo fmt` /\n  `clippy` / `test` / `install`) and the `Cargo.toml` version\n  bumps assume you have added a crate; the template carries docs\n  and notes only (no `Cargo.toml` / `src/` yet).\n- **The `vc-x1` companion tool.** Steps that invoke `vc-x1`\n  (`fix-todo`, `validate-todo`, `chid`, `push`, `finalize`) need\n  [vc-x1](https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1) installed; the\n  underlying jj steps are documented so the flow also works\n  without it.\n\n## Cloning\n\nThe Bot session repo is setup as a git submodule which\nmakes it easier to clone both repos. By\ndefault `cargo install` ignores `Cargo.lock` and re-resolves\ndependencies from scratch, so it can silently build the binary from\na different — possibly broken — dependency graph than `cargo build`\n/ `cargo test` ran against.\n\n| command | reads `Cargo.lock`? | re-resolves? |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `cargo build` / `test` / `run`  | yes     | only if `Cargo.toml` changed |\n| `cargo build --locked` (etc.)   | yes     | never; errors if it would need to |\n| `cargo install` (default)       | **no**  | always, from scratch |\n| `cargo install --locked`        | yes     | never; errors if it would need to |\n\nThere's no stable cargo config knob to make `--locked` the default\nfor `cargo install`, so the discipline lives in the per-commit cargo\ncycle and shell aliases (e.g. `alias ci='cargo install --locked'`).\n\nThe trade-off is predictable-as-tested (`--locked`) vs picking up\nupstream fixes via fresh resolves (default). Either is defensible —\npick what fits your project, then edit this section and the\nper-commit cargo cycle to match. Background:\n[cargo#7169](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/7169),\n[cargo#9436](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/9436).\n\n## jj Tips for Git Users\n\nThis project uses [Jujutsu (jj)](https://docs.jj-vcs.dev/latest/)\nalongside git. `gitk`\n159\t\n160\tIf you're coming from git, jj's log output can be surprising compared to\n161\ttools like `gitk --all`.\n162\t\n163\tjj tracks *changes* (identified by change IDs), not individual git commits.\n164\tWhen you rewrite a change (`jj describe`, `jj rebase`, `jj squash`, etc.),\n165\tjj creates a new git commit and keeps the old one under `refs/jj/keep/*` as\n166\tundo history. `gitk --all` sees all of these obsolete commits; `jj log` only\n167\tshows the current version of each change.\n168\t\n169\t## Useful commands\n170\t\n171\t| Command | Description |\n172\t|---------|-------------|\n173\t| `jj log` | Show recent visible commits (default revset) |\n174\t| `jj log -r ::@` | Show **all** ancestors of the working copy |\n175\t| `jj log -r 'all()'` | Show all non-hidden commits (needed if you have multiple heads/branches) |\n176\t| `jj st` | Show the status of the Working and Parent commits |\n177\t| `jj st -r <chid>` | Status of the commit, `<chid>` such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n178\t| `jj show` | Show the Working commit (`-r @`) |\n179\t| `jj show -r <chid>` | Show the commit, `<chid>` such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n180\t| `jj evolog -r <chid>` | Show the evolution history of a single change |\n181\t| `jj op log` | Show operation history (each rewrite operation) |\n182\t\n183\t\n184\tIn a single-branch workflow, `jj log -r ::@` and `jj log -r 'all()'` give\n185\tthe same result. Use `all()` when you have multiple branches or heads.\n186\t\n187\t## Revsets\n188\t\n189\tRevsets (sets of revisions) are how jj addresses commits. A\n190\trevision is identified by `@`, a chid, or a cid, and revsets are\n191\tbuilt from those identifiers plus the operators `-`, `+`, `..`,\n192\tand `::`. There is a complete language available — see\n193\t`jj help -k revsets`.\n194\t\n195\tSummary:\n196\t\n197\t- A revision (rev) is used for addressing/referring to commits.\n198\t- jj supports a change_id (chid) and commit_id (cid).\n199\t  - The chid is permanent and doesn't change.\n200\t  - The cid is the SHA of the current commit and changes with any\n201\t    change to it or its ancestors.\n202\t- A revset is a set of revisions.\n203\t- In many jj commands revsets can address multiple commits.\n204\t- There is one root commit; chid=zzz sha=0 owner=root.\n205\t- The root commit never has content nor description.\n206\t- There can be multiple independent lineages of commits off root():\n207\t  - to create:\n208\t    - `jj new 'root()'`\n209\t    - `git switch --orphan <name>`\n210\t  - to see these:\n211\t    - `jj log -r 'roots(~root())'`\n212\t    - `git log --all --max-parents=0 --oneline`\n213\t\n214\tThe examples below show these primitives in action.\n215\t\n216\t### A jj repo with some commits\n217\t\n218\tSome examples of revisions/rev:\n219\t   - @, chid=tkpvsrop, cid=ad2ba9b4 is the current commit\n220\t   - @-, chid=wxtmosqz, cid=35ac2422 is the ancestor of the current commit\n221\t   - @--, chid=vktlnyvm, cid=a0b0285e is the ancestor of the ancestor and so on\n222\t\n223\t```\n224\t$ jj log -r 'all()'\n225\t@  tkpvsrop wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 ad2ba9b4\n226\t│  count 3\n227\t○  wxtmosqz wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 35ac2422\n228\t│  count 2\n229\t○  vktlnyvm wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 a0b0285e\n230\t│  count 1\n231\t○  nvwytkrw wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 base 54fd18f7\n232\t│  count 0\n233\t◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000\n234\t```\n235\t\n236\tMove @ to vktlnyvm. (This could also have been done with `jj edit -r @--`.)\n237\t\n238\t```\n239\t$ jj edit -r vkt\n240\tWorking copy  (@) now at: vktlnyvm a0b0285e count 1\n241\tParent commit (@-)      : nvwytkrw 54fd18f7 base | count 0\n242\t```\n243\t\n244\t### Referencing commits with relative revsets\n245\t\n246\t```\n247\t$ jj log -r @\n248\t@  vktlnyvm count 1\n249\t$ jj log -r @-\n250\t○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n251\t$ jj log -r @--\n252\t◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000\n253\t$ jj log -r @+\n254\t○  wxtmosqz count 2\n255\t$ jj log -r @++\n256\t○  tkpvsrop count 3\n257\t$ jj log -r @+++      # empty — nothing that far out\n258\t$ jj log -r @---      # empty\n259\t$ jj log -r @..\n260\t○  tkpvsrop count 3\n261\t○  wxtmosqz count 2\n262\t$ jj log -r @::\n263\t○  tkpvsrop count 3\n264\t○  wxtmosqz count 2\n265\t@  vktlnyvm count 1\n266\t$ jj log -r ..@\n267\t@  vktlnyvm count 1\n268\t○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n269\t$ jj log -r ::@\n270\t@  vktlnyvm count 1\n271\t○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n272\t◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000\n273\t```\n274\t\n275\t#### Interpretation\n276\t\n277\t- `@-` and `@--` resolve to single revisions: parent and\n278\t  grandparent of @. `@+` and `@++` are children. The blank output\n279\t  for `@+++` and `@---` is the empty revset — there is no revision\n280\t  that far away in this chain.\n281\t- `@..` and `@::` are ranges going outward from @ toward\n282\t  descendants:\n283\t  - `@..` is the *open* form: descendants of @, **excluding** @\n284\t    itself (here: count 2 and count 3).\n285\t  - `@::` is the *closed* form: descendants of @, **including** @\n286\t    itself (here: @=count 1, count 2, count 3).\n287\t- `..@` and `::@` are ranges going inward from some implicit start\n288\t  toward ancestors of @:\n289\t  - `..@` includes @ and its ancestors but **excludes** the root\n290\t    commit (here: @=count 1, base=count 0).\n291\t  - `::@` includes the root commit as well.\n292\t\n293\tMnemonic: `..` and `::` both produce ranges; `::` includes the\n294\timplicit endpoint (root or visible heads), `..` excludes it. The\n295\tnamed operand is always part of the result on the target side; on\n296\tthe source side it depends on which dot-form is used (excluded by\n297\t`..`, included by `::`).\n298\t\n299\t### Referencing commits with absolute revsets\n300\t\n301\t```\n302\t$ jj log -r v          # unambiguous prefix of vktlnyvm\n303\t@  vktlnyvm count 1\n304\t$ jj log -r vktln\n305\t@  vktlnyvm count 1\n306\t$ jj log -r w+         # w matches wxtmosqz, + takes its child\n307\t○  tkpvsrop count 3\n308\t$ jj log -r w--\n309\t○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n310\t$ jj log -r w..\n311\t○  tkpvsrop count 3\n312\t$ jj log -r ..w\n313\t○  wxtmosqz count 2\n314\t@  vktlnyvm count 1\n315\t○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n316\t$ jj log -r w::\n317\t○  tkpvsrop count 3\n318\t○  wxtmosqz count 2\n319\t$ jj log -r ::w\n320\t○  wxtmosqz count 2\n321\t@  vktlnyvm count 1\n322\t○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n323\t◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000\n324\t```\n325\t\n326\t#### Interpretation\n327\t\n328\t- `v` and `vktln` both resolve to chid `vktlnyvm` because they are\n329\t  unambiguous prefixes within this repo — no other chid starts\n330\t  with those letters.\n331\t- `w+` resolves in two stages: `w` matches `wxtmosqz` (count 2) by\n332\t  prefix, then `+` takes its child, giving count 3.\n333\t- `w--` grandparent of w.\n334\t- `w..` descendants of w, excluding w.\n335\t- `..w` ancestors of w, not including root.\n336\t- `::w` ancestors of w, including root.\n337\t- `w::` descendants of w, including w.\n338\t\n339\tPrefix rule: jj rejects ambiguous prefixes. If two chids both\n340\tstart with the same letters, the prefix must be lengthened until\n341\texactly one chid matches.\n342\t\n343\t## Cross-repo Linking with Git Trailers\n344\t\n345\tEach commit cross-references its counterpart in the other repo\n346\tvia an `ochid:` git trailer. (identified by change IDs), not individual git commits.\nWhen you rewrite a change (`jj describe`, `jj rebase`, `jj squash`, etc.),\njj creates a new git commit and keeps the old one under `refs/jj/keep/*` as\nundo history. `gitk --all` sees all of these obsolete commits; `jj log` only\nshows the current version of each change.\n\n## Useful commands\n\n| Command | Description |\n|---------|-------------|\n| `jj log` | Show recent visible commits (default revset) |\n| `jj log -r ::@` | Show **all** ancestors of the working copy |\n| `jj log -r 'all()'` | Show all non-hidden commits (needed if you have multiple heads/branches) |\n| `jj st` | Show the status of the Working and Parent commits |\n| `jj st -r <chid>` | Status of the commit, `<chid>` such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n| `jj show` | Show the Working commit (`-r @`) |\n| `jj show -r <chid>` | Show the commit, `<chid>` such as `@`, `@-`, `xyz` |\n| `jj evolog -r <chid>` | Show the evolution history of a single change |\n| `jj op log` | Show operation history (each rewrite operation) |\n\n\nIn a single-branch workflow, `jj log -r ::@` and `jj log -r 'all()'` give\nthe same result. Use `all()` when you have multiple branches or heads.\n\n## Revsets\n\nRevsets (sets of revisions) are how jj addresses commits. A\nrevision is identified by `@`, a chid, or a cid, and revsets are\nbuilt from those identifiers plus the operators `-`, `+`, `..`,\nand `::`. There is a complete language available — see\n`jj help -k revsets`.\n\nSummary:\n\n- A revision (rev) is used for addressing/referring to commits.\n- jj supports a change_id (chid) and commit_id (cid).\n  - The chid is permanent and doesn't change.\n  - The cid is the SHA of the current commit and changes with any\n    change to it or its ancestors.\n- A revset is a set of revisions.\n- In many jj commands revsets can address multiple commits.\n- There is one root commit; chid=zzz sha=0 owner=root.\n- The root commit never has content nor description.\n- There can be multiple independent lineages of commits off root():\n  - to create:\n    - `jj new 'root()'`\n    - `git switch --orphan <name>`\n  - to see these:\n    - `jj log -r 'roots(~root())'`\n    - `git log --all --max-parents=0 --oneline`\n\nThe examples below show these primitives in action.\n\n### A jj repo with some commits\n\nSome examples of revisions/rev:\n   - @, chid=tkpvsrop, cid=ad2ba9b4 is the current commit\n   - @-, chid=wxtmosqz, cid=35ac2422 is the ancestor of the current commit\n   - @--, chid=vktlnyvm, cid=a0b0285e is the ancestor of the ancestor and so on\n\n```\n$ jj log -r 'all()'\n@  tkpvsrop wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 ad2ba9b4\n│  count 3\n○  wxtmosqz wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 35ac2422\n│  count 2\n○  vktlnyvm wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 a0b0285e\n│  count 1\n○  nvwytkrw wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 base 54fd18f7\n│  count 0\n◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000\n```\n\nMove @ to vktlnyvm. (This could also have been done with `jj edit -r @--`.)\n\n```\n$ jj edit -r vkt\nWorking copy  (@) now at: vktlnyvm a0b0285e count 1\nParent commit (@-)      : nvwytkrw 54fd18f7 base | count 0\n```\n\n### Referencing commits with relative revsets\n\n```\n$ jj log -r @\n@  vktlnyvm count 1\n$ jj log -r @-\n○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n$ jj log -r @--\n◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000\n$ jj log -r @+\n○  wxtmosqz count 2\n$ jj log -r @++\n○  tkpvsrop count 3\n$ jj log -r @+++      # empty — nothing that far out\n$ jj log -r @---      # empty\n$ jj log -r @..\n○  tkpvsrop count 3\n○  wxtmosqz count 2\n$ jj log -r @::\n○  tkpvsrop count 3\n○  wxtmosqz count 2\n@  vktlnyvm count 1\n$ jj log -r ..@\n@  vktlnyvm count 1\n○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n$ jj log -r ::@\n@  vktlnyvm count 1\n○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000\n```\n\n#### Interpretation\n\n- `@-` and `@--` resolve to single revisions: parent and\n  grandparent of @. `@+` and `@++` are children. The blank output\n  for `@+++` and `@---` is the empty revset — there is no revision\n  that far away in this chain.\n- `@..` and `@::` are ranges going outward from @ toward\n  descendants:\n  - `@..` is the *open* form: descendants of @, **excluding** @\n    itself (here: count 2 and count 3).\n  - `@::` is the *closed* form: descendants of @, **including** @\n    itself (here: @=count 1, count 2, count 3).\n- `..@` and `::@` are ranges going inward from some implicit start\n  toward ancestors of @:\n  - `..@` includes @ and its ancestors but **excludes** the root\n    commit (here: @=count 1, base=count 0).\n  - `::@` includes the root commit as well.\n\nMnemonic: `..` and `::` both produce ranges; `::` includes the\nimplicit endpoint (root or visible heads), `..` excludes it. The\nnamed operand is always part of the result on the target side; on\nthe source side it depends on which dot-form is used (excluded by\n`..`, included by `::`).\n\n### Referencing commits with absolute revsets\n\n```\n$ jj log -r v          # unambiguous prefix of vktlnyvm\n@  vktlnyvm count 1\n$ jj log -r vktln\n@  vktlnyvm count 1\n$ jj log -r w+         # w matches wxtmosqz, + takes its child\n○  tkpvsrop count 3\n$ jj log -r w--\n○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n$ jj log -r w..\n○  tkpvsrop count 3\n$ jj log -r ..w\n○  wxtmosqz count 2\n@  vktlnyvm count 1\n○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n$ jj log -r w::\n○  tkpvsrop count 3\n○  wxtmosqz count 2\n$ jj log -r ::w\n○  wxtmosqz count 2\n@  vktlnyvm count 1\n○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000\n```\n\n#### Interpretation\n\n- `v` and `vktln` both resolve to chid `vktlnyvm` because they are\n  unambiguous prefixes within this repo — no other chid starts\n  with those letters.\n- `w+` resolves in two stages: `w` matches `wxtmosqz` (count 2) by\n  prefix, then `+` takes its child, giving count 3.\n- `w--` grandparent of w.\n- `w..` descendants of w, excluding w.\n- `..w` ancestors of w, not including root.\n- `::w` ancestors of w, including root.\n- `w::` descendants of w, including w.\n\nPrefix rule: jj rejects ambiguous prefixes. If two chids both\nstart with the same letters, the prefix must be lengthened until\nexactly one chid matches.\n\n## Cross-repo Linking with Git Trailers\n\nEach commit cross-references its counterpart in the other repo\nvia an `ochid:` git trailer. That is a cross-repo convention\nrather than a jj mechanic — for the full definition (trailer\nsyntax, per-commit mechanics, `.vc-config.toml`) see\n[Cross-repo linking (ochid trailers)](../AGENTS.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)\nin AGENTS.md.\n","numLines":351,"startLine":1,"totalLines":351}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"dd03594a-5f3a-45a5-986b-b3de7d7297f5","session_id":"67d3518a-81ae-481f-bcf7-5f7eb013123c","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/vc-x1-work-repo-template","sessionId":"67d3518a-81ae-481f-bcf7-5f7eb013123c","version":"2.1.217","gitBranch":"HEAD"}

A\n+revision is identified by `@`, a chid, or a cid, and revsets are\n+built from those identifiers plus the operators `-`, `+`, `..`,\n+and `::`. There is a complete language available — see\n+`jj help -k revsets`.\n+\n+Summary:\n+\n+- A revision (rev) is used for addressing/referring to commits.\n+- jj supports a change_id (chid) and commit_id (cid).\n+  - The chid is permanent and doesn't change.\n+  - The cid is the SHA of the current commit and changes with any\n+    change to it or its ancestors.\n+- A revset is a set of revisions.\n+- In many jj commands revsets can address multiple commits.\n+- There is one root commit; chid=zzz sha=0 owner=root.\n+- The root commit never has content nor description.\n+- There can be multiple independent lineages of commits off root():\n+  - to create:\n+    - `jj new 'root()'`\n+    - `git switch --orphan <name>`\n+  - to see these:\n+    - `jj log -r 'roots(~root())'`\n+    - `git log --all --max-parents=0 --oneline`\n+\n+The examples below show these primitives in action.\n+\n+### A jj repo with some commits\n+\n+Some examples of revisions/rev:\n+   - @, chid=tkpvsrop, cid=ad2ba9b4 is the current commit\n+   - @-, chid=wxtmosqz, cid=35ac2422 is the ancestor of the current commit\n+   - @--, chid=vktlnyvm, cid=a0b0285e is the ancestor of the ancestor and so on\n+\n+```\n+$ jj log -r 'all()'\n+@  tkpvsrop wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 ad2ba9b4\n+│  count 3\n+○  wxtmosqz wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 35ac2422\n+│  count 2\n+○  vktlnyvm wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 a0b0285e\n+│  count 1\n+○  nvwytkrw wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 base 54fd18f7\n+│  count 0\n+◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000\n+```\n+\n+Move @ to vktlnyvm. A\n+revision is identified by `@`, a chid, or a cid, and revsets are\n+built from those identifiers plus the operators `-`, `+`, `..`,\n+and `::`. There is a complete language available — see\n+`jj help -k revsets`.\n+\n+Summary:\n+\n+- A revision (rev) is used for addressing/referring to commits.\n+- jj supports a change_id (chid) and commit_id (cid).\n+  - The chid is permanent and doesn't change.\n+  - The cid is the SHA of the current commit and changes with any\n+    change to it or its ancestors.\n+- A revset is a set of revisions.\n+- In many jj commands revsets can address multiple commits.\n+- There is one root commit; chid=zzz sha=0 owner=root.\n+- The root commit never has content nor description.\n+- There can be multiple independent lineages of commits off root():\n+  - to create:\n+    - `jj new 'root()'`\n+    - `git switch --orphan <name>`\n+  - to see these:\n+    - `jj log -r 'roots(~root())'`\n+    - `git log --all --max-parents=0 --oneline`\n+\n+The examples below show these primitives in action.\n+\n+### A jj repo with some commits\n+\n+Some examples of revisions/rev:\n+   - @, chid=tkpvsrop, cid=ad2ba9b4 is the current commit\n+   - @-, chid=wxtmosqz, cid=35ac2422 is the ancestor of the current commit\n+   - @--, chid=vktlnyvm, cid=a0b0285e is the ancestor of the ancestor and so on\n+\n+```\n+$ jj log -r 'all()'\n+@  tkpvsrop wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 ad2ba9b4\n+│  count 3\n+○  wxtmosqz wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 35ac2422\n+│  count 2\n+○  vktlnyvm wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 a0b0285e\n+│  count 1\n+○  nvwytkrw wink@saville.com 2026-05-01 08:41:05 base 54fd18f7\n+│  count 0\n+◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000\n+```\n+\n+Move @ to vktlnyvm. The\n+named operand is always part of the result on the target side; on\n+the source side it depends on which dot-form is used (excluded by\n+`..`, included by `::`).\n+\n+### Referencing commits with absolute revsets\n+\n+```\n+$ jj log -r v          # unambiguous prefix of vktlnyvm\n+@  vktlnyvm count 1\n+$ jj log -r vktln\n+@  vktlnyvm count 1\n+$ jj log -r w+         # w matches wxtmosqz, + takes its child\n+○  tkpvsrop count 3\n+$ jj log -r w--\n+○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n+$ jj log -r w..\n+○  tkpvsrop count 3\n+$ jj log -r ..w\n+○  wxtmosqz count 2\n+@  vktlnyvm count 1\n+○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n+$ jj log -r w::\n+○  tkpvsrop count 3\n+○  wxtmosqz count 2\n+$ jj log -r ::w\n+○  wxtmosqz count 2\n+@  vktlnyvm count 1\n+○  nvwytkrw base | count 0\n+◆  zzzzzzzz root() 00000000\n+```\n+\n+#### Interpretation\n+\n+- `v` and `vktln` both resolve to chid `vktlnyvm` because they are\n+  unambiguous prefixes within this repo — no other chid starts\n+  with those letters.\n+- `w+` resolves in two stages: `w` matches `wxtmosqz` (count 2) by\n+  prefix, then `+` takes its child, giving count 3.\n+- `w--` grandparent of w.\n+- `w..` descendants of w, excluding w.\n+- `..w` ancestors of w, not including root.\n+- `::w` ancestors of w, including root.\n+- `w::` descendants of w, including w.\n+\n+Prefix rule: jj rejects ambiguous prefixes. Three concerns:\n\n1. **It's a new convention living only in the template's example text.** AGENTS.md's \"Conventional-commit shape\" section defines the ladder-step form as `X.Y.Z-N <title>` plus `(current)`/`(done)` — no ref slot — and cycle-protocol.md was just synced as a \"shared protocol doc set\" from vc-x1. Per your own convention, a `[[N]]` inside a code span is a literal token, not a citation — so either back-tick them (`` `[[1]]` ``) or put the four-line ladder example in a fenced code block. The sentence itself is also tangled (\"This contains an empty reference…, version, followed by the title and marked…\"); something like: *\"each step is a `[[N]]` slot (backfilled with the step's commit ref once pushed), the version, the title, and a `(done|current)` marker\"* reads cleaner.\n\n`vc-x1 validate-todo TODO.md` passes, though with 0 numbered entries it isn't exercising much.\n\n## vc-template-x1.claude-empty\n\nThe structure (licenses + README + jj/git colocated, one pushed \"Initial Commit\" on `main`) is right for its purpose. Plain\n52\t`cargo install` ignores `Cargo.lock` and re-resolves dependencies\n53\tfrom scratch, so it can silently produce a binary built from a\n54\tdifferent (and possibly broken) dependency graph than `cargo build`\n55\t/ `cargo test` ran against. There is no stable cargo config knob\n56\tto make `--locked` the default for `cargo install`, so the\n57\tdiscipline lives in the project's pre-commit checklist and shell\n58\taliases.\n59\t\n60\tThe trade-off is predictable-as-tested (`--locked`) vs picking up\n61\tupstream security/bug fixes via fresh resolves (default). vc-template-x1\n\nThis is the main repo of a dual-repo convention for using\na bot to help in the development of a coding project. The goal\nis that this main repo contains the \"what\", while the partner\nbot repo contains \"why\" and \"how\". The key to the convention\nis each change is cross-referenced to the other. Thus there\nis a coherent story of the development of the project across time.\n\nThe beginnings of that tool is [vc-x1](https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1)\nwhich currently does achieve this goal, but is being used as a\nfirst test bed.\n\n## This is a template — customize freely\n\n`CLAUDE.md` and this `README.md` are just starting points.\nRead both and edit either to match the conventions you want for your\nproject. In particular, decisions like the `cargo install` behavior\n(default re-resolve vs `--locked`) under [Releasing](#releasing) are\nyours to make — pick what fits and update the docs (and the CLAUDE.md\npre-commit checklist) so the choice is recorded for future readers.\n\n## Cloning\n\nThe Bot session repo is setup as a git submodule which\nmakes it easier to clone both repos. The easiest is to\nclone both when doing the initial clone:\n```\ngit clone --recurisve git@github.com:winksaville/vc-template-x1\n```\n\nIf you forget to use --recurisze you need to do two additional\nsteps \"init\" and \"update\":\n```\ngit clone git@github.com:winksaville/vc-template-x1\ngit submodule init\ngit submodule update\n```\n\nAnd these can be combined using 'update --init' if you like\n```\ngit clone git@github.com:winksaville/vc-template-x1\ngit submodule update --init\n```\n\n## Releasing\n\n**`cargo install` lockfile gotcha.**\n\nIf you install your project's binary with `cargo install --path .`,\nthis template recommends also passing `--locked`. Plain\n`cargo install` ignores `Cargo.lock` and re-resolves dependencies\nfrom scratch, so it can silently produce a binary built from a\ndifferent (and possibly broken) dependency graph than `cargo build`\n/ `cargo test` ran against. There is no stable cargo config knob\nto make `--locked` the default for `cargo install`, so the\ndiscipline lives in the project's pre-commit checklist and shell\naliases.\n\nThe trade-off is predictable-as-tested (`--locked`) vs picking up\nupstream security/bug fixes via fresh resolves (default). Either\nis defensible — pick what fits your project, then edit this\nsection and CLAUDE.md's pre-commit step 6 to match.\n\nFull background, repro details, and upstream cargo-issue links:\n[notes/cargo-locked-issue.md](notes/cargo-locked-issue.md).\n\n## jj Tips for Git Users\n\nSee [Steve The `-dev` prefix\n395\t+adds no information the git log doesn't already convey and\n396\t+doubles typing per commit.\n397\t+\n398\t+The final release commit (no suffix) signals completion rather than\n399\t+amending prior commits. This keeps history readable and makes it easy\n400\t+to see which commits were exploratory vs final.\n401\t+\n402\t+For decomposition finer than `X.Y.Z-N` — sub-steps (`X.Y.Z-N.M`)\n403\t+or sub-sub-steps (`X.Y.Z-N.M-K`) — see\n404\t+[Sub-step Workflow](#sub-step-workflow). The cycle close-out\n405\t+choice (squash to one commit vs land each sub-step separately)\n406\t+is made at close-out, not cycle start.\n407\t+\n408\t+See also [`notes/substep-protocol.md`](notes/substep-protocol.md)\n409\t+for the full protocol — when to use, per-substep contract\n410\t+(`cargo test --bins` is non-negotiable), navigation, the validated\n411\t+close-out squash recipe, and recovery. Revset primitives the\n412\t+protocol relies on (`@`, `@-`, `..`, `::`, prefix matching) live in\n413\t+[`notes/jj-revsets.md`](notes/jj-revsets.md).\n414\t+\n415\t+### Headings and entries that record a commit\n416\t+\n417\t+A `chores-NN.md` `##` section header that records a specific\n418\t+commit, the matching `todo.md > ## Done` entry, and any `[N]`\n419\t+reference to that section all use **exactly that commit's\n420\t+title** — `<type>: <desc> (<version>)`, the same string the\n421\t+commit gets (see [Commit Message Style](#commit-message-style)).\n422\t+E.g. the chores header `## refactor: port push to Context\n423\t+(0.48.0-6)` and the Done line `- refactor: port push to Context\n424\t+(0.48.0-6) [[3]]`. For a multi-step cycle the `## Done` entry\n425\t+uses the close-out commit's title.\n426\t+\n427\t+This does **not** apply to organizational headings (`## Todo`,\n428\t+`## In Progress`, `# References`) or to design `###` subsections\n429\t+inside a chores section — those are named for whatever fits.\n430\t+Among the commit-recording ones, exact match is the strong\n431\t+default (nothing absolute): a near-miss just makes it harder to\n432\t+line a record up with its commit.\n433\t+\n434\t+A commit-recording header is provisional while the work is in\n435\t+progress; the *last* edit before `vc-x1 push` syncs it — and the\n436\t+`## Done` entry / `[N]` anchor for that commit — to the final\n437\t+commit title. See [Markdown anchor links](#markdown-anchor-links)\n438\t+for the slug algorithm; the pre-commit checklist catches a\n439\t+dangling `#anchor`, and a future `vc-x1 validate-repo` should too\n440\t+(and should verify the recorded title matches the commit).\n441\t+\n442\t+Existing sections and `## Done` entries (most of chores-01..09;\n443\t+the pre-`0.48.1` `## Done` lines) predate this and keep their\n444\t+free-form text; the convention applies going forward — `0.48.2`\n445\t+converts the `0.48.1` section + its Done entry as the worked\n446\t+example.\n447\t+\n448\t+### Chores section content — no edit list; git is the record\n449\t+\n450\t+A chores section is: a `Commits:` line (first line under the\n451\t+header — see below), a short intro paragraph (what changed and\n452\t+*why*, a notch above file-list granularity), and any `###`\n453\t+design subsections. It does **not** carry a per-file edit list —\n454\t+that lives in the commit message body, which is the source of\n455\t+truth for \"what changed mechanically\" (immutable, `git\n456\t+show`-able, naturally scoped to the commit). The chores section\n457\t+is the source of truth for the design thinking; the two\n458\t+cross-link, neither restates the other.\n459\t+\n460\t+When the intro starts wanting to explain a mechanism,\n461\t+hypothesis, or wrinkle, don't inflate it — promote that to its\n462\t+own `###` subsection inside the same `chores-NN.md`. If the\n463\t+wrinkle is a live design concern (something that *should*\n464\t+change, not just be recorded), also add a `notes/todo.md` item\n465\t+with a `[N]` ref pointing at that subsection (todo→chores is the\n466\t+normal ref direction).\n467\t+\n468\t+**Why:** a chores edit list and the commit body were specified\n469\t+to be the same content in two places — and detail written twice\n470\t+drifts. Git owns the mechanical record; chores owns the\n471\t+narrative; `Commits:` links them.\n472\t+\n473\t+### Chores commit references\n474\t+\n475\t+The first line under a chores section header is a `Commits:`\n476\t+line citing the git commit(s) that section records:\n477\t+\n478\t+```\n479\t+## refactor: port push to Context (0.48.0-6)\n480\t+\n481\t+Commits: [[3]]\n482\t+\n483\t+<intro paragraph...>\n484\t+```\n485\t+\n486\t+`Commits:` uses the file-local `[N]` reference machinery (see\n487\t+[notes/README.md](notes/README.md#reference-numbering)),\n488\t+**double-bracketed** so the brackets render — `Commits: [[3]]`,\n489\t+or `Commits: [[3]],[[5]]` for several. (`[[3]]` shows as a\n490\t+literal `[`, the `[3]` link, then a literal `]`; the inner\n491\t+`[3]` resolves against its `[3]:` definition — CommonMark /\n492\t+GitHub / VS Code all do this.) The `# References` definition\n493\t+puts the **commit URL** as the destination, with the **full\n494\t+40-hex SHA** in the title slot:\n495\t+\n496\t+```\n497\t+[3]: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/commit/<12-hex> \"<40-hex>\"\n498\t+```\n499\t+\n500\t+- The 12-hex short SHA in the URL keeps it short; GitHub /\n501\t+  GitLab resolve a unique prefix to the canonical commit page\n502\t+  (GitLab's path has a `/-/` before `commit/`).\n503\t+- The full SHA in the title is host-agnostic and unambiguous —\n504\t+  it survives a repo host change, `git show <40-hex>` works in\n505\t+  any clone, and external tooling scraping the notes (a\n506\t+  database, say) gets the canonical identifier.\n507\t+\n508\t+**Timing.** The commit doesn't exist when its chores section is\n509\t+written, so the `Commits:` line is **backfilled when the next\n510\t+change to that repo is started** — the cycle-start step grabs\n511\t+the just-pushed commit's URL + SHA and fills it in. The single\n512\t+newest section is briefly `Commits:`-less; that's fine — the\n513\t+commit itself is the record, and `git log --grep \"(X.Y.Z)\"`\n514\t+finds it.\n515\t+\n516\t+### Pre-commit checklist\n517\t+\n518\t+At cycle *start* (before the version bump): backfill the\n519\t+previous chores section's `Commits:` ref with the just-pushed\n520\t+commit's URL + full SHA — see\n521\t+[Chores commit references](#chores-commit-references).\n522\t+\n523\t+Before proposing a commit, run all of the following and fix any issues:\n524\t+\n525\t+1. `cargo fmt`\n526\t+2. `cargo clippy`\n527\t+3. `cargo test`\n528\t+4. `cargo install --path . --locked` (if applicable) — `--locked`\n529\t+   is required: without it, `cargo install` ignores `Cargo.lock`\n530\t+   and re-resolves from scratch, which can pick incompatible\n531\t+   versions even when `cargo build` / `cargo test` succeed.\n532\t+5. Retest after install\n533\t+6. Update `notes/todo.md` — for multi-step cycles, flip the\n534\t+   just-completed step's marker from `(current)` to `(done)`\n535\t+   **before** running `vc-x1 push`. The commit being pushed\n536\t+   should reflect the new state. (The next step's `(current)`\n537\t+   marker is set later, at the *start* of that step — see the\n538\t+   Versioning multi-step section.)\n539\t+7. Update `notes/todo.md` — at cycle close-out (final commit),\n540\t+   move the entry from `## In Progress` to `## Done`.\n541\t+8. Update `notes/chores-*.md` — add a section (header =\n542\t+   provisional commit title; intro paragraph + any `###` design\n543\t+   subsections; **no** per-file edit list — that's the commit\n544\t+   body).\n545\t+9. Sync the chores section header to the **final** commit title\n546\t+   and update every markdown anchor back-reference to it.\n547\t+10. Update `notes/README.md` — if functionality changed (new\n548\t+    flags, new subcommands, changed behavior).\n549\t+\n550\t+## Sub-step Workflow\n551\t+\n552\t+Larger work decomposes into named depths. The version-suffix\n553\t+scheme nests:\n554\t+\n555\t+- **Single step** — one change, one commit + push + finalize.\n556\t+- **Multi-step** — planned series within a target bump:\n557\t+  `0.5.0 → 0.6.0-0`, `0.6.0-0 → 0.6.0-1`, …, `0.6.0-N → 0.6.0`.\n558\t+- **Sub-step** — finer granularity within a step:\n559\t+  `0.6.0-3.1 → 0.6.0-3.2 → … → 0.6.0-3` (close-out).\n560\t+- **Sub-sub-step** — finer still:\n561\t+  `0.6.0-3.4-0 → 0.6.0-3.4-1 → … → 0.6.0-3.4` (close-out).\n562\t+\n563\t+The conventions below apply at **whichever leaf depth the\n564\t+current cycle planned to** — sub-step, sub-sub-step, etc.\n565\t+\"Sub-step\" reads as shorthand for that leaf level throughout\n566\t+this section.\n567\t+\n568\t+### Version suffix in titles and Cargo.toml\n569\t+\n570\t+Sub-step commits carry the leaf-level version in commit titles\n571\t+**and** `Cargo.toml`. So `vc-x1 -V` shows the active sub-step\n572\t+at build time. Bump Cargo.toml at the start of each sub-step\n573\t+(extends the existing `X.Y.Z-N` step-start bump rule down a\n574\t+level).\n575\t+\n576\t+Cargo accepts arbitrary numeric segments in semver pre-release\n577\t+identifiers; lexical comparison gives the expected ordering\n578\t+(`0.6.0-3.4-1 < 0.6.0-3.4-2 < 0.6.0-3.4`).\n579\t+\n580\t+### todo.md status flips\n581\t+\n582\t+Markers in `notes/todo.md > ## In Progress` flip on a defined\n583\t+cadence:\n584\t+\n585\t+- **Start of (M):** mark (M) `(current)` as the first edit.\n586\t+- **End of (M):** flip (M) `(current)` → `(done)` **before**\n587\t+  the cargo cycle and commit. The commit captures the\n588\t+  completed state.\n589\t+- **Start of (M+1):** mark (M+1) `(current)` as that\n590\t+  sub-step's first edit.\n591\t+\n592\t+Each sub-step's commit carries the \"this sub-step is done\"\n593\t+record; the next sub-step's commit carries \"next sub-step\n594\t+starts.\"\n595\t+\n596\t+### Pre-commit cargo cycle (per sub-step)\n597\t+\n598\t+Run before every sub-step commit (not just at cycle close-out):\n599\t+\n600\t+1. `cargo fmt`\n601\t+2. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`\n602\t+3. `cargo test`\n603\t+4. `cargo install --path . --locked`\n604\t+5. (re-test if anything substantive)\n605\t+\n606\t+Keeps every intermediate commit buildable so bisection works\n607\t+across the cycle's stack.\n608\t+\n609\t+### Commit-first review model\n610\t+\n611\t+Per sub-step:\n612\t+\n613\t+1. Make the sub-step changes.\n614\t+2. Run the cargo cycle.\n615\t+3. **Commit immediately** (both repos with ochid trailers, no\n616\t+   separate approval gate at sub-step granularity).\n617\t+4. Summarize the commit briefly in chat.\n618\t+5. User reviews the committed revision in their editor (full\n619\t+   file context, not chat-pasted diffs).\n620\t+6. User iterates if needed; bot squashes follow-ups into the\n621\t+   sub-step commit via `jj squash --into @-` (and\n622\t+   `jj describe @-` — plus the chores section header and its\n623\t+   anchor back-refs — if the title needs to change).\n624\t+7. User signals \"go to (M+1)\" to advance.\n625\t+\n626\t+This **replaces** the per-sub-step review pause that the\n627\t+top-level `### Review before proposing the commit block` and\n628\t+`### Per-file review checkpoints` rules would otherwise\n629\t+impose. Local jj commits are mutable until close-out, so\n630\t+committing freely is safe.\n631\t+\n632\t+The two-gate ceremony (review + message approval) is preserved\n633\t+for the **cycle-level push** at close-out — that crosses the\n634\t+local→remote boundary and warrants explicit approval.\n635\t+\n636\t+### Ochid trailers on sub-step commits\n637\t+\n638\t+Sub-step commits include ochid trailers paired across the two\n639\t+repos (same shape as top-level cycle commits):\n640\t+\n641\t+- App body: `ochid: /.claude/<.claude-chid>`\n642\t+- `.claude` body: `ochid: /<app-chid>`\n643\t+\n644\t+Use `vc-x1 chid -R .,.claude -L` to capture both pre-commit\n645\t+change IDs (first line app, second `.claude`).\n646\t+\n647\t+### `.claude` cadence\n648\t+\n649\t+`.claude` commits **per sub-step alongside the app repo**.\n650\t+Each sub-step's `.claude` commit captures the session state at\n651\t+that moment.\n652\t+\n653\t+Alternative considered (`.claude` accumulates across the cycle\n654\t+and commits once at close-out) was rejected — keeping the\n655\t+per-sub-step pairing preserves flexibility (any sub-step can\n656\t+be promoted to its own push without restructuring).\n657\t+\n658\t+**`.claude` is a linear journal — all session work lives on\n659\t+`main`.** The repo has no need for parallel feature-branch\n660\t+bookmarks to mirror app-side branches. When the app sits on\n661\t+e.g. `init-clone-refactor`, `.claude` still commits to `main`.\n662\t+Cross-references between sides are carried by the `ochid:`\n663\t+trailer + commit timestamps; that's enough to associate\n664\t+session activity with whichever app-side branch the cycle was\n665\t+on.\n666\t+\n667\t+**Do not create or maintain `.claude` bookmarks that mirror\n668\t+app-side branches.** This was tried once during 0.41.1-6.7 on\n669\t+the impression that an app-side fork needed a `.claude`\n670\t+partner; the partner bookmark went unused for the cycle and\n671\t+the work landed on `.claude main` regardless. Keeping such\n672\t+bookmarks risks the bot misreading them as \"this branch needs\n673\t+to advance\" and steering session pushes to the wrong remote\n674\t+ref.\n675\t+\n676\t+### Cycle close-out — squash or keep separate?\n677\t+\n678\t+Two valid shapes for landing the sub-step stack on `main`:\n679\t+\n680\t+- **Squash to one cycle commit** — single entry on `main`;\n681\t+  sub-step granularity preserved only in the commit body's\n682\t+  edit list. Right when the work is one logical change with\n683\t+  intermediate validation points. **Cost:** the per-sub-step\n684\t+  chores sections collapse into one, whose header becomes the\n685\t+  single close-out commit title, and every anchor back-ref to a\n686\t+  now-gone per-sub-step section gets re-pointed — real work,\n687\t+  done as part of the squash.\n688\t+- **Keep separate (N + 1 commits)** when the decomposition is\n689\t+  itself informative (different conceptual stages, design\n690\t+  progression worth showing in `git log`). Used on\n691\t+  `0.41.1-6.7` (8 sub-sub-step commits + 1 close-out commit).\n692\t+  Each section keeps its own header / `Commits:` ref — no\n693\t+  consolidation churn.\n694\t+\n695\t+Pick at close-out, not at cycle start. No firm default — weigh\n696\t+the squash's chores-consolidation cost against a cleaner\n697\t+`git log`; that cost biases toward keeping separate unless the\n698\t+decomposition genuinely isn't informative.\n699\t+\n700\t+### Reviewing committed sub-steps\n701\t+\n702\t+The commit-first model assumes the reviewer can read the diff\n703\t+of an already-committed revision. Don't `jj edit -r @-` back\n704\t+into a past commit to view it — that marks the commit mutable,\n705\t+shifts the WC pointer, forces a `jj new -r <head>` recovery.\n706\t+Use one of:\n707\t+\n708\t+**Terminal (always works):**\n709\t+\n710\t+```\n711\t+jj diff -r @-                  # diff of previous commit\n712\t+jj diff --from <X> --to <Y>    # diff between two arbitrary revs\n713\t+jj show -r <X>                 # description + diff for one rev\n714\t+jj log -r @-..@                # what's between two points\n715\t+```\n716\t+\n717\t+Pipe through `delta` / `diff-so-fancy | less -R` for color and\n718\t+side-by-side.\n719\t+\n720\t+**External diff tool** — configure jj to launch your editor:\n721\t+\n722\t+```\n723\t+# ~/.config/jj/config.toml\n724\t+[ui]\n725\t+diff-editor = [\"zed\", \"--diff\", \"$left\", \"$right\"]\n726\t+```\n727\t+\n728\t+Then `jj diff -r @-` opens the configured tool. Works for\n729\t+arbitrary `--from`/`--to` ranges.\n730\t+\n731\t+**VS Code** — Source Control panel → Commit Graph →\n732\t+right-click commit A → \"Copy Commit ID\" → right-click commit\n733\t+B → \"Compare with…\" → paste / pick A. Two-commit diff opens\n734\t+with the changed-files list. GitLens extension adds richer\n735\t+\"Open Comparison\" actions; `Git: Compare with…` in the\n736\t+Command Palette is a fallback.\n737\t+\n738\t ## Code Conventions\n739\t \n740\t ### Doc comments on every file, function, and method\n741\t@@ -311,10 +622,21 @@\n742\t inside function bodies remain discouraged unless they capture a\n743\t non-obvious WHY.\n744\t \n745\t-For longer doc comments, follow\n746\t-[Writing style: prefer sub-bullets](#writing-style-prefer-sub-bullets)\n747\t-— short intro then a bullet list, with the `verbatim_doc_comment`\n748\t-caveat for clap-derive args.\n749\t+**Shape:** short intro (1–3 sentences, shorter is better), then\n750\t+a `-` bullet list for any structured details. A\n`[N]` *inside a code span* (`` `[72]` ``) is different — that's\na quoted identifier: literal text naming a ref-key (often from\nanother file's namespace), data, not a citation; it needs no\ndefinition here. To point at a section of another file from\nprose, use an inline link with an anchor —\n`[that section](../chores-07.md#…)` — not a bare number.\n\nA `chores-NN.md` `# References` entry is usually a\n`/notes/<file>.md#anchor` (or `/ARCHITECTURE.md`) path, but may\nalso be a **commit reference** —\n`[N]: <commit-url-with-12-hex-SHA> \"<full-40-hex-SHA>\"`, cited by\na section's `Commits:` line. See\n[Chores commit references](#chores-commit-references) for the\nwhy and the exact shape.\n\nA file's `# References` can be **re-packed** to a contiguous\n`[1]..[N]` in first-citation-appearance order — walk the file's\nprose in document order (`todo.md`: `## Todo` then `## Done`;\n`chores-NN.md`: top to bottom) and number refs as their first\n`[[N]]` citation appears. This is a file-local rewrite — only\nthat file's `[[N]]` citations and `[N]:` definitions move; every\ntarget and sibling file is untouched. A `[[N]]` inside a `` ` ``\ncode span is a literal token, not a citation, and is left alone.\nDo it opportunistically (when the namespace has drifted enough to\nannoy), not on a schedule: `todo.md` fragments fastest (entries\nland and get pruned every cycle) and is the usual candidate;\n`chores-NN.md` / `done.md` are append-mostly and only need it\nafter an unusual event (e.g. a bulk retrofit that allocated slots\nout of document order).\n\n### Markdown anchor links\n\nGitHub anchor algorithm: lowercase, strip non-alphanumeric\ncharacters in place, map remaining spaces to hyphens 1-for-1. Do\n**not** collapse adjacent whitespace — so `a + b` → `a--b` (spaces\non both sides of `+`), but `a: b` → `a-b` (only trailing space on\n`:`). General markdown reference:\n[markdownguide.org](https://www.markdownguide.org). GitHub\npublishes no official spec for auto-generated anchors; the\nde-facto reference implementation is\n[github-slugger](https://github.com/Flet/github-slugger).\n\n### Todo format\n\n`todo.md` is organized into `## In Progress`, `## Todo`\n(strict priority rank, #1 highest; long-tail backlog in\n[todo-backlog.md](notes/todo-backlog.md)), `## Ideas`,\n`## Bugs` (pointer to [bugs.md](notes/bugs.md)), and\n`## Done` sections. Each item is a short description with\nreference links to more detail.\n\n`## Todo` and `## Bugs` entries carry explicit `1.` `2.` …\nnumbers in the source. For `## Todo` the number is its\n**priority rank** (#1 highest, descending); for `## Bugs`\nit's just an index. They're for grepping and at-a-glance\n\"let's do #1\" — **not stable IDs**: reorder (to\nreprioritize), insert, or delete freely, then\n`vc-x1 fix-todo --no-dry-run` renumbers and normalizes\ncontinuation-line indent, so any given number is positional.\n**To refer to a Todo durably, name it by its title — a\nplain, greppable text mention.** Not its number (positional,\nrenumbered) and not a markdown link: a numbered list item has\nno anchor to link to.\n\nNumbering helps a human orient in a long list but makes links\ndifficult and fragile — especially an external reference\npointing in, which can't be auto-fixed when the list\nrenumbers. A robust fix (a number-free anchor, or a\nnumber-tolerant dereference that matches the title slug and\nwildcards the numeric prefix — a GitHub slug like `5-foo` is\nencoded, not opaque, so the title is recoverable) is a\n`validate-numbering` design question, out of scope here.\n\n`vc-x1 fix-todo` alone only previews; `vc-x1 validate-todo`\nis the read-only check. The `## Done` section keeps `-`\nbullets — items aren't referenced by number once completed.\n\nExample shape:\n\n```\n# Todo\n- Add new feature X [details](features.md#feature-x)\n- Fix bug Y [[1]]\n\n# Done\n- Fixed issue Z [[2]],[[3]]\n\n[1]: bugs.md#bug-y\n[2]: issues.md#issue-z\n[3]: fixes.md#fix-z\n```\n\n### Retiring Done entries\n\n`todo.md`'s `## Done` section is a rolling buffer of recently\nshipped work, not a permanent log. Move entries into `done.md`\nat two natural beats:\n\n- **Closing a ladder** — when the final `X.Y.Z` (no suffix)\n  commit ships, decide which prior entries are no longer\n  needed for nearby context and migrate them.\n- **Opening a new ladder** — at `X.Y.Z-0`, do the same sweep\n  before bumping the version.\n\nMigration mechanics:\n\n- Move the bullet itself from `todo.md > ## Done` to\n  `done.md` (preserving the original ref number).\n- Copy any references the moved entries cite into\n  `done.md`'s `# References` section (those refs are\n  file-local, so coexisting with `todo.md`'s namespace is\n  fine).\n- Prune any references in `todo.md > # References` no longer\n  cited by anything in `## In Progress` / `## Todo` /\n  `## Done`. This frees the numbers for future reuse.\n\n## Chores conventions\n\n### Headings and entries that record a commit\n\nA `chores-NN.md` `##` section header that records a specific\ncommit, the matching `todo.md > ## Done` entry, and any `[N]`\nreference to that section all use **exactly that commit's\ntitle** — `<type>: <desc> (<version>)`, the same string the\ncommit gets (see [Per-commit flow](notes/cycle-protocol.md#per-commit-flow)).\nE.g. the chores header `## refactor: port push to Context\n(0.48.0-6)` and the Done line `- refactor: port push to Context\n(0.48.0-6) [[3]]`. The `## Done` entry uses the close-out\ncommit's title.\n\nThis does **not** apply to organizational headings (`## Todo`,\n`## In Progress`, `# References`) or to design `###` subsections\ninside a chores section — those are named for whatever fits.\nAmong the commit-recording ones, exact match is the strong\ndefault (nothing absolute): a near-miss just makes it harder to\nline a record up with its commit.\n\nA commit-recording header is provisional while the work is in\nprogress; the *last* edit before `vc-x1 push` syncs it — and the\n`## Done` entry / `[N]` anchor for that commit — to the final\ncommit title. See [Markdown anchor links](#markdown-anchor-links)\nfor the slug algorithm; the pre-commit checklist catches a\ndangling `#anchor`, and a future `vc-x1 validate-repo` should too\n(and should verify the recorded title matches the commit).\n\nExisting sections and `## Done` entries (most of chores-01..09;\nthe pre-`0.48.1` `## Done` lines) predate this and keep their\nfree-form text; the convention applies going forward — `0.48.2`\nconverts the `0.48.1` section + its Done entry as the worked\nexample.\n\n### Chores section content — no edit list; git is the record\n\nA chores section is: a `Commits:` line (first line under the\nheader — see below), then [Prose form](#prose-form) (intro +\nbullets) for what landed and why, and any `###` design\nsubsections. Bullets here are **conceptual** — design points,\nstructural notes — never a per-file edit list. That lives in the\ncommit message body, which is the source of truth for \"what\nchanged mechanically\" (immutable, `git show`-able, naturally\nscoped to the commit). The chores section is the source of truth\nfor the design thinking; the two cross-link, neither restates the\nother.\n\nWhen the intro starts wanting to explain a mechanism,\nhypothesis, or wrinkle, don't inflate it — promote that to its\nown `###` subsection inside the same `chores-NN.md`. If the\nwrinkle is a live design concern (something that *should*\nchange, not just be recorded), also add a `notes/todo.md` item\nwith a `[N]` ref pointing at that subsection (todo→chores is the\nnormal ref direction).\n\n**Why:** a chores edit list and the commit body were specified\nto be the same content in two places — and detail written twice\ndrifts. Git owns the mechanical record; chores owns the\nnarrative; `Commits:` links them.\n\n### Chores commit references\n\nThe first line under a chores section header is a `Commits:`\nline citing the git commit(s) that section records:\n\n```\n## refactor: port push to Context (0.48.0-6)\n\nCommits: [[3]]\n\n<intro paragraph...>\n```\n\n`Commits:` uses the file-local `[N]` reference machinery (see\n[Reference numbering](#reference-numbering)),\n**double-bracketed** so the brackets render — `Commits: [[3]]`,\nor `Commits: [[3]],[[5]]` for several. (`[[3]]` shows as a\nliteral `[`, the `[3]` link, then a literal `]`; the inner\n`[3]` resolves against its `[3]:` definition — CommonMark /\nGitHub / VS Code all do this.) The `# References` definition\nputs the **commit URL** as the destination, with the **full\n40-hex SHA** in the title slot:\n\n```\n[3]: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/commit/<12-hex> \"<40-hex>\"\n```\n\n- The 12-hex short SHA in the URL keeps it short; GitHub /\n  GitLab resolve a unique prefix to the canonical commit page\n  (GitLab's path has a `/-/` before `commit/`).\n- The full SHA in the title is host-agnostic and unambiguous —\n  it survives a repo host change, `git show <40-hex>` works in\n  any clone, and external tooling scraping the notes (a\n  database, say) gets the canonical identifier.\n\n**Timing.** The commit doesn't exist when its chores section is\nwritten, so the `Commits:` line is **backfilled when the next\nchange to that repo is started** — the cycle-start step grabs\nthe just-pushed commit's URL + SHA and fills it in. The single\nnewest section is briefly `Commits:`-less; that's fine — the\ncommit itself is the record, and `git log --grep \"(X.Y.Z)\"`\nfinds it.\n\n## Cycle Protocol\n\nEvery change runs as a **cycle**: Preparation (`X.Y.Z-0`) →\nWork commits (`X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, …) → Close-out (bare\n`X.Y.Z`). Each commit runs through a per-commit flow whose\ncargo cycle is `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets\n-- -D warnings`, `cargo test`, `cargo install --path .\n--locked` (skip-able for purely-docs commits; mandatory at\nclose-out). The full protocol — numbering, per-commit\nflow, reviewing changes, close-out, pushing, ochid\ntrailers, sub-cycles — lives in\n[`notes/cycle-protocol.md`](notes/cycle-protocol.md). Read\nit before any commit work.\n\n\n## Code Conventions\n\n### Doc comments on every file, function, and method\n\nEvery `.rs` file must begin with a `//!` module docstring. Every\nfunction and method must have a `///` doc comment. Keep them brief —\none sentence of purpose is often enough; the discipline is that the\ncomment exists, not that it be long. Doc comments follow the\n[Prose form](#prose-form) shape (intro + bullets).\n\nThis is a deliberate override of the generic \"write no comments\"\ndefault that applies to inline `//` comments. Doc comments on the\nmodule / item surface are expected; inline explanatory comments\ninside function bodies remain discouraged unless they capture a\nnon-obvious WHY.\n\n**Clap-derive args:** doc comments on `#[arg(...)]` fields drive\n`--help` output. Clap reflows by default and collapses bullets\ninto running prose. Add `#[arg(verbatim_doc_comment, ...)]` on\nany field whose doc comment uses bullets so each `- …` lands on\nits own line in the rendered help.\n\n### `// OK: …` comments on `unwrap*` calls (Rust)\n\nNon-test code that calls `.unwrap()`, `.unwrap_or(…)`,\n`.unwrap_or_default()`, or `.unwrap_or_else(…)` must have a trailing\n`// OK: …` comment that justifies why the call is acceptable.\n\n- `// OK: <specific reason>` — document the real precondition,\n  invariant, or domain reason. Preferred whenever the reason isn't\n  self-evident.\n- `// OK: obvious` — the default is self-evident from context (e.g.\n  `desc.lines().next().unwrap_or(\"\")` — empty desc → empty title).\n\nBare `// OK` is not used (reads like a truncated comment).\nAbbreviations (e.g. `SE`) are not used because they require a decoder\nring for readers seeing the code out of context.\n\nFor provably-unreachable `.unwrap()` calls, also prefix with\n`#[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]` so the site stays silent if we enable\nthe project-wide `clippy::unwrap_used` lint later.\n\n```rust\nlet max = stderr_level.unwrap_or(LevelFilter::Info); // OK: default verbosity when -v/-vv absent\nlet first_line = desc.lines().next().unwrap_or(\"\");  // OK: obvious\n\nmatch matches.len() {\n    1 => {\n        #[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]\n        // OK: `1 =>` arm guarantees matches.len() == 1\n        Ok(TitleMatch::One(matches.into_iter().next().unwrap()))\n    }\n    // ...\n}\n```\n\nTests (`#[cfg(test)]`) are exempt — panicking on setup failure is the\ncorrect test behavior.\n\n### Ask for clarification on ambiguous input\n\nWhen user input is ambiguous or missing necessary detail, stop and\nask a specific question. Do not proceed on a guess and hope the\nresult lands right — a clarifying question costs a few seconds;\nredoing misaligned work costs much more.\n\n### Recognize when stuck\n\nIf a simple task has eaten 5+ minutes of thinking or back-and-forth\nwithout progress, stop.
