There is no\n153\t`jj mv`: to move/rename a tracked file, just `mv` it on disk and\n154\tjj detects the rename by content.\n155\t\n156\t- `jj st -R .` / `jj st -R .claude` — show working copy status\n157\t- `jj log -R .` / `jj log -R .claude` — show commit log\n158\t- `jj commit -m \"title\" -m \"body\" -R <repo>` — finalize working copy into a commit\n159\t- `jj describe -m \"title\" -m \"body\" -R <repo>` — set description without committing\n160\t- `jj git push --bookmark <name> -R <repo>` — push a bookmark (no\n161\t  `--allow-new` flag; jj pushes new bookmarks without special flags)\n162\t- In jj, the working copy (@) is always a mutable commit being edited.\n163\t  `jj commit` finalizes it and creates a new empty working copy on top.\n164\t- The `.claude` repo always has uncommitted changes during an active\n165\t  session because session data updates continuously.\n166\t- `jj rebase` uses `--onto`/`-o` to name the destination(s).\n167\t\n168\t## Cross-repo linking (ochid trailers)\n169\t\n170\tThe cross-reference between the app repo and the `.claude` bot\n171\trepo is what makes the dual-repo work: every commit points at its\n172\tcounterpart in the other repo, so the \"what\" (code) and the\n173\t\"why / how\" (session) stay linked across time. That pointer is the\n174\t**ochid** (Other Change ID) git trailer.\n175\t\n176\tA **chid** is jj's change ID — a permanent identifier that\n177\tsurvives rebases and `describe`s (unlike the commit ID / git SHA,\n178\twhich changes on rewrite). An **ochid** trailer carries the\n179\tcounterpart commit's chid as a workspace-root-relative path:\n180\t\n181\t- Paths start with `/` — the workspace root, i.e. the app repo\n182\t  (vc-template-x1). `/.claude` is the bot session sub-repo.\n183\t- `ochid: /<chid>` references a change in the **app repo**.\n184\t- `ochid: /.claude/<chid>` references a change in the **`.claude`\n185\t  repo**.\n186\t\n187\tTrailers are blank-line-separated `key: value` lines at the end of\n188\tthe commit body, using the chid's **12-character** prefix:\n189\t\n190\t```\n191\tochid: /.claude/xvzvruqowktp   # points to a .claude repo change\n192\tochid: /wtpmottvxqzl           # points to an app repo change\n193\t```\n194\t\n195\tHow many, and which direction:\n196\t\n197\t- **Code-side commits** each carry one\n198\t  `ochid: /.claude/<.claude-chid>` — the `.claude` change ID.\n199\t- **The `.claude` commit** carries one `ochid: /<code-chid>` per\n200\t  code commit in that push. More than one occurs on a Merge\n201\t  non-ff close-out (one ochid per Work commit in the cycle).\n202\t\n203\tUse `vc-x1 chid -s code,bot -L` to capture the change IDs (first\n204\tline app, second `.claude`).\n205\t\n206\t### Resolvability\n207\t\n208\tA change ID travels with its commit: a **pushed** commit resolves\n209\tto the same chid in every clone — cloning the `.claude` repo gave\n210\tthe published `main` tip the same chid as an existing clone. We\n211\tthink jj carries the change ID in the git commit object, so it\n212\tsurvives `jj git clone` / fetch.\n213\t\n214\tThe local-only case is the **working-copy `@`**: jj mints a fresh\n215\trandom chid for `@` in each clone, so an unpushed `@` is never a\n216\tstable ochid target. This is why a `.claude` ochid names `@-`\n217\t(the last committed change), not `@`.\n218\t\n219\t### .vc-config.toml\n220\t\n221\tEach repo contains a `.vc-config.toml` that identifies its\n222\tlocation within the workspace, so tools resolve these paths\n223\twithout repeating the workspace path in every trailer:\n224\t\n225\t```toml\n226\t# In vc-template-x1 (workspace root):\n227\t[workspace]\n228\tpath = \"/\"\n229\t\n230\t# In .claude (sub-repo):\n231\t[workspace]\n232\tpath = \"/.claude\"\n233\t```\n234\t\n235\t## Prose form\n236\t\n237\tLong-lived prose on this project follows one basic shape: a short intro\n238\tthat explains the *why* or the high-level *what*, then a `-` bullet\n239\tlist for the details. Wrap lines at ≤72 cols (bullet continuations\n240\tindent two spaces). Avoid wall-of-prose paragraphs — they hide the\n241\tstructure that bullets make scannable.\n242\t\n243\tSurfaces that use this shape:\n244\t\n245\t- Module / function / struct / field doc comments in `.rs` files —\n246\t  see [Doc comments](#doc-comments-on-every-file-function-and-method).\n247\t- Commit message bodies (both app-repo and session-repo). The\n248\t  ≤50-col title is the commit-specific add-on; see\n249\t  [Per-commit flow](notes/cycle-protocol.md#per-commit-flow).\n250\t- Chore descriptions in `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` — see\n251\t  [Chores section content](#chores-section-content--no-edit-list-git-is-the-record).\n252\t- Todo and Done entries in `notes/todo.md` when an entry needs more\n253\t  than one line of detail. Pure one-liners are still fine.\n254\t\n255\tBullet *content* differs by surface:\n256\t\n257\t- **Commit bodies** — bullets are file-by-file: one bullet per file\n258\t  changed, file plus a one-line gist (e.g.\n259\t  `README.md: new Overview intro`). Source of truth for the\n260\t  mechanical edit list.\n261\t- **Chores / todo / done** — bullets are conceptual (design points,\n262\t  structural notes, the \"what landed and why\" at a notch above\n263\t  file-list granularity). Never a copy of the commit's edit list —\n264\t  see [Chores section content](#chores-section-content--no-edit-list-git-is-the-record).\n265\t- **Doc comments** — bullets are whatever structure fits (fields,\n266\t  cases, invariants).\n267\t\n268\t### Problem + plan shape\n269\t\n270\t`## In Progress` cycle blocks, chores section intros, and `## Todo`\n271\tentries use a sharper form of the same shape:\n272\t\n273\t- **Problem statement** (the why) — one or two sentences;\n274\t  don't pad with intent, don't restate the plan.\n275\t- **Plan bullets** (the what/when) — formality differs by\n276\t  surface:\n277\t  - In Progress / chores: a committed ladder, one step per\n278\t    commit — see\n279\t    [Conventional-commit shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--chores--commit)\n280\t    for the per-step title + `(current)` / `(done)` form.\n281\t  - Todo entries: rough informal bullets, no numbering;\n282\t    formalized only when the entry is picked up into a\n283\t    cycle.\n284\t\n285\t### Semicolons inside bullets\n286\t\n287\tA bullet that joins multiple clauses with semicolons (`A; B; C`)\n288\tis a list hiding inside running prose — break the clauses into\n289\tsub-bullets so the structure shows. Semicolons in running prose\n290\t(intro paragraphs, sentence-joins) are fine. Not absolute: very\n291\tshort clauses or tight pairs can stay joined inside a bullet when\n292\tbreaking would be more noise than signal.\n293\t\n294\t### Conventional-commit shape (ladder / chores / commit)\n295\t\n296\tA ladder step, its chores section, and its commit description\n297\tshare a *title* shape — a\n298\t[Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/)\n299\ttitle over [Prose form](#prose-form) detail. They differ in the\n300\ttitle's prefix / marker (below) and in bullet *content* — commit\n301\tbodies are file-by-file, ladder / chores conceptual (see \"Bullet\n302\t*content* differs by surface\" above). The shared template:\n303\t\n304\t```\n305\t<optional - X.Y.Z[-N]> <title>   # <title> is the commit's `<type>: <desc>`\n306\t<optional prose intro>\n307\t  - <optional item>\n308\t    <optional prose intro>\n309\t      - <optional sub-item>\n310\t      ...\n311\t```\n312\t\n313\tThe three surfaces apply it as:\n314\t\n315\t- **Ladder step** (`notes/todo.md` `## In Progress`): the title is\n316\t  prefixed with the version — `X.Y.Z-N <title>` — and\n317\t  carries a `(current)` / `(done)` marker. The bare three-element\n318\t  `X.Y.Z` (no `-N`) is the close-out step. Detail is bulleted,\n319\t  never `;`-joined inline.\n320\t- **Chores section** (`notes/chores/chores-NN.md`): no version\n321\t  prefix — the `##` header *is* the bare title, with a\n322\t  `Commits: [[ref]]` line first under it (empty until backfilled —\n323\t  see [Chores commit references](#chores-commit-references)).\n324\t- **Commit description**: no version prefix — the title is the\n325\t  ≤50-col first line; the body is the prose (file-by-file for the\n326\t  app repo, per [Per-commit flow](notes/cycle-protocol.md#per-commit-flow)).\n327\t\n328\tThe title is **identical** across all three for a given step, so a\n329\tstep's ladder entry, its chores `##` header, and its commit title\n330\tline up verbatim — pick the commit title first and reuse it.\n331\t\n332\tThat identity is **per step**, not per cycle: each step in a\n333\tcycle gets its own distinct descriptive title — never one shared\n334\tcycle title uniquified by a step marker. The cycle's chores\n335\tsection header carries the anticipated *close-out* title. To keep\n336\ta cycle's commits collectable with one `git log --grep`, give the\n337\tstep titles a common greppable stem (e.g. `config loader`).\n338\t\n339\t## Notes file conventions\n340\t\n341\tConventions the bot follows when writing notes files\n342\t(`notes/todo.md`, `notes/todo-backlog.md`, `notes/bugs.md`,\n343\t`notes/chores/chores-NN.md`, `notes/done.md`). One source\n344\tof truth lives here; [`notes/README.md`](notes/README.md)\n345\tpoints back.\n346\t\n347\t### Notes references\n348\t\n349\tReference *citations* are double-bracketed so the brackets render\n350\t— `[[N]]`, or `[[2]],[[3]]` for several (comma-separated, not\n351\t`[2,3]` or `[[2]][[3]]`). The `[N]:` definitions in a file's\n352\t`# References` section and inline `[text](url)` / `[text](#anchor)`\n353\tlinks stay single-bracketed.\n354\t\n355\t### Reference numbering\n356\t\n357\tEvery note file (`todo.md`, `todo-backlog.md`, `bugs.md`,\n358\t`chores-NN.md`, `done.md`) keeps a file-local `# References`\n359\tsection at the bottom. Reference numbers are scoped to that\n360\tfile — `[1]` in `chores-07.md` and `[1]` in `chores-01.md`\n361\tare independent slots that may point at completely different\n362\tURLs. New chores files start their numbering at `[1]`.\n363\t\n364\tTreat `[N]` like a **footnote**: the number is a local slot, only\n365\tmeaningful within its file's `# References`. So a `[N]` *citation*\n366\t(bare `[N]`, or doubled `[[N]]`) never reuses another file's number; to cite a target a sibling\n367\tfile references, pick your own next-local slot and define it\n368\t(the same target may carry a different number in each file). A\n369\t`[N]` *inside a code span* (`` `[72]` ``) is different — that's\n370\ta quoted identifier: literal text naming a ref-key (often from\n371\tanother file's namespace), data, not a citation; it needs no\n372\tdefinition here. To point at a section of another file from\n373\tprose, use an inline link with an anchor —\n374\t`[that section](../chores-07.md#…)` — not a bare number.\n375\t\n376\tA `chores-NN.md` `# References` entry is usually a\n377\t`/notes/<file>.md#anchor` (or `/ARCHITECTURE.md`) path, but may\n378\talso be a **commit reference** —\n379\t`[N]: <commit-url-with-12-hex-SHA> \"<full-40-hex-SHA>\"`, cited by\n380\ta section's `Commits:` line. See\n381\t[Chores commit references](#chores-commit-references) for the\n382\twhy and the exact shape.\n383\t\n384\tA file's `# References` can be **re-packed** to a contiguous\n385\t`[1]..[N]` in first-citation-appearance order — walk the file's\n386\tprose in document order (`todo.md`: `## Todo` then `## Done`;\n387\t`chores-NN.md`: top to bottom) and number refs as their first\n388\t`[[N]]` citation appears. This is a file-local rewrite — only\n389\tthat file's `[[N]]` citations and `[N]:` definitions move; every\n390\ttarget and sibling file is untouched. A `[[N]]` inside a `` ` ``\n391\tcode span is a literal token, not a citation, and is left alone.\n392\tDo it opportunistically (when the namespace has drifted enough to\n393\tannoy), not on a schedule: `todo.md` fragments fastest (entries\n394\tland and get pruned every cycle) and is the usual candidate;\n395\t`chores-NN.md` / `done.md` are append-mostly and only need it\n396\tafter an unusual event (e.g. a bulk retrofit that allocated slots\n397\tout of document order).\n398\t\n399\t### Markdown anchor links\n400\t\n401\tGitHub anchor algorithm: lowercase, strip non-alphanumeric\n402\tcharacters in place, map remaining spaces to hyphens 1-for-1. Do\n403\t**not** collapse adjacent whitespace — so `a + b` → `a--b` (spaces\n404\ton both sides of `+`), but `a: b` → `a-b` (only trailing space on\n405\t`:`). General markdown reference:\n406\t[markdownguide.org](https://www.markdownguide.org). GitHub\n407\tpublishes no official spec for auto-generated anchors; the\n408\tde-facto reference implementation is\n409\t[github-slugger](https://github.com/Flet/github-slugger).\n410\t\n411\t### Todo format\n412\t\n413\t`todo.md` is organized into `## In Progress`, `## Todo`\n414\t(strict priority rank, #1 highest; long-tail backlog in\n415\t[todo-backlog.md](notes/todo-backlog.md)), `## Ideas`,\n416\t`## Bugs` (pointer to [bugs.md](notes/bugs.md)), and\n417\t`## Done` sections. Each item is a short description with\n418\treference links to more detail.\n419\t\n420\t`## Todo` and `## Bugs` entries carry explicit `1.` `2.` …\n421\tnumbers in the source. For `## Todo` the number is its\n422\t**priority rank** (#1 highest, descending); for `## Bugs`\n423\tit's just an index. They're for grepping and at-a-glance\n424\t\"let's do #1\" — **not stable IDs**: reorder (to\n425\treprioritize), insert, or delete freely, then\n426\t`vc-x1 fix-todo --no-dry-run` renumbers and normalizes\n427\tcontinuation-line indent, so any given number is positional.\n428\t**To refer to a Todo durably, name it by its title — a\n429\tplain, greppable text mention.** Not its number (positional,\n430\trenumbered) and not a markdown link: a numbered list item has\n431\tno anchor to link to.\n432\t\n433\tNumbering helps a human orient in a long list but makes links\n434\tdifficult and fragile — especially an external reference\n435\tpointing in, which can't be auto-fixed when the list\n436\trenumbers. A robust fix (a number-free anchor, or a\n437\tnumber-tolerant dereference that matches the title slug and\n438\twildcards the numeric prefix — a GitHub slug like `5-foo` is\n439\tencoded, not opaque, so the title is recoverable) is a\n440\t`validate-numbering` design question, out of scope here.\n441\t\n442\t`vc-x1 fix-todo` alone only previews; `vc-x1 validate-todo`\n443\tis the read-only check. The `## Done` section keeps `-`\n444\tbullets — items aren't referenced by number once completed.\n445\t\n446\tExample shape:\n447\t\n448\t```\n449\t# Todo\n450\t1. Add new feature X [details](features.md#feature-x)\n451\t2. Fix bug Y [[1]]\n452\t\n453\t# Done\n454\t- Fixed issue Z [[2]],[[3]]\n455\t\n456\t[1]: bugs.md#bug-y\n457\t[2]: issues.md#issue-z\n458\t[3]: fixes.md#fix-z\n459\t```\n460\t\n461\t### Retiring Done entries\n462\t\n463\t`todo.md`'s `## Done` section is a rolling buffer of recently\n464\tshipped work, not a permanent log. Move entries into `done.md`\n465\tat two natural beats:\n466\t\n467\t- **Closing a ladder** — when the final `X.Y.Z` (no suffix)\n468\t  commit ships, decide which prior entries are no longer\n469\t  needed for nearby context and migrate them.\n470\t- **Opening a new ladder** — at `X.Y.Z-0`, do the same sweep\n471\t  before bumping the version-of-record.\n472\t\n473\tMigration mechanics:\n474\t\n475\t- Move the bullet itself from `todo.md > ## Done` to\n476\t  `done.md` (preserving the original ref number).\n477\t- Copy any references the moved entries cite into\n478\t  `done.md`'s `# References` section (those refs are\n479\t  file-local, so coexisting with `todo.md`'s namespace is\n480\t  fine).\n481\t- Prune any references in `todo.md > # References` no longer\n482\t  cited by anything in `## In Progress` / `## Todo` /\n483\t  `## Done`. This frees the numbers for future reuse.\n484\t\n485\t## Chores conventions\n486\t\n487\t### Headings and entries that record a commit\n488\t\n489\tA commit's title is reused verbatim across its records — see\n490\t[Conventional-commit shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--chores--commit)\n491\tfor the rule. Beyond the chores `##` header, that same string is\n492\tused for the matching `todo.md > ## Done` entry and any `[N]`\n493\treference to that section. Titles carry **no `(<version>)`\n494\tsuffix** — see\n495\t[Commit description](notes/cycle-protocol.md#commit-description)\n496\tfor why.\n497\tE.g. the chores header `## refactor: extract config loader`\n498\tand the Done line `- refactor: extract config loader [[3]]`.\n499\tThe `## Done` entry uses the close-out commit's title.\n500\t\n501\tThis does **not** apply to organizational headings (`## Todo`,\n502\t`## In Progress`, `# References`) or to design `###` subsections\n503\tinside a chores section — those are named for whatever fits.\n504\tAmong the commit-recording ones, exact match is the strong\n505\tdefault (nothing absolute): a near-miss just makes it harder to\n506\tline a record up with its commit.\n507\t\n508\tA commit-recording header is provisional while the work is in\n509\tprogress; the *last* edit before `vc-x1 push` syncs it — and the\n510\t`## Done` entry / `[N]` anchor for that commit — to the final\n511\tcommit title. See [Markdown anchor links](#markdown-anchor-links)\n512\tfor the slug algorithm; the pre-commit checklist catches a\n513\tdangling `#anchor`, and a future `vc-x1 validate-repo` should too\n514\t(and should verify the recorded title matches the commit).\n515\t\n516\tAny pre-existing sections and `## Done` entries that predate\n517\tthis convention keep their free-form text; the convention\n518\tapplies going forward.\n519\t\n520\t### Chores section content — no edit list; git is the record\n521\t\n522\tA chores section is: a `Commits:` line (first line under the\n523\theader — see below), then [Prose form](#prose-form) (intro +\n524\tbullets) for what landed and why, and any `###` design\n525\tsubsections. Bullets here are **conceptual** — design points,\n526\tstructural notes — never a per-file edit list. That lives in the\n527\tcommit message body, which is the source of truth for \"what\n528\tchanged mechanically\" (immutable, `git show`-able, naturally\n529\tscoped to the commit). The chores section is the source of truth\n530\tfor the design thinking; the two cross-link, neither restates the\n531\tother.\n532\t\n533\tWhen the intro starts wanting to explain a mechanism,\n534\thypothesis, or wrinkle, don't inflate it — promote that to its\n535\town `###` subsection inside the same `chores-NN.md`. If the\n536\twrinkle is a live design concern (something that *should*\n537\tchange, not just be recorded), also add a `notes/todo.md` item\n538\twith a `[N]` ref pointing at that subsection (todo→chores is the\n539\tnormal ref direction).\n540\t\n541\t**Why:** a chores edit list and the commit body were specified\n542\tto be the same content in two places — and detail written twice\n543\tdrifts. Git owns the mechanical record; chores owns the\n544\tnarrative; `Commits:` links them.\n545\t\n546\t### Chores commit references\n547\t\n548\tThe first line under a chores section header is a `Commits:`\n549\tline citing the git commit(s) that section records:\n550\t\n551\t```\n552\t## refactor: extract config loader\n553\t\n554\tCommits: [[3]]\n555\t\n556\t<intro paragraph...>\n557\t```\n558\t\n559\t`Commits:` uses the file-local `[N]` reference machinery (see\n560\t[Reference numbering](#reference-numbering)),\n561\t**double-bracketed** so the brackets render — `Commits: [[3]]`,\n562\tor `Commits: [[3]],[[5]]` for several. (`[[3]]` shows as a\n563\tliteral `[`, the `[3]` link, then a literal `]`; the inner\n564\t`[3]` resolves against its `[3]:` definition — CommonMark /\n565\tGitHub / VS Code all do this.) The `# References` definition\n566\tputs the **commit URL** as the destination, with the **full\n567\t40-hex SHA** in the title slot:\n568\t\n569\t```\n570\t[3]: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/commit/<12-hex> \"<40-hex>\"\n571\t```\n572\t\n573\t- The 12-hex short SHA in the URL keeps it short; GitHub /\n574\t  GitLab resolve a unique prefix to the canonical commit page\n575\t  (GitLab's path has a `/-/` before `commit/`).\n576\t- The full SHA in the title is host-agnostic and unambiguous —\n577\t  it survives a repo host change, `git show <40-hex>` works in\n578\t  any clone, and external tooling scraping the notes (a\n579\t  database, say) gets the canonical identifier.\n580\t\n581\t**Timing.** A commit's SHA isn't stable until it lands on a\n582\t**permanent branch** (`main`, or a long-lived release/patch\n583\tbranch) — a rebase or squash rewrites it on the way. A commit\n584\tcan't record its own SHA, so the fill lands one push later:\n585\tevery section opens with an **empty `Commits:`**, and each push\n586\tbackfills the `Commits:` of the commits the previous push made\n587\tpermanent. On a topic branch a section waits until the branch\n588\tlands. The commit itself is the record, and\n589\t`git log --grep \"<title>\"` finds it. See cycle-protocol\n590\t[Commits backfill](notes/cycle-protocol.md#commits-backfill).\n591\t\n592\t## Cycle Protocol\n593\t\n594\tEvery change runs as a **cycle**: Preparation (`X.Y.Z-0`) →\n595\tWork commits (`X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, …) → Close-out (bare\n596\t`X.Y.Z`). Each commit runs through a per-commit flow whose\n597\tvalidation step is medium-specific — the Rust example is the\n598\tcargo cycle (fmt → clippy → test → install); skip-able for\n599\tnotes-only commits, mandatory at close-out. The full protocol\n600\t— numbering, per-commit flow, reviewing changes, close-out,\n601\tpushing, ochid trailers, sub-cycles — lives in\n602\t[`notes/cycle-protocol.md`](notes/cycle-protocol.md). Read\n603\tit before any commit work — and before any push, cycle or\n604\tnot: pushes always need per-push user approval (see\n605\t[Pushing policy](notes/cycle-protocol.md#policy)).\n606\t\n607\t**Versioning.** How this repo numbers cycles, where the\n608\tversion-of-record lives, and its bump cadence are\n609\tproject-specific and documented in\n610\t[versioning.md](notes/versioning.md) — the single source of\n611\ttruth that AGENTS.md and cycle-protocol.md refer to\n612\tabstractly.\n613\t\n614\t**Hard stop after push/finalize.** Once a push or `.claude`\n615\tfinalize is invoked (`vc-x1 push` does both), do no further\n616\twork — no verification, no summary, no next-step offers —\n617\tuntil the user speaks. Put all closing words *before* the\n618\tinvoke. The harness rejects an empty turn, so it may force a\n619\tvisible token after the tool returns; if so, emit a bare\n620\tacknowledgment only (e.g. \"landed\") — never a summary or more\n621\twork. Post-push verification happens next turn at the user's\n622\tdirection. See\n623\t[After push or finalize](notes/cycle-protocol.md#after-push-or-finalize-stop-and-wait).\n624\t\n625\t**`vc-x1 push` behaviors to keep in mind.** Two, independent\n626\tof project language:\n627\t\n628\t- **Preflight** runs the cargo cycle (fmt → clippy → test). On\n629\t  a cargo project it works as-is, so `vc-x1 push <bookmark>`\n630\t  runs it before the review gate. If a mechanism, hypothesis, or causal claim\nenters the text, prefix it with \"We think ...\" (a royal \"we\") so a\nreader can tell the measured from the inferred.\n\n**Why:** unmarked speculation reads like evidence, and a future reader\n(or the bot on a later session) can pick it up as a known fact when\nit's not. That pointer is the\n**ochid** (Other Change ID) git trailer.\n\nA **chid** is jj's change ID — a permanent identifier that\nsurvives rebases and `describe`s (unlike the commit ID / git SHA,\nwhich changes on rewrite). An **ochid** trailer carries the\ncounterpart commit's chid as a workspace-root-relative path:\n\n- Paths start with `/` — the workspace root, i.e. the app repo\n  (vc-template-x1). `/.claude` is the bot session sub-repo.\n- `ochid: /<chid>` references a change in the **app repo**.\n- `ochid: /.claude/<chid>` references a change in the **`.claude`\n  repo**.\n\nTrailers are blank-line-separated `key: value` lines at the end of\nthe commit body, using the chid's **12-character** prefix:\n\n```\nochid: /.claude/xvzvruqowktp   # points to a .claude repo change\nochid: /wtpmottvxqzl           # points to an app repo change\n```\n\nHow many, and which direction:\n\n- **Code-side commits** each carry one\n  `ochid: /.claude/<.claude-chid>` — the `.claude` change ID.\n- **The `.claude` commit** carries one `ochid: /<code-chid>` per\n  code commit in that push. More than one occurs on a Merge\n  non-ff close-out (one ochid per Work commit in the cycle).\n\nUse `vc-x1 chid -s code,bot -L` to capture the change IDs (first\nline app, second `.claude`).\n\n### Resolvability\n\nA change ID travels with its commit: a **pushed** commit resolves\nto the same chid in every clone — cloning the `.claude` repo gave\nthe published `main` tip the same chid as an existing clone. We\nthink jj carries the change ID in the git commit object, so it\nsurvives `jj git clone` / fetch.\n\nThe local-only case is the **working-copy `@`**: jj mints a fresh\nrandom chid for `@` in each clone, so an unpushed `@` is never a\nstable ochid target. Not absolute: very\nshort clauses or tight pairs can stay joined inside a bullet when\nbreaking would be more noise than signal.\n\n### Conventional-commit shape (ladder / chores / commit)\n\nA ladder step, its chores section, and its commit description\nshare a *title* shape — a\n[Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/)\ntitle over [Prose form](#prose-form) detail. They differ in the\ntitle's prefix / marker (below) and in bullet *content* — commit\nbodies are file-by-file, ladder / chores conceptual (see \"Bullet\n*content* differs by surface\" above). The shared template:\n\n```\n<optional - X.Y.Z[-N]> <title>   # <title> is the commit's `<type>: <desc>`\n<optional prose intro>\n  - <optional item>\n    <optional prose intro>\n      - <optional sub-item>\n      ...\n```\n\nThe three surfaces apply it as:\n\n- **Ladder step** (`notes/todo.md` `## In Progress`): the title is\n  prefixed with the version — `X.Y.Z-N <title>` — and\n  carries a `(current)` / `(done)` marker. The `[N]:` definitions in a file's\n`# References` section and inline `[text](url)` / `[text](#anchor)`\nlinks stay single-bracketed.\n\n### Reference numbering\n\nEvery note file (`todo.md`, `todo-backlog.md`, `bugs.md`,\n`chores-NN.md`, `done.md`) keeps a file-local `# References`\nsection at the bottom. Reference numbers are scoped to that\nfile — `[1]` in `chores-07.md` and `[1]` in `chores-01.md`\nare independent slots that may point at completely different\nURLs. New chores files start their numbering at `[1]`.\n\nTreat `[N]` like a **footnote**: the number is a local slot, only\nmeaningful within its file's `# References`. So a `[N]` *citation*\n(bare `[N]`, or doubled `[[N]]`) never reuses another file's number; to cite a target a sibling\nfile references, pick your own next-local slot and define it\n(the same target may carry a different number in each file). A\n`[N]` *inside a code span* (`` `[72]` ``) is different — that's\na quoted identifier: literal text naming a ref-key (often from\nanother file's namespace), data, not a citation; it needs no\ndefinition here. To point at a section of another file from\nprose, use an inline link with an anchor —\n`[that section](../chores-07.md#…)` — not a bare number.\n\nA `chores-NN.md` `# References` entry is usually a\n`/notes/<file>.md#anchor` (or `/ARCHITECTURE.md`) path, but may\nalso be a **commit reference** —\n`[N]: <commit-url-with-12-hex-SHA> \"<full-40-hex-SHA>\"`, cited by\na section's `Commits:` line. This is a file-local rewrite — only\nthat file's `[[N]]` citations and `[N]:` definitions move; every\ntarget and sibling file is untouched. A `[[N]]` inside a `` ` ``\ncode span is a literal token, not a citation, and is left alone.\nDo it opportunistically (when the namespace has drifted enough to\nannoy), not on a schedule: `todo.md` fragments fastest (entries\nland and get pruned every cycle) and is the usual candidate;\n`chores-NN.md` / `done.md` are append-mostly and only need it\nafter an unusual event (e.g. a bulk retrofit that allocated slots\nout of document order).\n\n### Markdown anchor links\n\nGitHub anchor algorithm: lowercase, strip non-alphanumeric\ncharacters in place, map remaining spaces to hyphens 1-for-1. Do\n**not** collapse adjacent whitespace — so `a + b` → `a--b` (spaces\non both sides of `+`), but `a: b` → `a-b` (only trailing space on\n`:`). General markdown reference:\n[markdownguide.org](https://www.markdownguide.org). GitHub\npublishes no official spec for auto-generated anchors; the\nde-facto reference implementation is\n[github-slugger](https://github.com/Flet/github-slugger).\n\n### Todo format\n\n`todo.md` is organized into `## In Progress`, `## Todo`\n(strict priority rank, #1 highest; long-tail backlog in\n[todo-backlog.md](notes/todo-backlog.md)), `## Ideas`,\n`## Bugs` (pointer to [bugs.md](notes/bugs.md)), and\n`## Done` sections. Each item is a short description with\nreference links to more detail.\n\n`## Todo` and `## Bugs` entries carry explicit `1.` `2.` …\nnumbers in the source. For `## Todo` the number is its\n**priority rank** (#1 highest, descending); for `## Bugs`\nit's just an index. They're for grepping and at-a-glance\n\"let's do #1\" — **not stable IDs**: reorder (to\nreprioritize), insert, or delete freely, then\n`vc-x1 fix-todo --no-dry-run` renumbers and normalizes\ncontinuation-line indent, so any given number is positional.\n**To refer to a Todo durably, name it by its title — a\nplain, greppable text mention.** Not its number (positional,\nrenumbered) and not a markdown link: a numbered list item has\nno anchor to link to.\n\nNumbering helps a human orient in a long list but makes links\ndifficult and fragile — especially an external reference\npointing in, which can't be auto-fixed when the list\nrenumbers. A robust fix (a number-free anchor, or a\nnumber-tolerant dereference that matches the title slug and\nwildcards the numeric prefix — a GitHub slug like `5-foo` is\nencoded, not opaque, so the title is recoverable) is a\n`validate-numbering` design question, out of scope here.\n\n`vc-x1 fix-todo` alone only previews; `vc-x1 validate-todo`\nis the read-only check. The `## Done` section keeps `-`\nbullets — items aren't referenced by number once completed.\n\nExample shape:\n\n```\n# Todo\n1. Add new feature X [details](features.md#feature-x)\n2. Fix bug Y [[1]]\n\n# Done\n- Fixed issue Z [[2]],[[3]]\n\n[1]: bugs.md#bug-y\n[2]: issues.md#issue-z\n[3]: fixes.md#fix-z\n```\n\n### Retiring Done entries\n\n`todo.md`'s `## Done` section is a rolling buffer of recently\nshipped work, not a permanent log. Move entries into `done.md`\nat two natural beats:\n\n- **Closing a ladder** — when the final `X.Y.Z` (no suffix)\n  commit ships, decide which prior entries are no longer\n  needed for nearby context and migrate them.\n- **Opening a new ladder** — at `X.Y.Z-0`, do the same sweep\n  before bumping the version-of-record.\n\nMigration mechanics:\n\n- Move the bullet itself from `todo.md > ## Done` to\n  `done.md` (preserving the original ref number).\n- Copy any references the moved entries cite into\n  `done.md`'s `# References` section (those refs are\n  file-local, so coexisting with `todo.md`'s namespace is\n  fine).\n- Prune any references in `todo.md > # References` no longer\n  cited by anything in `## In Progress` / `## Todo` /\n  `## Done`. This frees the numbers for future reuse.\n\n## Chores conventions\n\n### Headings and entries that record a commit\n\nA commit's title is reused verbatim across its records — see\n[Conventional-commit shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--chores--commit)\nfor the rule. Beyond the chores `##` header, that same string is\nused for the matching `todo.md > ## Done` entry and any `[N]`\nreference to that section. Titles carry **no `(<version>)`\nsuffix** — see\n[Commit description](notes/cycle-protocol.md#commit-description)\nfor why.\nE.g. the chores header `## refactor: extract config loader`\nand the Done line `- refactor: extract config loader [[3]]`.\nThe `## Done` entry uses the close-out commit's title.\n\nThis does **not** apply to organizational headings (`## Todo`,\n`## In Progress`, `# References`) or to design `###` subsections\ninside a chores section — those are named for whatever fits.\nAmong the commit-recording ones, exact match is the strong\ndefault (nothing absolute): a near-miss just makes it harder to\nline a record up with its commit.\n\nA commit-recording header is provisional while the work is in\nprogress; the *last* edit before `vc-x1 push` syncs it — and the\n`## Done` entry / `[N]` anchor for that commit — to the final\ncommit title. See [Markdown anchor links](#markdown-anchor-links)\nfor the slug algorithm; the pre-commit checklist catches a\ndangling `#anchor`, and a future `vc-x1 validate-repo` should too\n(and should verify the recorded title matches the commit).\n\nAny pre-existing sections and `## Done` entries that predate\nthis convention keep their free-form text; the convention\napplies going forward.\n\n### Chores section content — no edit list; git is the record\n\nA chores section is: a `Commits:` line (first line under the\nheader — see below), then [Prose form](#prose-form) (intro +\nbullets) for what landed and why, and any `###` design\nsubsections. Bullets here are **conceptual** — design points,\nstructural notes — never a per-file edit list. That lives in the\ncommit message body, which is the source of truth for \"what\nchanged mechanically\" (immutable, `git show`-able, naturally\nscoped to the commit). The chores section is the source of truth\nfor the design thinking; the two cross-link, neither restates the\nother.\n\nWhen the intro starts wanting to explain a mechanism,\nhypothesis, or wrinkle, don't inflate it — promote that to its\nown `###` subsection inside the same `chores-NN.md`. If the\nwrinkle is a live design concern (something that *should*\nchange, not just be recorded), also add a `notes/todo.md` item\nwith a `[N]` ref pointing at that subsection (todo→chores is the\nnormal ref direction).\n\n**Why:** a chores edit list and the commit body were specified\nto be the same content in two places — and detail written twice\ndrifts. Git owns the mechanical record; chores owns the\nnarrative; `Commits:` links them.\n\n### Chores commit references\n\nThe first line under a chores section header is a `Commits:`\nline citing the git commit(s) that section records:\n\n```\n## refactor: extract config loader\n\nCommits: [[3]]\n\n<intro paragraph...>\n```\n\n`Commits:` uses the file-local `[N]` reference machinery (see\n[Reference numbering](#reference-numbering)),\n**double-bracketed** so the brackets render — `Commits: [[3]]`,\nor `Commits: [[3]],[[5]]` for several. (`[[3]]` shows as a\nliteral `[`, the `[3]` link, then a literal `]`; the inner\n`[3]` resolves against its `[3]:` definition — CommonMark /\nGitHub / VS Code all do this.) The `# References` definition\nputs the **commit URL** as the destination, with the **full\n40-hex SHA** in the title slot:\n\n```\n[3]: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/commit/<12-hex> \"<40-hex>\"\n```\n\n- The 12-hex short SHA in the URL keeps it short; GitHub /\n  GitLab resolve a unique prefix to the canonical commit page\n  (GitLab's path has a `/-/` before `commit/`).\n- The full SHA in the title is host-agnostic and unambiguous —\n  it survives a repo host change, `git show <40-hex>` works in\n  any clone, and external tooling scraping the notes (a\n  database, say) gets the canonical identifier.\n\n**Timing.** A commit's SHA isn't stable until it lands on a\n**permanent branch** (`main`, or a long-lived release/patch\nbranch) — a rebase or squash rewrites it on the way. A commit\ncan't record its own SHA, so the fill lands one push later:\nevery section opens with an **empty `Commits:`**, and each push\nbackfills the `Commits:` of the commits the previous push made\npermanent. On a topic branch a section waits until the branch\nlands. The commit itself is the record, and\n`git log --grep \"<title>\"` finds it. See cycle-protocol\n[Commits backfill](notes/cycle-protocol.md#commits-backfill).\n\n## Cycle Protocol\n\nEvery change runs as a **cycle**: Preparation (`X.Y.Z-0`) →\nWork commits (`X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, …) → Close-out (bare\n`X.Y.Z`). Each commit runs through a per-commit flow whose\nvalidation step is medium-specific — the Rust example is the\ncargo cycle (fmt → clippy → test → install); skip-able for\nnotes-only commits, mandatory at close-out. The full protocol\n— numbering, per-commit flow, reviewing changes, close-out,\npushing, ochid trailers, sub-cycles — lives in\n[`notes/cycle-protocol.md`](notes/cycle-protocol.md). Read\nit before any commit work — and before any push, cycle or\nnot: pushes always need per-push user approval (see\n[Pushing policy](notes/cycle-protocol.md#policy)).\n\n**Versioning.** How this repo numbers cycles, where the\nversion-of-record lives, and its bump cadence are\nproject-specific and documented in\n[versioning.md](notes/versioning.md) — the single source of\ntruth that AGENTS.md and cycle-protocol.md refer to\nabstractly.\n\n**Hard stop after push/finalize.** Once a push or `.claude`\nfinalize is invoked (`vc-x1 push` does both), do no further\nwork — no verification, no summary, no next-step offers —\nuntil the user speaks. Put all closing words *before* the\ninvoke. The harness rejects an empty turn, so it may force a\nvisible token after the tool returns; if so, emit a bare\nacknowledgment only (e.g. \"landed\") — never a summary or more\nwork. Post-push verification happens next turn at the user's\ndirection. See\n[After push or finalize](notes/cycle-protocol.md#after-push-or-finalize-stop-and-wait).\n\n**`vc-x1 push` behaviors to keep in mind.** Two, independent\nof project language:\n\n- **Preflight** runs the cargo cycle (fmt → clippy → test). On\n  a cargo project it works as-is, so `vc-x1 push <bookmark>`\n  runs it before the review gate. On a project with no cargo\n  cycle — or any time preflight can't run — invoke `vc-x1 push\n  <bookmark> --from message ...` to skip preflight and the\n  interactive review gate, doing the diff review in\n  conversation first.\n- **ochid trailers** are injected by `vc-x1 push` itself —\n  don't hand-write them into the commit body or\n  `--title`/`--body`.\n\n\n## Code Conventions\n\n### Doc comments on every file, function, and method\n\nEvery `.rs` file must begin with a `//!` module docstring. Every\nfunction and method must have a `///` doc comment. Keep them brief —\none sentence of purpose is often enough; the discipline is that the\ncomment exists, not that it be long. Doc comments follow the\n[Prose form](#prose-form) shape (intro + bullets).\n\nThis is a deliberate override of the generic \"write no comments\"\ndefault that applies to inline `//` comments. Doc comments on the\nmodule / item surface are expected; inline explanatory comments\ninside function bodies remain discouraged unless they capture a\nnon-obvious WHY.\n\n**Clap-derive args:** doc comments on `#[arg(...)]` fields drive\n`--help` output. Clap reflows by default and collapses bullets\ninto running prose. Add `#[arg(verbatim_doc_comment, ...)]` on\nany field whose doc comment uses bullets so each `- …` lands on\nits own line in the rendered help.\n\n### `// OK: …` comments on `unwrap*` calls (Rust)\n\nNon-test code that calls `.unwrap()`, `.unwrap_or(…)`,\n`.unwrap_or_default()`, or `.unwrap_or_else(…)` must have a trailing\n`// OK: …` comment that justifies why the call is acceptable.\n\n- `// OK: <specific reason>` — document the real precondition,\n  invariant, or domain reason. Preferred whenever the reason isn't\n  self-evident.\n- `// OK: obvious` — the default is self-evident from context (e.g.\n  `desc.lines().next().unwrap_or(\"\")` — empty desc → empty title).\n\nBare `// OK` is not used (reads like a truncated comment).\nAbbreviations (e.g. `SE`) are not used because they require a decoder\nring for readers seeing the code out of context.\n\nFor provably-unreachable `.unwrap()` calls, also prefix with\n`#[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]` so the site stays silent if we enable\nthe project-wide `clippy::unwrap_used` lint later.\n\n```rust\nlet max = stderr_level.unwrap_or(LevelFilter::Info); // OK: default verbosity when -v/-vv absent\nlet first_line = desc.lines().next().unwrap_or(\"\");  // OK: obvious\n\nmatch matches.len() {\n    1 => {\n        #[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]\n        // OK: `1 =>` arm guarantees matches.len() == 1\n        Ok(TitleMatch::One(matches.into_iter().next().unwrap()))\n    }\n    // ...\n}\n```\n\nTests (`#[cfg(test)]`) are exempt — panicking on setup failure is the\ncorrect test behavior.\n\n### Ask for clarification on ambiguous input\n\nWhen user input is ambiguous or missing necessary detail, stop and\nask a specific question. Do not proceed on a guess and hope the\nresult lands right — a clarifying question costs a few seconds;\nredoing misaligned work costs much more.\n\n### Recognize when stuck\n\nIf a simple task has eaten 5+ minutes of thinking or back-and-forth\nwithout progress, stop. Summarize what's blocking — unclear\nrequirements, unfamiliar API surface, conflicting signals — and ask.\nContinued flailing produces worse outcomes than a direct \"I'm stuck\non X.\"\n","numLines":713,"startLine":1,"totalLines":713}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"24b31ea1-7176-4d13-81c7-b3bfe799e59f","session_id":"04208ddf-0312-452c-982b-f5492fd4fda2","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/vc-template-x1","sessionId":"04208ddf-0312-452c-982b-f5492fd4fda2","version":"2.1.211","gitBranch":"HEAD"}

/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/vc-x1-work-repo-template/.claude/04208ddf-0312-452c-982b-f5492fd4fda2.jsonl:259:{"parentUuid":"dc9ecde2-b29b-4163-a8fc-04b0a50847ad","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"edited_text_file","filename":"/home/wink/data/prgs/rust/vc-x1/notes/cycle-protocol.md","snippet":"1\t# Cycle protocol\n2\t\n3\tThis protocol uses [Prose form](../AGENTS.md#prose-form). It\n4\tcontains instructions on how a commit cycle is accomplished.\n5\t\n6\tThe artifact a cycle produces is whatever the bot generates from\n7\tthe conversation — code, prose, an image, a song, a screenplay.\n8\tThe steps below use a Rust crate as the running example (the\n9\tcargo cycle, `Cargo.toml` versioning); substitute your medium's\n10\tequivalents — this project's manifest is recorded in\n11\t[versioning.md](versioning.md).\n12\t\n13\t## Cycles\n14\t\n15\tA cycle has three phases:\n16\t\n17\t- **[Preparation](#preparation)** (`X.Y.Z-0`) — the cycle's\n18\t  first commit, when it needs setup (a lightweight cycle omits\n19\t  it and starts at `-1` — see\n20\t  [versioning.md](versioning.md#step-numbering)). Sets up the\n21\t  cycle:\n22\t  - Bump the version-of-record to `X.Y.Z-0` (where it lives\n23\t    and the suffix scheme are project-specific — see\n24\t    [versioning.md](versioning.md)).\n25\t  - Pick up a `## Todo` item (typically the top-ranked,\n26\t    #1) into `## In Progress` (bold title + succinct problem\n27\t    statement + plan ladder).\n28\t  - Open the [chores section](#chores-sections).\n29\t- **[Work-N](#work-n)** (`X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, …) — the\n30\t  commits that implement the change. As many as the change\n31\t  needs; each runs through the\n32\t  [per-commit flow](#per-commit-flow).\n33\t- **[Close-out](#close-out)** (bare `X.Y.Z`) — the cycle's\n34\t  last commit. Bookkeeping only:\n35\t  - Move the picked-up item to a one-line entry in\n36\t    `## Done`.\n37\t  - Move the `## In Progress` block into the\n38\t    [chores section](#chores-sections).\n39\t  - Optionally update `notes/README.md` if functionality\n40\t    changed.\n41\t\n42\tA cycle's commits are published to the project remote\n43\teither incrementally or as one batch at close-out; the\n44\tresult must always be published at close-out. See\n45\t[Pushing](#pushing).\n46\t\n47\t**Sub-cycles.** When a Work commit's scope grows enough to\n48\twarrant its own ladder, it subdivides — `X.Y.Z-3.0`\n49\tPreparation, `X.Y.Z-3.1` / `X.Y.Z-3.2` Work, `X.Y.Z-3`\n50\tClose-out. The same three-phase shape applies recursively\n51\tat every depth. See [Numbering](#numbering) for the\n52\tsuffix rule and [Sub-cycle ladders](#sub-cycle-ladders)\n53\tfor the local-ladder mechanics.\n54\t\n55\t## Chores sections\n56\t\n57\tA **chores section** is a `##` section in\n58\t`notes/chores/chores-NN.md` recording landed work. In\n59\tgeneral, every commit that lands on the permanent branch\n60\tshould have a reference to it on a `Commits:` list in a\n61\tchores file.\n62\t\n63\tThe phrase **\"Open\" the chores section** means append a\n64\t`##` header to the current `notes/chores/chores-NN.md`\n65\twith the title it records (e.g. `## refactor: foo bar`),\n66\tfollowed by an **empty `Commits:`** line. The narrative\n67\tbody stays empty until close-out (see [Close-out](#close-out));\n68\tthe `Commits:` line is backfilled later, once the commit is\n69\tpermanent (see [Commits backfill](#commits-backfill) below).\n70\t\n71\tFuller chores conventions (content rules, header sync,\n72\tdesign subsection pattern, `Commits:` formatting) live in\n73\tAGENTS.md [Chores conventions](../AGENTS.md#chores-conventions).\n74\t\n75\t### Commits backfill\n76\t\n77\tA chores section's `Commits:` line cites the commit(s) it\n78\trecords, by SHA — but a SHA isn't stable until the commit\n79\tlands on a **permanent branch** (`main`, or a long-lived\n80\trelease/patch branch that won't be rewritten); a rebase or\n81\tsquash rewrites it on the way. So:\n82\t\n83\t- A chores section is **opened with an empty `Commits:`** line.\n84\t- **Backfill once the commit is on a permanent branch**,\n85\t  where its SHA is final. A commit can't record its own SHA\n86\t  (that would change the hash), so the fill always lands one\n87\t  push later: **each push backfills the `Commits:` of the\n88\t  commits the previous push made permanent.** On a topic\n89\t  branch the sections instead wait until the branch lands —\n90\t  so no SHA is ever written that a later rebase could\n91\t  invalidate.\n92\t\n93\tUse `[[N]]` refs — several as `[[N]],[[M]]` only when one\n94\tsection records multiple commits (a merge non-ff close-out) —\n95\twith the commit URL + 40-hex SHA in the file's `# References`\n96\t(format in AGENTS.md\n97\t[Chores commit references](../AGENTS.md#chores-commit-references)).\n98\tA section's `##` title matches its commit title, so a rare\n99\tdeliberate rewrite of a permanent-branch commit re-syncs via\n100\t`git log --grep \"<title>\"`.\n101\t\n102\tThe per-push cadence is a project choice, not dogma — a\n103\t**per-close-out** model (recording a cycle's SHAs at its\n104\tclose-out) is equally valid. The one invariant: a recorded\n105\tSHA must be permanent.\n106\t\n107\t## Preparation\n108\t\n109\tThe cycle's first commit (`X.Y.Z-0`), when the cycle needs\n110\tsetup (a lightweight cycle omits it — see\n111\t[versioning.md](versioning.md#step-numbering)):\n112\t\n113\t- **Bump the version-of-record** to `X.Y.Z-0`. Where it\n114\t  lives, the suffix scheme, and any derived files (a\n115\t  lockfile, a sourced manifest version) are\n116\t  project-specific — see [versioning.md](versioning.md).\n117\t- **Move a `## Todo` item** (if the cycle has one) into\n118\t  `## In Progress` and the todo item should have:\n119\t  - A **bold title line** — that will be the chores\n120\t    section header, minus the `## ` prefix.\n121\t  - A **succinct problem statement**; add if one is needed\n122\t  - A **plan ladder**.\n123\t- **Open the [chores section](#chores-sections)** —\n124\t  append a `##` header with the title it records — the\n125\t  cycle's anticipated close-out title.\n126\t\n127\t## Work-N\n128\t\n129\tThe cycle's work commits (`X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, …)\n130\timplement the change. As many as needed:\n131\t\n132\t- Each commit runs through the\n133\t  **[per-commit flow](#per-commit-flow)**.\n134\t- **Interim pushes** are optional (backup, progress\n135\t  visibility).\n136\t- Close-out is the only mandatory push (see\n137\t  [Pushing](#pushing)).\n138\t- **Subdivide into a sub-cycle** if a Work commit's\n139\t  scope grows enough (see\n140\t  [Sub-cycle ladders](#sub-cycle-ladders)).\n141\t\n142\t## Close-out\n143\t\n144\tThe cycle's last commit (bare `X.Y.Z`) does bookkeeping\n145\tonly — the commit body describes that bookkeeping, not\n146\twhat happens post-squash:\n147\t\n148\t- **Move the picked-up item** from `## In Progress` to a\n149\t  one-line entry (with a chores `[N]` ref) in `## Done`.\n150\t- **Move the `## In Progress` block into the\n151\t  [chores section](#chores-sections)** (the title-only\n152\t  placeholder opened during Preparation):\n153\t  - Cut the problem statement + plan ladder out of\n154\t    `## In Progress` (drop the bold title line — the\n155\t    chores `##` header already carries that string).\n156\t  - Paste under the chores `##` header.\n157\t  - Sync the chores header to the **final** commit title\n158\t    if the cycle's scope shifted; update every anchor\n159\t    back-reference.\n160\t  - Add an `### As-built ladder` listing the cycle's\n161\t    commits; optional `### Outcome` notes.\n162\t  - Replace `## In Progress` with\n163\t    `_No cycle currently in progress._`.\n164\t- **Update `notes/README.md`** if functionality changed\n165\t  (new flags, new subcommands, changed behavior).\n166\t\n167\tWhether to **squash** the cycle into one commit before the\n168\tpublishing push, or push as-is, is decided at push time —\n169\tsee [Pushing](#pushing).\n170\t\n171\t## Numbering\n172\t\n173\tEach commit's phase is encoded in the version suffix — `-0`\n174\tPreparation, `-1`/`-2`/… Work, bare `X.Y.Z` Close-out,\n175\trecursively for sub-cycles. The full scheme — disambiguation,\n176\tnesting, optional Preparation, the project's version-of-record\n177\tformat, and the per-phase bump — lives in\n178\t[versioning.md](versioning.md#step-numbering), which is the\n179\tsingle source of truth for this repo's versioning.\n180\t\n181\t## Per-commit flow\n182\t\n183\tEvery commit (Preparation, each Work commit, Close-out) goes\n184\tthrough:\n185\t\n186\t1. **Mark this commit `(current)`** as the first edit in\n187\t   `notes/todo.md > ## In Progress`.\n188\t2. **Do the work** (see [Iterative work](#iterative-work)\n189\t   for the loop-and-squash technique).\n190\t3. **Flip this commit `(current)` → `(done)`** in `## In\n\n... It\n4\tcontains instructions on how a commit cycle is accomplished.\n5\t\n6\tThe artifact a cycle produces is whatever the bot generates from\n7\tthe conversation — code, prose, an image, a song, a screenplay.\n8\tThe steps below use a Rust crate as the running example (the\n9\tcargo cycle, `Cargo.toml` versioning); substitute your medium's\n10\tequivalents — this project's manifest is recorded in\n11\t[versioning.md](versioning.md).\n12\t\n13\t## Cycles\n14\t\n15\tA cycle has three phases:\n16\t\n17\t- **[Preparation](#preparation)** (`X.Y.Z-0`) — the cycle's\n18\t  first commit, when it needs setup (a lightweight cycle omits\n19\t  it and starts at `-1` — see\n20\t  [versioning.md](versioning.md#step-numbering)). Sets up the\n21\t  cycle:\n22\t  - Bump the version-of-record to `X.Y.Z-0` (where it lives\n23\t    and the suffix scheme are project-specific — see\n24\t    [versioning.md](versioning.md)).\n25\t  - Pick up a `## Todo` item (typically the top-ranked,\n26\t    #1) into `## In Progress` (bold title + succinct problem\n27\t    statement + plan ladder).\n28\t  - Open the [chores section](#chores-sections).\n29\t- **[Work-N](#work-n)** (`X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, …) — the\n30\t  commits that implement the change. As many as the change\n31\t  needs; each runs through the\n32\t  [per-commit flow](#per-commit-flow).\n33\t- **[Close-out](#close-out)** (bare `X.Y.Z`) — the cycle's\n34\t  last commit. Bookkeeping only:\n35\t  - Move the picked-up item to a one-line entry in\n36\t    `## Done`.\n37\t  - Move the `## In Progress` block into the\n38\t    [chores section](#chores-sections).\n39\t  - Optionally update `notes/README.md` if functionality\n40\t    changed.\n41\t\n42\tA cycle's commits are published to the project remote\n43\teither incrementally or as one batch at close-out; the\n44\tresult must always be published at close-out. See\n45\t[Pushing](#pushing).\n46\t\n47\t**Sub-cycles.** When a Work commit's scope grows enough to\n48\twarrant its own ladder, it subdivides — `X.Y.Z-3.0`\n49\tPreparation, `X.Y.Z-3.1` / `X.Y.Z-3.2` Work, `X.Y.Z-3`\n50\tClose-out. The same three-phase shape applies recursively\n51\tat every depth. See [Numbering](#numbering) for the\n52\tsuffix rule and [Sub-cycle ladders](#sub-cycle-ladders)\n53\tfor the local-ladder mechanics.\n54\t\n55\t## Chores sections\n56\t\n57\tA **chores section** is a `##` section in\n58\t`notes/chores/chores-NN.md` recording landed work. In\n59\tgeneral, every commit that lands on the permanent branch\n60\tshould have a reference to it on a `Commits:` list in a\n61\tchores file.\n62\t\n63\tThe phrase **\"Open\" the chores section** means append a\n64\t`##` header to the current `notes/chores/chores-NN.md`\n65\twith the title it records (e.g. `## refactor: foo bar`),\n66\tfollowed by an **empty `Commits:`** line. The narrative\n67\tbody stays empty until close-out (see [Close-out](#close-out));\n68\tthe `Commits:` line is backfilled later, once the commit is\n69\tpermanent (see [Commits backfill](#commits-backfill) below).\n70\t\n71\tFuller chores conventions (content rules, header sync,\n72\tdesign subsection pattern, `Commits:` formatting) live in\n73\tAGENTS.md [Chores conventions](../AGENTS.md#chores-conventions).\n74\t\n75\t### Commits backfill\n76\t\n77\tA chores section's `Commits:` line cites the commit(s) it\n78\trecords, by SHA — but a SHA isn't stable until the commit\n79\tlands on a **permanent branch** (`main`, or a long-lived\n80\trelease/patch branch that won't be rewritten); a rebase or\n81\tsquash rewrites it on the way. So:\n82\t\n83\t- A chores section is **opened with an empty `Commits:`** line.\n84\t- **Backfill once the commit is on a permanent branch**,\n85\t  where its SHA is final. A commit can't record its own SHA\n86\t  (that would change the hash), so the fill always lands one\n87\t  push later: **each push backfills the `Commits:` of the\n88\t  commits the previous push made permanent.** On a topic\n89\t  branch the sections instead wait until the branch lands —\n90\t  so no SHA is ever written that a later rebase could\n91\t  invalidate.\n92\t\n93\tUse `[[N]]` refs — several as `[[N]],[[M]]` only when one\n94\tsection records multiple commits (a merge non-ff close-out) —\n95\twith the commit URL + 40-hex SHA in the file's `# References`\n96\t(format in AGENTS.md\n97\t[Chores commit references](../AGENTS.md#chores-commit-references)).\n98\tA section's `##` title matches its commit title, so a rare\n99\tdeliberate rewrite of a permanent-branch commit re-syncs via\n100\t`git log --grep \"<title>\"`.\n101\t\n102\tThe per-push cadence is a project choice, not dogma — a\n103\t**per-close-out** model (recording a cycle's SHAs at its\n104\tclose-out) is equally valid. The one invariant: a recorded\n105\tSHA must be permanent.\n106\t\n107\t## Preparation\n108\t\n109\tThe cycle's first commit (`X.Y.Z-0`), when the cycle needs\n110\tsetup (a lightweight cycle omits it — see\n111\t[versioning.md](versioning.md#step-numbering)):\n112\t\n113\t- **Bump the version-of-record** to `X.Y.Z-0`. Where it\n114\t  lives, the suffix scheme, and any derived files (a\n115\t  lockfile, a sourced manifest version) are\n116\t  project-specific — see [versioning.md](versioning.md).\n117\t- **Move a `## Todo` item** (if the cycle has one) into\n118\t  `## In Progress` and the todo item should have:\n119\t  - A **bold title line** — that will be the chores\n120\t    section header, minus the `## ` prefix.\n121\t  - A **succinct problem statement**; add if one is needed\n122\t  - A **plan ladder**.\n123\t- **Open the [chores section](#chores-sections)** —\n124\t  append a `##` header with the title it records — the\n125\t  cycle's anticipated close-out title.\n126\t\n127\t## Work-N\n128\t\n129\tThe cycle's work commits (`X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, …)\n130\timplement the change. As many as needed:\n131\t\n132\t- Each commit runs through the\n133\t  **[per-commit flow](#per-commit-flow)**.\n134\t- **Interim pushes** are optional (backup, progress\n135\t  visibility).\n136\t- Close-out is the only mandatory push (see\n137\t  [Pushing](#pushing)).\n138\t- **Subdivide into a sub-cycle** if a Work commit's\n139\t  scope grows enough (see\n140\t  [Sub-cycle ladders](#sub-cycle-ladders)).\n141\t\n142\t## Close-out\n143\t\n144\tThe cycle's last commit (bare `X.Y.Z`) does bookkeeping\n145\tonly — the commit body describes that bookkeeping, not\n146\twhat happens post-squash:\n147\t\n148\t- **Move the picked-up item** from `## In Progress` to a\n149\t  one-line entry (with a chores `[N]` ref) in `## Done`.\n150\t- **Move the `## In Progress` block into the\n151\t  [chores section](#chores-sections)** (the title-only\n152\t  placeholder opened during Preparation):\n153\t  - Cut the problem statement + plan ladder out of\n154\t    `## In Progress` (drop the bold title line — the\n155\t    chores `##` header already carries that string).\n156\t  - Paste under the chores `##` header.\n157\t  - Sync the chores header to the **final** commit title\n158\t    if the cycle's scope shifted; update every anchor\n159\t    back-reference.\n160\t  - Add an `### As-built ladder` listing the cycle's\n161\t    commits; optional `### Outcome` notes.\n162\t  - Replace `## In Progress` with\n163\t    `_No cycle currently in progress._`.\n164\t- **Update `notes/README.md`** if functionality changed\n165\t  (new flags, new subcommands, changed behavior).\n166\t\n167\tWhether to **squash** the cycle into one commit before the\n168\tpublishing push, or push as-is, is decided at push time —\n169\tsee [Pushing](#pushing).\n170\t\n171\t## Numbering\n172\t\n173\tEach commit's phase is encoded in the version suffix — `-0`\n174\tPreparation, `-1`/`-2`/… Work, bare `X.Y.Z` Close-out,\n175\trecursively for sub-cycles. The full scheme — disambiguation,\n176\tnesting, optional Preparation, the project's version-of-record\n177\tformat, and the per-phase bump — lives in\n178\t[versioning.md](versioning.md#step-numbering), which is the\n179\tsingle source of truth for this repo's versioning.\n180\t\n181\t## Per-commit flow\n182\t\n183\tEvery commit (Preparation, each Work commit, Close-out) goes\n184\tthrough:\n185\t\n186\t1. **Mark this commit `(current)`** as the first edit in\n187\t   `notes/todo.md > ## In Progress`.\n188\t2. **Do the work** (see [Iterative work](#iterative-work)\n189\t   for the loop-and-squash technique).\n190\t3. **Flip this commit `(current)` → `(done)`** in `## In\n\n... /home/wink/data/prgs/rust/vc-x1-work-repo-template/.claude/50b2d274-bea9-4677-b26a-399ee221b9fa.jsonl:41:{"parentUuid":"71906638-91e6-425a-9864-c3611f00b5a2","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"c6086211-a762-4eaa-9332-2e2af505c04d","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01MteNmmQZANvPRXC4W2VV5U","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Cycle protocol\n2\t\n3\tThis protocol uses [Prose form](../AGENTS.md#prose-form). It\n4\tcontains instructions on how a commit cycle is accomplished.\n5\t\n6\tThe artifact a cycle produces is whatever the bot generates from\n7\tthe conversation — code, prose, an image, a song, a screenplay.\n8\tThe steps below use a Rust crate as the running example (the\n9\tcargo cycle, `Cargo.toml` versioning); substitute your medium's\n10\tequivalents — this project's manifest is recorded in\n11\t[versioning.md](versioning.md).\n12\t\n13\t## Cycles\n14\t\n15\tA cycle has three phases:\n16\t\n17\t- **[Preparation](#preparation)** (`X.Y.Z-0`) — the cycle's\n18\t  first commit, when it needs setup (a lightweight cycle omits\n19\t  it and starts at `-1` — see\n20\t  [versioning.md](versioning.md#step-numbering)). Sets up the\n21\t  cycle:\n22\t  - Bump the version-of-record to `X.Y.Z-0` (where it lives\n23\t    and the suffix scheme are project-specific — see\n24\t    [versioning.md](versioning.md)).\n25\t  - Pick up a `## Todo` item (typically the top-ranked,\n26\t    #1) into `## In Progress` (bold title + succinct problem\n27\t    statement + plan ladder).\n28\t  - Open the [chores section](#chores-sections).\n29\t- **[Work-N](#work-n)** (`X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, …) — the\n30\t  commits that implement the change. As many as the change\n31\t  needs; each runs through the\n32\t  [per-commit flow](#per-commit-flow).\n33\t- **[Close-out](#close-out)** (bare `X.Y.Z`) — the cycle's\n34\t  last commit. Bookkeeping only:\n35\t  - Move the picked-up item to a one-line entry in\n36\t    `## Done`.\n37\t  - Move the `## In Progress` block into the\n38\t    [chores section](#chores-sections).\n39\t  - Optionally update `notes/README.md` if functionality\n40\t    changed.\n41\t\n42\tA cycle's commits are published to the project remote\n43\teither incrementally or as one batch at close-out; the\n44\tresult must always be published at close-out. See\n45\t[Pushing](#pushing).\n46\t\n47\t**Sub-cycles.** When a Work commit's scope grows enough to\n48\twarrant its own ladder, it subdivides — `X.Y.Z-3.0`\n49\tPreparation, `X.Y.Z-3.1` / `X.Y.Z-3.2` Work, `X.Y.Z-3`\n50\tClose-out. The same three-phase shape applies recursively\n51\tat every depth. See [Numbering](#numbering) for the\n52\tsuffix rule and [Sub-cycle ladders](#sub-cycle-ladders)\n53\tfor the local-ladder mechanics.\n54\t\n55\t## Chores sections\n56\t\n57\tA **chores section** is a `##` section in\n58\t`notes/chores/chores-NN.md` recording landed work. In\n59\tgeneral, every commit that lands on the permanent branch\n60\tshould have a reference to it on a `Commits:` list in a\n61\tchores file.\n62\t\n63\tThe phrase **\"Open\" the chores section** means append a\n64\t`##` header to the current `notes/chores/chores-NN.md`\n65\twith the title it records (e.g. `## refactor: foo bar`),\n66\tfollowed by an **empty `Commits:`** line. **Each work commit\n67\tthen appends its own As-built rung + narrative note as it\n68\tlands** — the chores record is built up per commit, not held\n69\tback and written all at once at close-out; close-out only\n70\t*finalizes* (title sync, design subsections, retiring the\n71\t`## In Progress` block). The `Commits:` line is backfilled\n72\tlater, once the commit is permanent (see\n73\t[Commits backfill](#commits-backfill) below).\n74\t\n75\tFuller chores conventions (content rules, header sync,\n76\tdesign subsection pattern, `Commits:` formatting) live in\n77\tAGENTS.md [Chores conventions](../AGENTS.md#chores-conventions).\n78\t\n79\t### Commits backfill\n80\t\n81\tA chores section's `Commits:` line cites the commit(s) it\n82\trecords, by SHA — but a SHA isn't stable until the commit\n83\tlands on a **permanent branch** (`main`, or a long-lived\n84\trelease/patch branch that won't be rewritten); a rebase or\n85\tsquash rewrites it on the way. So:\n86\t\n87\t- A chores section is **opened with an empty `Commits:`** line.\n88\t- **Backfill once the commit is on a permanent branch**,\n89\t  where its SHA is final. A commit can't record its own SHA\n90\t  (that would change the hash), so the fill always lands one\n91\t  push later: **each push backfills the `Commits:` of the\n92\t  commits the previous push made permanent.** On a topic\n93\t  branch the sections instead wait until the branch lands —\n94\t  so no SHA is ever written that a later rebase could\n95\t  invalidate.\n96\t\n97\tUse `[[N]]` refs — several as `[[N]],[[M]]` only when one\n98\tsection records multiple commits (a merge non-ff close-out) —\n99\twith the commit URL + 40-hex SHA in the file's `# References`\n100\t(format in AGENTS.md\n101\t[Chores commit references](../AGENTS.md#chores-commit-references)).\n102\tA section's `##` title matches its commit title, so a rare\n103\tdeliberate rewrite of a permanent-branch commit re-syncs via\n104\t`git log --grep \"<title>\"`.\n105\t\n106\tThe per-push cadence is a project choice, not dogma — a\n107\t**per-close-out** model (recording a cycle's SHAs at its\n108\tclose-out) is equally valid. The one invariant: a recorded\n109\tSHA must be permanent.\n110\t\n111\t## Preparation\n112\t\n113\tThe cycle's first commit (`X.Y.Z-0`), when the cycle needs\n114\tsetup (a lightweight cycle omits it — see\n115\t[versioning.md](versioning.md#step-numbering)):\n116\t\n117\t- **Bump the version-of-record** to `X.Y.Z-0`. Where it\n118\t  lives, the suffix scheme, and any derived files (a\n119\t  lockfile, a sourced manifest version) are\n120\t  project-specific — see [versioning.md](versioning.md).\n121\t- **Move a `## Todo` item** (if the cycle has one) into\n122\t  `## In Progress` and the todo item should have:\n123\t  - A **bold title line** — that will be the chores\n124\t    section header, minus the `## ` prefix.\n125\t  - A **succinct problem statement**; add if one is needed\n126\t  - A **plan ladder**.\n127\t- **Open the [chores section](#chores-sections)** —\n128\t  append a `##` header with the title it records — the\n129\t  cycle's anticipated close-out title.\n130\t\n131\t## Work-N\n132\t\n133\tThe cycle's work commits (`X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, …)\n134\timplement the change. As many as needed:\n135\t\n136\t- Each commit runs through the\n137\t  **[per-commit flow](#per-commit-flow)**.\n138\t- **Interim pushes** are optional (backup, progress\n139\t  visibility).\n140\t- Close-out is the only mandatory push (see\n141\t  [Pushing](#pushing)).\n142\t- **Subdivide into a sub-cycle** if a Work commit's\n143\t  scope grows enough (see\n144\t  [Sub-cycle ladders](#sub-cycle-ladders)).\n145\t\n146\t## Close-out\n147\t\n148\tThe cycle's last commit (bare `X.Y.Z`) does bookkeeping\n149\tonly — the commit body describes that bookkeeping, not\n150\twhat happens post-squash:\n151\t\n152\t- **Move the picked-up item** from `## In Progress` to a\n153\t  one-line entry (with a chores `[N]` ref) in `## Done`.\n154\t- **Finalize the chores section** (opened during Preparation\n155\t  and grown per commit — see [Chores sections](#chores-sections)):\n156\t  - The problem statement is already the chores intro (written\n157\t    when the section was opened) and the plan ladder is already\n158\t    the `### As-built ladder` (a rung appended per commit), so\n159\t    close-out only *finalizes*, it does not cut-and-paste.\n160\t  - Sync the chores header to the **final** commit title if the\n161\t    cycle's scope shifted; update every anchor back-reference.\n162\t  - Add any `### design subsections`; optional `### Outcome`\n163\t    notes.\n164\t  - Replace the `## In Progress` cycle block with\n165\t    `_No cycle currently in progress._`.\n166\t- **Update `notes/README.md`** if functionality changed\n167\t  (new flags, new subcommands, changed behavior).\n168\t\n169\tWhether to **squash** the cycle into one commit before the\n170\tpublishing push, or push as-is, is decided at push time —\n171\tsee [Pushing](#pushing).\n172\t\n173\t## Numbering\n174\t\n175\tEach commit's phase is encoded in the version suffix — `-0`\n176\tPreparation, `-1`/`-2`/… Work, bare `X.Y.Z` Close-out,\n177\trecursively for sub-cycles. The full scheme — disambiguation,\n178\tnesting, optional Preparation, the project's version-of-record\n179\tformat, and the per-phase bump — lives in\n180\t[versioning.md](versioning.md#step-numbering), which is the\n181\tsingle source of truth for this repo's versioning.\n182\t\n183\t## Per-commit flow\n184\t\n185\tEvery commit (Preparation, each Work commit, Close-out) goes\n186\tthrough:\n187\t\n188\t1. **Mark this commit `(current)`** as the first edit in\n189\t   `TODO.md > ## In Progress` (`TODO.md` is at the repo\n190\t   root).\n191\t2. **Do the work** (see [Iterative work](#iterative-work)\n192\t   for the loop-and-squash technique).\n193\t3. **Flip this commit `(current)` → `(done)`** in `## In\n194\t   Progress` — before the cargo cycle and the commit.\n195\t4. **Validate the artifact** — a medium-specific step, skip-able\n196\t   for notes-only commits, mandatory at close-out. For the Rust\n197\t   example the cargo cycle is:\n198\t   1. `cargo fmt`\n199\t   2. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`\n200\t   3. `cargo test`\n201\t   4. `cargo install --path . --locked`\n202\t   5. (re-test if anything substantive changed)\n203\t5. **Work review.** Stop *before* writing any description;\n204\t   tell the user \"ready to commit.\" The user reviews the\n205\t   changes and we iterate until complete.\n206\t6. **Write the commit description** — see\n207\t   [Commit description](#commit-description).\n208\t7. **Commit Description review.** Show the title + body\n209\t   and stop. The user reviews the description. Iterate.\n210\t8. **Commit.** `jj commit -m \"title\" -m \"body\" -R .` for\n211\t   the work repo, `-R .claude` for the bot repo (`-R` last\n212\t   keeps the verb visible):\n213\t\n214\t   ```\n215\t   jj commit -m \\\n216\t   \"<type>: <short description>\" \\\n217\t   -m \"<intro paragraph>\n218\t\n219\t   - file1: gist\n220\t   - file2: gist\n221\t\n222\t   ochid: /.claude/<chid>\" \\\n223\t   -R .\n224\t   ```\n225\t\n226\t**Two overrides apply:**\n227\t\n228\t- **Deviation or question** — any time the work deviates\n229\t  from the agreed plan, or a question arises, stop and\n230\t  surface it; don't push through.\n231\t- **ESC-ESC** — the user can interrupt at any point to pull\n232\t  a review or question forward.\n233\t\n234\t## Commit description\n235\t\n236\t[Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/):\n237\t\n238\t```\n239\t<type>: <short description>\n240\t```\n241\t\n242\tTitles carry **no trailing `(<version>)` suffix**. The\n243\tversion-of-record — where it lives and its bump cadence, see\n244\t[versioning.md](versioning.md) — is useful for confirming\n245\tyou're running the version you're testing, not a per-commit\n246\ttitle marker. We think per-commit version-in-title is\n247\tunstable on large projects: many changes are in flight\n248\tsimultaneously, and a\n249\tversion is only stable once merged into the main repo — so\n250\ttitles don't carry one.\n251\t\n252\t### Title\n253\t\n254\t- ≤50 chars total.\n255\t- Common types: `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `test`,\n256\t  `docs`, `chore`.\n257\t- Favor terse phrasings.\n258\t- **Distinct per step** — each of a cycle's commits gets its\n259\t  own descriptive title (no shared cycle title with a step\n260\t  marker). Share a greppable stem across the cycle's titles\n261\t  (e.g. `ring buffer`) so `git log --grep` collects them; the\n262\t  chores section header matches the close-out title. See\n263\t  AGENTS.md\n264\t  [Conventional-commit shape](../AGENTS.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--chores--commit).\n265\t\n266\t### Body\n267\t\n268\t[Prose form](../AGENTS.md#prose-form) (intro + bullets),\n269\twrap ≤72. Bullet content differs per repo:\n270\t\n271\t- **Work-repo body**: file-by-file. One bullet per file\n272\t  changed (file plus a one-line gist). Sub-bullets for\n273\t  files with multiple distinct changes:\n274\t\n275\t  ```\n276\t  - path/to/file1\n277\t    - first distinct change\n278\t    - second distinct change, wrapping to next line\n279\t       with continuation indented 5\n280\t  ```\n281\t\n282\t  The file-by-file list is the source of truth for the\n283\t  cycle's mechanical change record. Chores carries the\n284\t  narrative + design, not a copy of it. Promote any\n285\t  \"why\" beyond one sentence to a chores `###` subsection.\n286\t\n287\t- **Bot-repo (`.claude`) body**: bullets describe\n288\t  in-session activity rather than work-repo changes.\n289\t\n290\t### Trailer\n291\t\n292\t`ochid:` as the last line of the body — see\n293\t[Cross-repo linking (ochid trailers)](../AGENTS.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)\n294\tin AGENTS.md for the convention.\n295\t\n296\tFor breaking changes, use the hyphenated `BREAKING-CHANGE:`\n297\ttrailer key. `BREAKING CHANGE:` (with a space) is the only\n298\tspace-separated key the Conventional Commits spec allows; the\n299\thyphenated form is also valid and avoids the space ambiguity.\n300\t\n301\t## Reviewing changes\n302\t\n303\tWork review looks at the **uncommitted working-copy diff**,\n304\ton the way to commit. The user opens diffs in their\n305\teditor (Zed, VSCode); jj commands are for terminal:\n306\t\n307\t- `jj diff` — working-copy diff (uncommitted)\n308\t- `jj diff -r @-` — diff of the previous commit\n309\t- `jj diff --from <X> --to <Y>` — any two revisions\n310\t- `jj show -r <X>` — description + diff for one rev\n311\t\n312\tDon't `jj edit -r @-` to view a past commit — that marks\n313\tit mutable and shifts `@`; use `jj diff -r @-` or\n314\t`jj show -r @-`.\n315\t\n316\tSee [Sub-cycle ladders](#sub-cycle-ladders) for the\n317\tclose-out squash recipe and recovery; revset primitives\n318\tare in [`jj-tips.md`](jj-tips.md#revsets).\n319\t\n320\t## Pushing\n321\t\n322\t### Policy\n323\t\n324\tPush is **discretionary** during the cycle (backup,\n325\tprogress visibility) and **mandatory at close-out** —\n326\tthe cycle's result must be published.\n327\t\n328\t**Approval is per-push.** Every push — any repo, any kind:\n329\tcycle push, interim backup, recovery/surgery force-push —\n330\thappens only after the user has reviewed the changes to be\n331\tpublished and explicitly approved that specific push.\n332\tApproval of a plan that *includes* a push does not authorize\n333\tthe push itself; stop and ask again at the moment of pushing.\n334\t\n335\t**Default is interactive; an explicit scoped delegation waives\n336\tthe gates.** The gates above — per-push approval, the\n337\tcommit-description review (show title+body and stop), and the\n338\thard stop after push/squash-push — are the *interactive\n339\tdefault*.\n340\tThey yield when the user **explicitly** delegates a complete,\n341\tbounded task and authorizes carrying it through (\"do all of X\n342\tand push each step, don't check in\"). The bot then proceeds\n343\tthrough that task's commits and pushes without stopping, and\n344\tcontinues past each push to the next step. Conditions:\n345\t\n346\t- **Explicit grant** — never inferred from a task merely being\n347\t  well-scoped; the user's words must authorize unattended\n348\t  completion. \"Commit and push\" (or \"then push\") names the\n349\t  destination, not a waiver: it authorizes the push *after*\n350\t  the normal work review and description review, not skipping\n351\t  them. Only wording that explicitly waives the stops (\"don't\n352\t  check in\", \"no need to review\", \"carry it through\n353\t  unattended\") waives them.\n354\t- **Bounded goal** — covers the named task only; does not carry\n355\t  to the next task or a vaguer follow-on.\n356\t- **Destructive ops still pause** — delegation covers the task's\n357\t  ordinary commits and pushes; it does *not* pre-authorize a\n358\t  genuinely irreversible action (force-push over published\n359\t  history, history rewrite, deleting a remote branch). Those can\n360\t  permanently destroy work and aren't a normal cycle step, so the\n361\t  bot flags one before acting. An ordinary delegated cycle never\n362\t  reaches this.\n363\t- **Still transparent** — report each commit/push as it lands\n364\t  (title + outcome) so the user can catch up.\n365\t- **When in doubt, ask** — ambiguous authorization falls back to\n366\t  per-push approval.\n367\t\n368\t### Shape at close-out push\n369\t\n370\tAt close-out the cycle's *work* is done; its *published\n371\tshape* is the remaining choice, made at push time. Surface\n372\tthe options and get user approval before pushing — once on\n373\tthe target, changing shape is a remote rewrite (force-push,\n374\tneeds approval), so choose deliberately.\n375\t\n376\t- **Squash to one commit** — single entry on the target.\n377\t  Right for straightforward changes where the Work-N is\n378\t  focused on one or two files.\n379\t- **Merge non-ff** *(current default)* — `main` gains a\n380\t  merge commit (`X.Y.Z`); cycle commits stay reachable via\n381\t  two parents. `jj log -r ..@ -n <N>` shows the trapezoidal\n382\t  shape. See [Merge non-ff recipe](#merge-non-ff-recipe)\n383\t  for the full setup sequence.\n384\t- **Keep separate** — one commit per cycle entry on\n385\t  `main`. Use when the decomposition itself is\n386\t  informative.
